cs_why_february_2.title: Why the Fire Nation votes on February 2
cs_why_february_2.html:
Fire Nation constituencies elect their members of the National Diet on February 2, a date that marks two events at once: the Battle of Akagawa Ford and the opening of the Diet.

At the Battle of Akagawa Ford, the crown’s forces defeated the last of the rebelling lords. The kingdom then had no armed rival, and the provinces came to be governed by writ rather than by sword.

On the same date, around 300 BG, the Lord opened the Diet for the kingdom and gave the provinces a chamber of their own. The two anniversaries became one holiday. Voting on that day is how a province takes part in it.

Every National Diet election in the archive, from 156 to 190 AG, was held on February 2 except one. The 178 AG snap election, called after the bans and the bombings, was held in November. The Calderan Scire forecast for 194 AG assumes the February date returns.

cs_union_years.title: The Union years in numbers, 156 to 176 AG
cs_union_years.html:
The Union’s seats fell by about three quarters in six elections, from 150 in 156 AG (32% of the Diet) to 40 in 176 AG (9%). Its totals were 156 AG: 150; 160 AG: 128; 164 AG: 104; 168 AG: 82; 172 AG: 62; 176 AG: 40.

Its seats sat in eight core provinces: Shirashihoro, Umi, Yahahama, Takahama, Shinkawa, Narukawa, Kikonokawa and Hatsushima. In 156 AG it also held seats in Kazawa, Kimotari and Kamisukita. By 172 AG it was almost entirely inside the eight.

The People’s Coalition grew from 172 seats to 278 over the same period. The Concord of Nations banned the Equalist Party, The Collective and Salvation Front after the 176 AG vote, and the Union has not stood since.

cs_diet_election_190.title: The People’s Coalition wins Diet as National Alliance enters with 38 seats
cs_diet_election_190.html:
NCP was the largest single party with 168 seats. The National Alliance entered the Diet with 38 seats, and the SDP rebounded to 45.

By camp, The People’s Coalition holds 246 (up 23); The Way holds 216 (up 11); Independents hold 4 (down 34). The People’s Coalition can govern without partners. The Way trails by 30 seats.

Seats by party. The People’s Coalition: PDP 150, SDP 45, Agrarian Labor 14, Civic Progress 12. The Way: NCP 168, National Alliance 38. Independents: Independents 39.

No Union party stood.

Across 33 provinces, The People’s Coalition led in 17, The Way led in 14, Independents led in 2. The People’s Coalition was strongest in Kazawa (24 seats), Entoro (S) (21 seats), Yahahama (19 seats).

The closest provinces were Shinkawa, where The People’s Coalition won 3 seats to 1 for The Way; Kikonokawa, where The Way won 6 seats to 4 for The People’s Coalition; Kiyora, where The Way won 5 seats to 3 for The People’s Coalition.

No province changed hands from 186 AG.

Turnout was 66.0%, with about 104.7 million votes cast, up from 62.0% in 186 AG.

Voters in the Fire Nation’s 33 provinces elect the National Diet, and a majority is 234 seats. Polling day was the traditional February 2 (why February 2).

cs_diet_election_178.title: Snap election after bans and bombings produces hung Diet
cs_diet_election_178.html:
NCP was the largest single party with 214 seats. The vote followed the bans, the eviction of Union members from the Diet and the bombings of Caldera and other cities in 178 AG. No Union party stood. The SDP fell to 14 seats, and NCP and PDP together took 404 seats and formed the Reformation government.

By camp, The People’s Coalition holds 222 (down 56); The Way holds 214 (up 86); Independents hold 30 (up 10). No camp has a majority, so The People’s Coalition needs 12 more seats from other camps or independents to form a government. The Way trails by 8 seats.

Seats by party. The People’s Coalition: PDP 190, SDP 14, Civic Progress 10, Agrarian Labor 8. The Way: NCP 214. Independents: Independents 30.

Across 33 provinces, The People’s Coalition led in 17, The Way led in 14, Independents led in 2. The People’s Coalition was strongest in Kazawa (23 seats), Entoro (S) (21 seats), Yahahama (15 seats).

The closest provinces were Kikonokawa, where The Way won 5 seats to 4 for The People’s Coalition; Caldera, where The People’s Coalition won 4 seats to 3 for The Way; Shinkawa, where The People’s Coalition won 3 seats to 1 for The Way.

Eleven provinces changed hands from 176 AG, including Hoshima (The People’s Coalition to Independents), Kikonokawa (The Union to The Way), Kiyora (The People’s Coalition to The Way), Yahafurano (The People’s Coalition to The Way), Aokawa (The People’s Coalition to The Way).

Turnout was 85.0%, with about 126.4 million votes cast, up from 69.0% in 176 AG.

Voters in the Fire Nation’s 33 provinces elect the National Diet, and a majority is 234 seats. The vote was held outside the usual February 2 date.

cs_diet_election_176.title: Union wins 40 seats in final vote before bans
cs_diet_election_176.html:
SDP was the largest single party with 152 seats. The Way held 128 seats. The Concord of Nations then banned the Equalist Party, The Collective and Salvation Front, and their members were evicted from the Diet.

By camp, The People’s Coalition holds 278 (up 22); The Way holds 128 (up 2); The Union holds 40 (down 22); Independents hold 20 (down 2). The People’s Coalition can govern without partners. The Way trails by 150 seats.

Seats by party. The People’s Coalition: SDP 152, PDP 70, Agrarian Labor 44, Civic Progress 12. The Way: NCP 128. The Union: Salvation Front 16, Equalist Party 15, The Collective 9. Independents: Independents 20.

The Union, made up of the Equalist Party, The Collective and Salvation Front, won 40 seats, down 22 from 172 AG. Its strongest provinces were Umi (10), Yahahama (9), Kikonokawa (6).

Across 33 provinces, The People’s Coalition led in 24, The Way led in 6, The Union led in 3. The People’s Coalition was strongest in Kazawa (27 seats), Entoro (S) (21 seats), Youizumo (15 seats).

The closest provinces were Hoshima, where The People’s Coalition tied with Independents at 1 seat; Shinkawa, where The People’s Coalition tied with The Union at 2 seats; Higashikawa, where The People’s Coalition tied with The Way at 7 seats.

Five provinces changed hands from 172 AG, including Hoshima (Independents to The People’s Coalition), Shinkawa (The Union to The People’s Coalition), Yahahama (The Union to The People’s Coalition), Takahama (The Union to The People’s Coalition), Shirashihoro (The Union to The People’s Coalition).

Turnout was 69.0%, with about 101.5 million votes cast, down from 72.0% in 172 AG.

Voters in the Fire Nation’s 33 provinces elect the National Diet, and a majority is 234 seats. Polling day was the traditional February 2 (why February 2).

cs_diet_election_172.title: Union drops to 62 seats after crash-relief dispute
cs_diet_election_172.html:
SDP was the largest single party with 129 seats. The losses followed criticism of the Union’s handling of relief after the 171 AG crash. Its remaining seats lie almost entirely in Yahahama, Umi, Takahama, Shirashihoro and the island chain.

By camp, The People’s Coalition holds 256 (up 20); The Way holds 126 (unchanged); The Union holds 62 (down 20); Independents hold 22 (unchanged). The People’s Coalition can govern without partners. The Way trails by 130 seats.

Seats by party. The People’s Coalition: SDP 129, PDP 68, Agrarian Labor 45, Civic Progress 14. The Way: NCP 126. The Union: Equalist Party 24, Salvation Front 24, The Collective 14. Independents: Independents 22.

The Union, made up of the Equalist Party, The Collective and Salvation Front, won 62 seats, down 20 from 168 AG. Its strongest provinces were Yahahama (13), Umi (13), Kikonokawa (9).

Across 33 provinces, The People’s Coalition led in 19, The Union led in 7, The Way led in 6, Independents led in 1. The People’s Coalition was strongest in Kazawa (26 seats), Entoro (S) (21 seats), Youizumo (15 seats).

The closest provinces were Higashikawa, where The People’s Coalition tied with The Way at 7 seats; Hatsushima, where The People’s Coalition tied with The Union at 1 seat; Okunata, where The People’s Coalition tied with The Way at 9 seats.

Two provinces changed hands from 168 AG, including Jinya (The Way to The People’s Coalition), Hinokage (The Way to The People’s Coalition).

Turnout was 72.0%, with about 103.6 million votes cast, down from 74.0% in 168 AG.

The lore wiki of an industrial-war alternate universe · 154 pages
A century is a long time to spend learning what a year could have taught.
Inscription on the memorial at Qinglan Port, 105 AG
What is New Red Dawn?

New Red Dawn is an alternate universe of Avatar: The Last Airbender in which the Fire Nation is the Empire of Tajisaki, a modern industrial state, and the Hundred Year War is the first total war of the age of steam and steel. The wiki is written as its own world's encyclopedia, with disputed figures and rival histories. Read more >

The Hundred Year War was a global conflict that lasted from 0 AG to 100 AG, waged by the Empire of Tajisaki against the Earth Kingdom, the Water Tribes, the Air Nomads and, from 30 AG, the Qianchan Republic. It was begun by Fire Lord Sozin, who used the return of a comet to attack the four Air Temples and destroy the Air Nomads, among whom the next Avatar was to be born. Over the next hundred years the Empire occupied the whole west coast of the Earth Kingdom, subjugated the Water Tribes, and fought for the oil of the Si Wong Desert. It developed jets, power armor and a weapon of mass destruction on the scale of the comet. It killed about {{stat:hyw_deaths_direct}} people, a little under 8% of the world's population in 0 AG, and committed two genocides and the war's other atrocities with chemical weapons that only it possessed.

The war ended in July 100 AG, when the Empire fired the Sōen at Ba Sing Se and its ruler, Ozai, was killed the next day by the Avatar in the Battle of Qinglan Port. The Empire's central authority collapsed. The wars and famines that followed, which killed another {{stat:hyw_postwar_deaths}} people, are known as the Post-War Conflicts.

Prelude

The Fire Nation's industrial revolution

The Fire Nation's apothecaries discovered gunpowder in about 3000 BG (see the [[point_of_divergence|point of divergence]]), its armies began to use it in earnest in 1000–700 BG and, by 290 BG, had begun the world's first industrial revolution. By 80 BG it had a four-round bolt-action rifle, and in 27 BG its first aircraft flew. It discovered oil in the Si Wong in 28 BG. The Qianchan Republic, which had seceded from the Earth Kingdom in 255 BG, matched it in a technological race from 26 BG. The Earth Kingdom, a large agrarian state, lagged behind, and industrialized only in the 20s AG with Qianchan's help. Firearms had spread slowly in the earlier centuries, because the populations were small, the necessary equipment was scarce and bending had a sacred place in folklore.

Sozin's plan

Avatar Roku, Sozin's friend, died in 12 BG on Island Jezhi, and Sozin, who could have helped him, left him to die. Sozin knew that the next Avatar would be born among the Air Nomads. He militarized the Fire Nation for twelve years, and planned to use the comet's return to exterminate the Air Nomads, and then to subjugate the Water Tribes and conquer the Earth Kingdom.

The world in 0 AG

The world's population was about {{stat:world_pop_0}}: the Earth Kingdom {{stat:pop_ek_0}}, the Qianchan Republic {{stat:pop_qc_0}}, the Fire Nation {{stat:pop_fn_0}}, the Water Tribes {{stat:pop_nwt_0}}+{{stat:pop_swt_0}}+{{stat:pop_wt_other_0}} and the Air Nomads {{stat:pop_an_0}}. The Earth Kingdom, with its provincial lords, had little central authority outside Ba Sing Se. The Fire Nation was the most industrialized state in the world.

Early stage (0–30 AG)

The Air Nomad Genocide

On the night the comet arrived, the Empire attacked the four Air Temples at once, with zeppelins carrying aircraft that could reach 4,000 meters, and firebombs and napalm shells enlarged by comet-empowered firebenders. Within a week it had razed the Western and Eastern island chains with their civilians, firebombed the Northern Air Temple and kept its ruin for an airbase, and taken the Southern Air Temple, the home of the next Avatar. About 3 million Air Nomads, benders and non-benders, died, together with about 400,000 Water Tribe and other civilians killed as collateral on ships and islands. The last Air Nomad community was killed in the snow of the South Pole in 20 AG. About 300–400 people with airbending survived, deep in Qianchan or the Earth Kingdom, and most did not know what they were. The Empire occupied the Western and Southern chains completely and built bases on them.

The Water Tribes

A week after the genocide began, the Empire bombarded both poles on Sozin's orders. In the First Battle of Agna Qel'a (11–19 September 0 AG), the Northern Battlegroup and a zeppelin division attacked the Northern capital with an incendiary made for ice. The Northern Water Tribe, with elite riflemen and waterbenders, repelled the landing, at a cost of about 52,000 dead, and the Empire settled for a forward air base on the far eastern pole, from which it bombed Agna Qel'a periodically. In the South the landings succeeded. The leaders were captured and forced to cooperate, and the Empire ran an occupation of forced labor, reprisals and terror, aimed at working the Southern Tribe to death. Uprisings and insurgency followed, the last of the early ones in 29 AG, and the South's population fell to 75% of its pre-war number. This is described in the article on the Subjugation of the Water Tribes.

Yanakawa and the west coast

In January 1 AG the Empire launched the invasion of Yanakawa, the Earth Kingdom's western coastal province, from its bases on the Southern Air Temple chain. Its landing at Yu Dao began the Yanakawan Campaign, in which provincial levies attacked in mass against entrenched Imperial machine guns, and the Empire introduced mustard gas, the first use of chemical weapons in the war. The Earth Kingdom never acquired chemical weapons of its own. The campaign took ten years and killed about 3.5 million Earth Kingdom people and 450,000 Imperial soldiers. By 10 AG the Empire held the whole west coast.

The northern and southern pushes

From 10 AG the Empire pushed north into the mountains, and in the 20s tried to reach Omashu and break east from the south of Yanakawa. It was foiled, and instead turned into the high mountains and, by 25 AG, had cut the southern Omashu front off from the rest of the Earth Kingdom, which Qianchan then supplied by sea. By 27 AG the Empire pushed toward the Si Wong for its oil. Throughout, the Imperial Navy alone held naval superiority.

Qianchan enters the war

In 27 AG a Qianchan civilian ship was sunk near the Southern Air Temple waters. The first naval engagement between the Imperial and Qianchan navies, in 30 AG, was a draw, and Qianchan entered the war and allied with the Earth Kingdom. It supplied it with arms and doctrine, and helped it begin to industrialize.

Middle stage (30–95 AG)

Eastern Push (30–50 AG)

The Empire's General Staff planned to push east across the grasslands to the Si Wong for its oil. It took the western grasslands in a series of tank battles, including the Hesha Plains (37–38 AG) and the siege of Dongping (41–43 AG), and by 50 AG the Imperial front ran from the north coast down the western plains to the desert's western edge and across the sea through the Southern Air Temple chain. The Eastern Push killed about 6.8 million Earth Kingdom people.

Desert War (50–79 AG)

The Desert War was the Empire's first attempt on the oil fields, mostly an air war with small gains. It captured the fields four times, in 56, 63, 71 and 77 AG, and was thrown off each time by Qianchan–Earth Kingdom counter-offensives. About 1.1 million people died.

Si Wong Offensive (80–88 AG)

The second attempt, Plan Yellow, drawn up by General Iroh as the General Staff Directorate's Planning Director, was a ground offensive that took the Tongba oil basin and the desert's road and rail corridor between 8 July 80 and 23 August 88 AG. Coalition supply lines were forced around the desert, and the Empire held the oil until Ozai's death. About 1.9 million personnel fought on each side. The oil paid for the late war's technologies: the first jet flew in 81 AG, the mechanized Breaker armor in 83 AG, and the first assault rifle in 95 AG.

The South and the poles in the middle years

The Southern Water Tribe's population fell to about 50% by 99 AG, as the Empire turned the South into a colony and research base. Imperial raiding forces, the Southern Raiders, hunted the last waterbenders. The Northern Water Tribe, which had no navy, lost about 20% of its people to bombing by 40 AG. The Empire's policy toward both was elimination by labor and bombardment.

Jasmine Island (90 AG)

On 7 June 90 AG Rear Admiral Yueya destroyed the harbor town and fields of Jasmine Island, which killed about 2,000 civilians, in a mutiny that was stopped by the garrison, by Navy sailors who broke out of the brig of a battlecruiser, and by Captain Lu Ten of the Armored Corps. Lu Ten then submitted an Address on Conduct to the Diet, and became the center of a reform movement.

Late stage (95–100 AG)

Siege of Ba Sing Se (96–97 AG)

In 95 AG the Imperial eastern group took Hanxu and Babao, the junctions at the Si Wong's eastern edge, and the Empire, fueled by the Si Wong oil, launched its greatest offensive. Field Marshal Iroh's army besieged Ba Sing Se from 14 February 96 AG. Imperial bombers breached the Outer Wall in March with a super-heavy conventional bomb. The Empire's jets and turboprop bombers controlled the sky, and its aircraft dropped leaflets urging surrender, then bombs and chemical weapons across the rings. King Kuei's eyes were opened in the first weeks of the siege. Qianchan, which was in effect the southern province that had broken away, refused to commit troops until Kuei was evacuated, and kept its air force at the Omashu front. The city's western section was gassed and bombed, and civilians died in huge numbers: about 2.7 million of the siege's 3.5 million dead were civilians. In the Inner City, Imperial assault battalions took the Palace and held it for a week before civilian conscripts and metalbenders drove them out. Lu Ten was killed there on 25 November. A Qianchan-led counter-offensive retook Hanxu and Babao and cut the Imperial supply line, and the siege ended on 19 April 97 AG. Iroh was demoted, and Azulon, who had lost faith in him, issued an Ash Directive to raze the city, which Iroh opposed.

The Fire Nation: Azulon, Ozai and the Pardon Crisis

On 10 June 97 AG Fire Lord Azulon was poisoned at dinner and died in his sleep, in a killing that Ozai arranged and that the Court blamed on Qianchan agents. Ozai was crowned on 24 June, and on 3 July pardoned Yueya and Zhao, who had been convicted over Jasmine Island, and sent them to the Southern Water Tribe's small-scale insurgency. The Diet and part of the military lost faith in him. The opposition gathered around Iroh, who was forced to retire in 98 AG and given a seat in the Diet, and the Diet passed bills for veterans and for the people, but the Eastern Colonies Assimilation Bill, which would have given Yanakawa citizenship, was shelved. This polarized the Empire, as described in the Pardon Crisis of 97 AG.

The Earth Kingdom: the Dai Li coup attempt (98 AG)

In the early hours of 22 March 98 AG, the Dai Li, led by Grand Secretariat Long Feng, tried to seize King Kuei and rule through him, as they had murdered his father. The coup failed within fourteen hours, and killed about 1,900 people. The Dai Li were purged in the Great Review (98–99 AG), from 2,400 agents to about 700, and Kuei took direct command of the war from Ba Sing Se on the Northern Front. A second, smaller attempt in January 100 AG was also put down.

The polar operation (99 AG)

On 13 November 99 AG the Empire began a combined operation against both poles, to eradicate the Water Tribes so that no new Avatar could rise from them, and to scorch the poles clear for a new Fire Nation colony. In the South it crushed the Southern Uprising (12 May – 9 December 99 AG). The Avatar, Aang, was found in the ice by Southern guerrillas in late November and evacuated to Qianchan as the capital fell. In the North it launched the Siege of the North, the Second Battle of Agna Qel'a, with jets carrying chemical and napalm bombs and elite winter troops, many of them veterans of the South, in Arctic Breaker armor with flamethrowers. About 800,000 people died in the city in five weeks. The Chief and most of the Council were evacuated by Qianchan submarines. By June 100 AG the North's population had fallen to 50%, and the South's to about 30% by the end of the war.

The Coalition Northern Offensive and the Ba Sing Se Treaty (100 AG)

In February–March 100 AG a joint Qianchan–Earth Kingdom offensive tried to crush the Empire once and for all, and failed against Imperial air power, gas and fuel from the Si Wong. The Ba Sing Se Treaty (27 March) put the two armies under a Combined Coalition Command at Ba Sing Se, with Kuei as nominal head.

The Sōen

The Imperial Research Bureau had worked for decades, from 47 AG, to harness the comet and to build a nuclear-scale weapon of mass destruction. IRB scientists who refused to build a fission weapon were executed in 99 AG, and the program produced the Sōen, a fire-crystal array fed by firebending. It was built for one purpose, the strike on Ba Sing Se. On 17 July 100 AG Ozai, who was at the forward array at Qinglan Port, fired it, and the beam atomized the western Outer Wall and destroyed the Inner Wall. It killed about 380,000 people, blinded thousands and burned many more, and destroyed the Coalition's command for 36 hours. The Imperial army, which had been organized and ready, advanced into the disorganized defenders, and was thrown off by what followed.

Conclusion (July 100 AG)

Battle of Qinglan Port (18 July 100 AG)

The Yanakawan Liberation Front, which had been fighting the Empire since April, and Earth Kingdom and Qianchan units, with the Avatar, attacked Qinglan Port at noon on 18 July, to capture the Sōen array before a second discharge. The Imperial garrison was caught off guard, and Ozai, who had proclaimed himself Tentei (Emperor of the Sky) the day before, was killed by the Avatar in the Avatar State, with a stone lance through his lungs, 23 minutes after the first shells fell. Soldiers on both sides watched. At 12:27 an Imperial officer announced over the high command radio, "The Emperor is dead." The Empire's fanatical units fought on until 19:00, and the rest surrendered, fled or fought each other.

The succession crisis

The General Staff Directorate rigged the Privy Council's succession for Ozai's daughter Azula in a few violent days, over the Diet's resolution for the popular Zuko. The press was outraged, and the Diet's defiance in August was met with shooting. This was the start of the Fire Nation Civil War. Royalist propaganda later credited Zuko with the defeat of Ozai.

Aftermath

The Post-War Conflicts (100–120 AG)

The wars and famines that followed killed about 19 million people, and are counted as the third most deadly war in history, after the Hundred Year War and the Warring States wars.

  • Earth Kingdom warlord wars (100–112 AG). After the Sōen strike destroyed the command in Ba Sing Se, generals and warlords fought each other and starved the country, until Omashu, Ba Sing Se and Gaoling, the Qianchan capital, pacified them. About 13 million died.
  • Yanakawan War of Independence (100–110 AG). The YLF and its allies won independence in a war with twelve decisive battles, which ended on land with the Treaty of Qinglan on 28 April 105 AG. The Court faction under Azula continued the war at sea until 110 AG. About 1.2 million died. It led to the United Republic of Nations.
  • Fire Nation Civil War (100–118 AG). The Royalists under Zuko, the Ozai loyalists and the Salvationists fought for 18 years, with the Salvationists taking over most of the Court's field army from within and breaking with it in 116 AG. About 3.5 million died. The war ended with Azula's death in a duel with Zuko on 9 May 118 AG.
  • Holdouts and the polar famines accounted for the rest.

Zuko's reign and the United Republic

Zuko was crowned Fire Lord in 118 AG, survived an assassination attempt at his coronation, and spent his 50-year reign rebuilding. The United Republic of Nations emerged from Yanakawa, with a flag designed by Lord Sokka. Qianchan took custody of the Southern Air Temple and gave the remaining airbenders autonomy.

Casualties and demographics

About 30 million died before the Si Wong Offensive began. For every Fire Nation death there were about eight Earth Kingdom deaths, because of the industrial gap, the Earth Kingdom's mass-charge doctrine, its fragmented command, the Empire's chemical weapons and air power, and the occupation policy of genocide and famine. The ratio narrowed to about 1.4 to 1 at Si Wong, after Qianchan armed the Earth Kingdom, but the sieges of civilians kept the overall ratio high. The world's population was about 548 million in 100 AG, after about 81 million excess deaths (ledger).

Historiography

Imperial histories describe the war as a campaign of unification and economical conquest. Earth Kingdom histories tend to blame their provincial lords and give no casualty or famine figures. Qianchan archives, which hold the most complete record of ships, convoys, intercepts and gas casualties, are the main outside source. Royalist propaganda after 118 AG gave Zuko the credit for ending the war.

The Kingdom of Tajisaki, commonly the Fire Nation, is a constitutional monarchy on the Fire Islands, an archipelago in the south-east of the world. It has about 214 million inhabitants, a capital at Caldera City and a Fire Lord, Izumi, who has reigned since 168 AG. It is the world’s second-largest economy, after Qianchan, and the most densely industrialized, and until 118 AG it was the Empire of Tajisaki, the aggressor of the Hundred Year War. The Empire’s authority collapsed with the death of Fire Lord Ozai in July 100 AG, and the eighteen-year Fire Nation Civil War that followed ended with the victory of Zuko’s Royalists. The state that emerged was a kingdom in which the Fire Lord reigns and the National Diet, restored in 119 AG, governs.

In 170 AG the Fire Nation is a wealthy, orderly and uneasy country. It has rebuilt a devastated archipelago, converted its war industry to housing, rail and export, and returned to the family of nations through the Concord of Nations. It has also spent fifty-two years declining to settle what it thinks of its own past. The Diet has a majority for the People’s Coalition under Prime Minister Ryoko Sato, a large conservative opposition and a left, the Union, that has lost more than half its seats since 156 AG but still holds 82 of 466. The old Salvationist movement is banned as an armed organization and survives as a political tradition, as an embarrassment to the government and, in the western cities, as a threat. The port city of Joha has been under curfew in some districts for most of a year, and the Fire Lord’s father, Zuko, has not appeared in public since the autumn of 154 AG.

Names and etymology

The state’s formal name under the Empire was Tajisaki, after the ruling clan, and “the Fire Nation” was the name used by foreigners and, increasingly, by the Empire’s own press. The constitution of 119 AG adopted “the Kingdom of Tajisaki” as the formal name of the realm, dropped the word “Empire” and the title of Tentei that Ozai had claimed, and kept “Fire Nation” as the ordinary name in speech only. In law the state is the Kingdom of Tajisaki, in the Diet’s statutes, in treaties, on coinage and on passports, and every state institution takes its formal name from Tajisaki, as the Tajisaki Royal Navy does, with “Imperial” before 119 AG and “Royal” after it. Before the Empire, in the old Tajisaki clan’s law, it was Tajisaki in the same way. The Royal House is the House of Tajisaki, and the Fire Lord signs as such. The Concord of Nations seats it as the Kingdom of Tajisaki, and the United Republic’s press calls it the Fire Nation or, when it wishes to be unkind, the Empire.

The word Tajisaki is older than any document that mentions it. The Academy of Caldera’s linguists derive it from an Old Tajisaki phrase meaning “the cape that holds the fire,” and the clan’s own genealogies derive it from the cape on the principal island where the first Fire Lord was crowned. The people of the islands call themselves Fire Nationals, and the demonym has no religious or racial sense in law since 119 AG, when the Homeland Purity Initiative was repealed and the category of Recognized Imperial Persons abolished with it.

History since 118 AG

The earlier history of the state, from the unification in 4440 BG to the end of the Hundred Year War, is told at History of the Fire Nation and, in summary, in the section on the Empire of Tajisaki below. This section covers the kingdom.

Restoration and settlement (118–131 AG)

Zuko was crowned Fire Lord on 9 May 118 AG, after killing his sister Azula in the Duel of the Palace, and the armistice that ended the principal civil war took effect on 13 August. The country he ruled had lost about 3.5 million dead in the civil war, had 7 to 10 million people displaced, and was without a functioning currency in the western provinces. The first years of the reign were given to emergency relief. The new government’s priorities, set out in Zuko’s address to the Diet’s provisional council in October 118, were to feed the country, to reopen the railways and ports, to disarm the countryside and to bring the Court’s and the Salvationists’ officials to account. The first three were largely done by 122 AG. The last was left to the Commission on Imperial Conduct, which sat from 125 to 131.

The Revised Constitution of 118 AG, issued by Rescript and submitted to the Diet, was replaced the following year by the constitution of 119 AG, which restored the National Diet, abolished its exclusion from military and security questions, dissolved the ministries of Truth and National Harmony and placed the General Staff Directorate under the Cabinet. The Fire Lord, who had been absolute and inviolable, became head of state with the power to dissolve the House of Representatives on the Prime Minister’s advice and with a continuing role as the nation’s moral authority. The Fire Sages were restored to their spiritual functions under a Great Sage. Suffrage, which the Empire had tied to military service, was extended to all adults in 125 AG, and conscription was abolished in 122 AG. The Sōen arrays at Caldera were dismantled under the Caldera Accord of 121 AG, which also founded the Concord of Nations, and the chemical stockpiles were destroyed under international inspection in the years that followed.

The Commission on Imperial Conduct published its report in 131 AG. It named about 2,400 officials, officers and propagandists as responsible for atrocities in the war, recommended 190 prosecutions, of which 112 led to convictions, and set out in detail the work of the Ministry of Truth, the General Staff Directorate and the Imperial Research Bureau. The report did not recommend proceedings against the Royalist command, and its silence on the siege of Hira and on the Royalist conduct of the war was criticized at the time and has been criticized since. It remains the founding document of the postwar state, and its chapter on the Eastern Territories, which has no counterpart in earlier Fire Nation historiography, is taught in the schools.

Reconstruction and growth (131–153 AG)

The economic recovery of 140 AG, which brought output above its level of 99 AG for the first time, is the point from which most Fire Nationals date the end of the war. Housing, rail and the conversion of the war industries to civilian production drove it. The great shipyards at Port Hana built merchant tonnage, the ironworks of the northern islands supplied the rail programme, and the Tajisaki Institute of Science, which had succeeded the Imperial Research Bureau’s western complex, began the work on jet propulsion and fission engineering that has been the country’s main scientific export. Joint research on fission with Qianchan began in 144 AG. The oil that the Empire had taken from the Si Wong Desert was now bought under the Si Wong Accord, and the cost of that purchase, a fifth of imports by value, became the country’s principal strategic dependence.

The Diet in these years was dominated by the Restoration Party, the Royalists’ successor, which governed alone until 141 AG and in coalition thereafter. The party split in 141 over the pace of land reform, and its conservative wing, representing the landowners of the west and north, became the National Conservative Party, known in the press as the Old Guard and abbreviated NCP. Its liberal-urban wing became the Democratic Reform Party, the DRP, which the press called the Reform bloc and the early notes sometimes call the PDP. Neither party has held a majority since. The left, which had been banned in its Salvationist form, reorganized in the legal parties of the Union: the Equalist Party, the Salvation Front and the Collective, which were registered between 133 and 141 AG and were by 156 AG the largest force in the industrial south and the western ports.

The Joha Crisis and the withdrawal of the Fire Lord (153–155 AG)

The death of King Kuei of the Earth Kingdom in August 153 AG revived leftist rallies in cities from Caldera City outward, and the failure of the Caldera lender Hakuryu Trust on 27 September brought the Caldera Exchange down by 31 percent in two sessions. The shock hit the ports hardest. In Joha, the port city whose quay had been the site of the killings of July 100 AG, two companies laid off 2,300 workers on 5 October, and the Dockworkers’ Union, which says that the harbor’s employers have owed back pay since the reconstruction, called a march for the 9th. Police fired on the marchers at the Customs Road crossing. Three people were killed, according to both police and union; by December there were riots in the grain towns inland and curfews in four of the prefecture’s six districts. The Joha Crisis, which lasted until at least September 154 AG, is covered in its own article. Its political effects were three.

First, it brought the Union into the Diet in force. The elections of February 156 AG, the first held after the crisis, gave the three Union parties 150 of 466 seats, 32 percent of the House and the second-largest bloc, behind the People’s Coalition (172) and ahead of the Old Guard (118). Second, it broke the Royal Household’s silence. Zuko, who had visited Joha on 11 September 154 AG to calm the city, left public view after the visit. The Household said that he was resting on his physicians’ advice, and in the years that followed he was seen only by his family, his doctors and a handful of ministers. His daughter, Her Highness Izumi, took over the ceremonial duties of the throne. Third, the Household’s attempt to give the nation a symbol of stability, in the birth of Izumi’s second child, Kiko, on 28 December 155 AG and her name, “hope,” made the court a topic of popular discussion for the first time in thirty years.

The Union years and the unrest (156–168 AG)

The decade after 156 AG is called the Union years in the Fire Nation press. The Union’s seats fell from 150 in 156 to 128 in 160, 104 in 164 and 82 in 168, as scandals over the misspending of relief money in its provincial machines hurt it, and the People’s Coalition, a bloc of the Social Democrats, the DRP, Agrarian Labor and the Civic Progress Party, grew from 172 seats to 236. The Union never lost its core. Its seats lay in eight provinces, Shirashihoro, Umi, Yahahama, Takahama, Shinkawa, Narukawa, Kikonokawa and Hatsushima, and in the western ports, and after 164 AG it sat almost entirely inside them.

The unrest that began in the United Republic, the Earth Kingdom and the Water Tribes in 167 AG, with the founding of the Equalists and the revival of the Harmonists, reached the Fire Nation at the edges. The Union’s three parties disowned the Equalist movement abroad, and the Diet’s Old Guard did not believe them. The Thunderbolt sect, which broke from the Salvationists in 169 AG, drew its members from unemployed veterans and students, and its attacks in the western cities in 170 AG, mostly with old Court weapons, killed about thirty people. See Unrest of 167–171 AG.

Abdication and the reign of Izumi (168–170 AG)

Zuko abdicated on 20 May 168 AG in a rescript read in the Diet by the Grand Chamberlain. The Household gave his health as the reason, and the press has reported, without confirmation, that the physicians suspected poisoning. Izumi, who had performed the ceremonial duties of the throne for fourteen years, was crowned in a short ceremony at the Palace in Caldera City, the first in which the Fire Lord took an oath to the constitution and not to the nation. She was about forty-seven, and she reigned beside her husband, Ryota Kōga, with her son Iroh as Crown Prince.

The People’s Coalition won an outright majority in the Diet election of February 168 AG, the first time that any camp had done so since the Restoration Party’s fall, and Ryoko Sato, the Social Democrats’ leader, formed a government. Her first two years in office were given to the relief programme for the western ports, the unsettled back pay of the Joha dock crews, and the rising disorder abroad. By the summer of 170 AG the government was watching the crisis in Republic City with a concern that, in the Cabinet’s minutes, is more than diplomatic: the United Republic’s radical movements had friends in the Fire Nation, and the Republic’s refugees, if there were any, would arrive on the Fire Nation’s coast.

Government and politics

The Fire Nation is a unitary constitutional monarchy. The constitution of 119 AG, which replaced the Revised Constitution of 118 AG, vests executive power in the Cabinet, responsible to the House of Representatives, and gives the Fire Lord the functions of a head of state: the opening of the Diet, the appointment of the Prime Minister on the House’s nomination, the signing of statutes, the dissolution of the House on the Prime Minister’s advice and the representation of the realm abroad. The Fire Lord is no longer sacred in law, may be investigated through the Grand Chamberlain by the Diet’s Committee on the Household, and no longer commands the armed forces alone. She remains, by custom and by the constitution’s preamble, the “moral head of the nation,” a phrase that has given rise to more legal argument than any other in the text.

The Throne and the Household

The Royal Household Office speaks for the Throne in official statements, and a Grand Chamberlain answers to the Diet for the Household’s budget and conduct. The Palace Protocol Office handles state occasions. The Fire Lord in 170 AG is Izumi, who reigns beside her husband, Ryota Kōga, a former shipping lawyer whom the press calls the Consort. Their elder child, Iroh, is Crown Prince; their younger, Kiko (Princess Ayako), is a singer who signed with the AZura label in 170 AG and is the second non-bender born into the House of Tajisaki in more than five hundred years. The line of succession follows the Fire Lord’s designation, confirmed by the Diet, a change from the Empire’s rule that a designation was final and that the Privy Council confirmed it by a fire-producing ceremony within seven days. The Privy Council was abolished in 119 AG, and the ceremony, which had been the cause of the rigged succession of 100 AG, was dropped from the constitution.

The Household’s reputation, as of 170 AG, is strained by the long absence of the previous Fire Lord. Zuko has not been seen in public since the visit to Joha on 11 September 154 AG, and the Office’s statements, that he is “at rest” in the Palace’s eastern wing, have been disbelieved by a third of the public in opinion surveys. The Diet’s Committee on the Household has asked three times since 168 AG for a medical statement, and has received a letter signed by three physicians.

The National Diet

The National Diet has two houses. The House of Lords holds the heads of the thirteen great houses, who serve ten-year terms, and appointed life peers, and may delay but not block legislation, except on matters touching the Household, on which it has a veto. The House of Representatives has 466 members, elected every four years by the voters of the Fire Nation’s 33 provinces, with 234 seats a majority. Each province returns a block of members, from one in Hatsushima to twenty-six in Kazawa, and the House’s size was fixed by the electoral law of 125 AG, which also established universal adult suffrage. By custom elections are held on 2 February, the date of the Battle of Akagawa Ford in about 300 BG and of the first opening of the Diet, a holiday that the Fire Nation has kept for 2,400 years. Turnout in the election of 168 AG was 74 percent, with about 104.1 million votes cast.

The House that sat in 170 AG was elected on 2 February 168 and is the product of a decade in which the main camps have changed places. The People’s Coalition, the governing bloc, holds 236 seats: the Social Democratic Party (SDP) 115, the Democratic Reform Party (DRP) 66, the Agrarian Labor Party 41 and the Civic Progress Party 14. The Old Guard, in the press the Way, is the National Conservative Party (NCP), with 126 seats. The Union holds 82: the Equalist Party 34, the Salvation Front 32 and the Collective 16. There are 22 independents. A Coalition government can pass legislation without partners, a position that no camp has held since 141 AG.

Parties and currents

The politics of the kingdom is a contest of three camps and a fringe. The Old Guard, the National Conservative Party, is conservative, agrarian and traditionalist, the party of the great landowners of the west and north and of the families that were Royalist officers, and is strongest in the western and northern provinces. It has held between 118 and 126 seats since 156 AG. The People’s Coalition unites four parties whose programs differ, and which have contested each other’s seats at every election. The SDP is the legal moderate left, supported by unions and tenant farmers in the industrial south. The DRP is liberal-urban, the party of merchants, bankers and the professional classes, strongest in the central and eastern provinces. The Agrarian Labor Party is the party of small farmers and rural workers. The Civic Progress Party is a small group of technocrats and reforming officials, strongest in the cities. The Coalition is held together by its opposition to the Old Guard and, since 164 AG, by the need to compete with the Union.

The Union is the legal heir of the Salvationist tradition, though its parties would deny it in the form of a lineage. The Equalist Party, which has no connection to the Equalist movement of the United Republic that its enemies assert, campaigns for equal pay and for the abolition of the army’s service academies’ preference for bending families. The Salvation Front, the largest of the three until 164 AG, takes its name and a part of its program from the veterans’ committees of the civil war, and its leaders say that it stands for the committees’ social program without their methods. The Collective is a farm-labor party that draws on the peasant committees of the western provinces. The three parties sit as a bloc, share funds and a whip, and were registered between 133 and 141 AG after the Diet decided that the Salvationists’ armed organization had ended and that its veterans could organize politically. Their strongest provinces are Umi, Yahahama and Takahama, and their weakest are the central and eastern provinces, where in 168 AG they won no seats at all.

Outside the law are the Salvationist remnants, who were banned in 120 AG and who survive as a few cells in the western cities, the Thunderbolt sect, a faction of the younger Salvationists that broke away in 169 AG and has attacked police stations and railway depots in the west, and the Harmonists and Equalists of the United Republic, whose handbills the police found in the Joha unrest. The government treats them as a police problem, and the Union’s parties condemn their violence. The Old Guard does not accept the distinction.

Administration and law

The Fire Nation is divided into 33 provinces, each under a governor appointed by the Cabinet and a provincial assembly elected by the voters. The provinces include the main islands’ industrial heartland (Kazawa, Entoro North and South, Okuzawa, Youizumo), the western belt (Jinya, Funashina, Okugata, Hinokage, Kamisukita) and the southern island chain (Shirashihoro, Hatsushima). The five cities of more than five million, Caldera City, Harbor Kuro, Shinja, Port Hana and Taisu, are governed by their own mayors under provincial charters. The prefectures within the provinces, such as Joha’s six districts, are the units of police and tax administration. The Ministry of the Interior appoints the prefectural governors, among them Genji Hoshino at Joha.

The legal system is a civil-law system with a Supreme Court of fifteen justices, appointed by the Cabinet with the consent of the House of Representatives, and with a Constitutional Chamber that decides disputes between the Diet and the Cabinet. The courts of the Empire, which were subject to the Ministry of Truth, were reformed in 119 AG, and the Ministry’s successors are the National Police Agency and the Public Security Bureau, both under the Ministry of the Interior. Capital punishment was abolished in 128 AG. The Agni Kai, which the Empire had made a duel to the death, survives as a regulated, non-lethal contest of honor with a physician present.

Foreign relations

The Fire Nation is a member of the Concord of Nations, founded by the Caldera Accord of 121 AG, and has full relations with every state. Its foreign policy is run by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs under Foreign Minister Hayato Mori, and its guiding principle, stated in successive white papers, is “no rival, no empire, no isolation.” The Royal Household also has a diplomatic role: the Fire Lord receives ambassadors, and the Palace has hosted the Concord’s ceremonial sessions.

Qianchan. Relations with the Qianchan Republic have moved from the rivalry of the technology race and the wartime alliance of convenience to a wary partnership. The two states are the Concord’s founders and its largest contributors, compete in steel, shipbuilding and machine tools, and run joint research on fission, which began in 144 AG. Qianchan armed and supplied the Royalists through the Southern Air Temple island chain and holds the Fire Nation’s gratitude and its suspicion in about equal measure. The Salvationist exiles who settled in Qianchan’s southern island chain after 120 AG are a standing irritant.

The United Republic of Nations. The Fire Nation’s relations with the Republic, born of its former colonies, are close and tense. The two share a language of commerce and a long history of grievance, and the Republic’s veterans remember the Eastern Territories. About 600,000 Fire Nationals live in the Republic, and its Fire Nation minority, the largest in the Republic’s cities, has a seat on the Republic Council in the person of Councillor Ilama of Yu Dao. The government wants trade and a common commercial framework without reopening the claims that the Republic’s Truth and Reconciliation Commission has left unsettled. In 170 AG, with Republic City in turmoil, Prime Minister Sato’s government is careful to avoid any public comment on the Republic’s internal affairs.

The Earth Kingdom. The Fire Nation pays no cash reparations for the war, but funds the Rebuilding Fund for the Earth Kingdom’s occupied provinces, and is the largest importer of its grain. Relations with Queen Hou-Ting’s government are correct and cold. Hou-Ting’s reversal of the reforms of King Kuei has made her unpopular with the Diet’s liberals, and the Old Guard regards her as a necessary evil.

Other states. The Fire Nation has embassies in the Northern and Southern Water Tribes, whose navies are small, and an old and sensitive relationship with the airbenders of the Southern Air Temple, where the Fire Lord’s apology for the Air Nomad Genocide, delivered by Zuko in 119 AG and repeated by Izumi in 169, is remembered by both sides. Relations with the Yanakawan peninsula, whose independence the Empire fought for ten years after Ozai’s death, are those of ordinary neighbors, with a border arrangement on the island of Kuroshima that the Diet renews every five years.

Military

The armed forces of the Fire Nation number about 420,000 active personnel, a small fraction of the 8,000,000 that the Empire fielded in 80 AG. Conscription was abolished in 122 AG, and the forces are volunteer, with a reserve of about 900,000. The Army, Navy and Air Service answer to the Ministry of Defense, which has been under civilian ministers since 119 AG, and the General Staff Directorate, once an independent organ with a right of direct audience with the Fire Lord, was placed under the Cabinet and is now the Defense Staff. The old divide between the Army and the Navy persists mainly as a rivalry over the budget, which in 170 AG is about 2.1 percent of output.

The Tajisaki Royal Navy keeps the world’s largest fleet by tonnage, built around a carrier force inherited from the Empire, and the Marine Corps, with about 38,000 members, is the most prestigious unit in the forces. The Air Service flies the jet aircraft that the Imperial Research Bureau developed, now supplemented by the products of the Tajisaki Institute. The Army, which has about 210,000 members and about 700 tanks, is organized in twelve divisions, of which eight are in the west and north and four in the southern chain. The Sōen arrays at Caldera were dismantled under the Caldera Accord, and the chemical stockpiles were destroyed under international inspection in 123–131 AG. The Fire Nation has no nuclear weapons and has signed the Concord’s protocol against their development, a position that the Old Guard and the National Renewal group in the Diet have criticized as the abandonment of a national tradition.

The Home Guard, a part-time territorial force that Ito Shigeru set up during the insurgency, was reorganized as the National Guard in 125 AG and has about 60,000 members. It is a reserve for disaster relief and, in extremity, for internal security. The police, who carry sidearms in the west, are under the Ministry of the Interior, and the government has used the National Guard in Joha since December 153 AG.

Economy

The Fire Nation is the world’s second-largest economy, after Qianchan, with a nominal output of {{stat:gdp_fn_170}} in 170 AG, or {{stat:gdppc_fn_170}} a person, and one of the most densely industrialized. Output is led by steel, shipbuilding, machinery, chemicals, electronics and rail equipment, and by a services sector that employs about 58 percent of the workforce. Industry accounts for about 31 percent of employment and agriculture for about 11 percent. The Gini coefficient was 35.1 in 166 AG, a moderate figure that hides a persistent gap between the industrial cities and the rural south. The currency is the ryō, issued by the Bank of Tajisaki, which has been independent of the Cabinet since 126 AG.

Energy and strategic dependence

The Empire lost the oil of the Si Wong Desert in 100 AG and the kingdom buys it under the Si Wong Accord, a contract that covers about 60 percent of its liquid fuel and costs a fifth of its imports by value. The dependence is the main strategic fact of the economy, and every government since 118 AG has tried to reduce it. A third of the country’s electricity now comes from volcanic geothermal plants, built at Mount Hakai, Shirasaka and the southern chain from the 130s, and about a fifth from civilian fission, produced at four reactors built with Qianchan technology at Taigan, Kuma Bay, Oshima and Hanegawa. Coal, which supplied three quarters of power in 80 AG, supplies about a seventh. The Ember Greens, a pressure group rather than a party, campaign for the expansion of both geothermal and fission power, and the Union campaigns against the Si Wong Accord.

Industry, trade and finance

The great shipyards of Port Hana and Harbor Kuro are the world’s largest, and their order books in 170 AG run four years ahead, mostly for bulk carriers and container ships. The ironworks of the northern islands supply steel for the railway programme, which has electrified about 70 percent of the network since 135 AG. The Imperial Research Bureau’s old western complex is now the civilian Tajisaki Institute of Science, whose spin-offs make jet engines, ceramic armor and industrial robots. The Caldera Exchange, whose 31 percent fall in 153 AG set off the Joha Crisis, is the world’s second-largest by capitalization, and the Bank of Tajisaki holds about a fifth of the world’s official reserves. The Fire Nation’s largest trading partners are Qianchan, the Earth Kingdom, which supplies grain, and the United Republic. See Market crashes of 153 and 171 AG.

The unfinished business of the ports

The postwar economy was rebuilt around housing, rail and reconstruction, with the war industries converted to civilian production, and the rebuilding of the ports was done largely by dock crews who were paid in part with promissory notes. The notes were never fully redeemed. The Joha Dockworkers’ Union’s secretary, Haruki Nomura, puts the arrears at about 1.4 billion ryō, and the Dockworkers’ Union at Port Hana and Harbor Kuro have made similar claims. The Cabinet’s position is that the notes were a wartime instrument settled by the amnesty of 120 AG, a view that the Supreme Court has twice declined to review. The arrears are the economic root of the Joha Crisis and, with the Salvation Front’s organizing in the ports, of the Old Guard’s fear of a second revolution.

Science and technology

The Imperial Research Bureau was dissolved in 119 AG, and its western complex, which the Salvationists seized in 109 AG with its Ryuusei missiles and Tetsuken systems, became the Tajisaki Institute of Science in 121. The Institute leads in jet propulsion, materials science, volcanic engineering and seismology, and shares a civilian fission program with Qianchan. Its director, Dr. Ayako Minamoto, has said in public that the Institute has no weapons programme, and the Concord’s inspectors, who visit twice a year, have so far agreed. The Fire Nation’s universities are among the oldest in the world, and the Academy of Caldera, which also trains the country’s historians, is the largest. The Library of the Sages in Caldera City is the largest repository of the early records, and the Palace Archive, which holds the Court’s and the Ministry of Truth’s papers, was opened to scholars in 132 AG.

Demographics

The population was estimated at about 214 million in 170 AG, an increase of about 24 percent since 100 AG, and is among the most urbanized in the world, concentrated on the coastal plains and in the five cities of more than five million. They are Caldera City, Harbor Kuro, Shinja, Port Hana and Taisu. The census of 168 AG found a population that is about 91 percent Fire National by descent, with large minorities of Earth Kingdom, Water Tribe and mixed origin, many of them descendants of those deported during the war and of the settlers of the Eastern Territories who returned after 118 AG. Life expectancy is 79 years, and the median age is 41. The fertility rate has fallen below replacement since 150 AG, and the government’s demographic council has predicted a decline in population from the 190s.

The state religion was abolished in 119 AG. The Fire Sages remain the largest religious body, with about 38 percent of the population, and their Great Sage is one of the country’s most trusted public figures. Sunnic, Air Nomad-inspired and Spirit traditions are growing, and about a quarter of the population describes itself as not religious. Fire Nation Common is the national language, and Old Tajisaki is liturgical. Sunnic is spoken by about two million in the southern chain, and the Eastern Islander dialects are spoken in the resettled districts of the east. Education is free and compulsory to the age of sixteen, and literacy is 99 percent. The universities enroll about 28 percent of each cohort.

Culture

Fire Nation culture is known for its theater, among them the Ember Island troupes and the Caldera Opera, formal gardens, tea ceremonies, calligraphy, festivals and martial arts. The theater is a mass art, and Love amongst the Dragons is performed each year in every large town. The festivals include the Festival of Szeto, the Fire Lily Festivals in August and the traveling Fire Days Festival, and the election day of 2 February is a public holiday. Cuisine is spicy and seafood-based, with noodles, rice, meat and spiced tea. The flag has the circular emblem adopted in Zuko’s reign, a black-and-gold flame within a ring on a red field, and the anthem, Hi no Miyo, was revised in 119 AG to remove its references to the Empire’s destiny.

Popular music has been transformed since the 150s by the genre called N-pop, an urban pop with jazz and city-pop elements, which the labels AZura and Republic have exported to the United Republic. Its best-selling artist in 170 AG is Princess Ayako, the Fire Lord’s younger daughter, who performs as Kiko. The press, which is free, is led by the Calderan Scire, the national daily, and a lively provincial press, and the Diet’s transcripts are printed in full. The Agni Kai, the duel of honor, survives in its regulated form, and the Marine Corps’ annual contest at Port Hana is among the most watched sporting events.

The country’s memory of the war is divided between those who treat it as a national shame and those who treat it as a national tragedy, and public ceremonies on the anniversary of the comet are held in silence. The Day of Ash, on the date of the Sōen strike, is a day of mourning. The civil war’s memorials, among them the Hira Cliffs memorial unveiled in 119 AG, the war cemetery at Iwakura Plain and the memorial park at Joha’s quay, are visited by about nine million people a year. The novelists of the 140s and 150s, among them Itsuki Hanabusa, whose The Ledger of Ash sold three million copies, have made the war a central subject of literature, and the Salvationist movement a literary motif.

Security and the radical movements

The Fire Nation’s internal security is the work of the National Police Agency and the Public Security Bureau, which together employ about 310,000 people, and of the National Guard. Their principal concern in 170 AG is the western cities, where the Thunderbolt sect and the remnants of the Salvationist cells have operated since the late 160s, and the port of Joha, where curfews have covered four of six districts since December 153 AG. The Public Security Bureau’s estimate of the Thunderbolt’s membership, of 3,000 to 5,000, is regarded as high by the Union and low by the Old Guard. The police found a weapons cache in a Joha warehouse in April 154 AG and handbills in the old Salvationist slogans, and Commissioner Rin Katsura said at the time that “someone is doing the digging on purpose.” See Thunderbolt sect and Salvationists.

The government’s policy, set out by Prime Minister Sato in her address of March 170 AG, is to separate the Union’s legal parties from the armed groups, to settle the arrears of the ports and to avoid giving the Old Guard the emergency powers it demands. The policy has been criticized from both sides. The Old Guard says that the Union is a front, and the Union says that the government’s police are creating the enemy that they claim to find. The Concord of Nations, whose members agreed in the Caldera Accord of 121 AG to consult on groups that seek to overthrow a member’s order by force, has begun to ask whether the Union belongs on the list.

Current affairs, 170 AG

Inside the country

The reign of Izumi is in its third year, and the Cabinet of Ryoko Sato governs with a majority in the National Diet. The Coalition and the Old Guard compete over reconstruction, the military budget and the pace of fission power. The economy grows at about 2.8 percent a year. The memory of the war is marked in silence, and the report of the Commission on Imperial Conduct still shapes the debate about the army and the throne. The curfews in Joha and the question of the absent Fire Lord are the two unresolved matters of the reign.

Geopolitical decisions

Paying for the peace: the Fire Nation pays no cash reparations, but funds the Rebuilding Fund for the Earth Kingdom’s occupied provinces and is the largest importer of its grain. A wary partnership with Qianchan: joint research on fission continues beside rivalry in heavy industry. The United Republic: the government wants trade and a common language of commerce with its former colonies, without reopening old grievances, and is watching the Republic City crisis of 170 AG. The Concord: the Fire Nation chairs the preparatory committee for the forum that will meet in Caldera City in September 176.

After 170 AG

The kingdom’s later history is told at History of Tajisaki, 171–190 AG. In summary, the People’s Coalition won the election of February 172 and the Union fell to 62 seats. The Concord of Nations banned the Union’s three parties on 17 March 176 and the Diet’s forty Union members were removed. Coordinated bombings on 12 September 178 led to a snap election in which the National Conservative Party and the Democratic Reform Party took 404 of 466 seats and formed the Reformation government. The Earth Empire’s attack on the kingdom began with the raid on Caldera City of 2–3 February 181 and the occupation of the southern islands from April, and ended, after an atomic missile destroyed the old city on 21 December 182, with the Empire’s collapse. Zuko was killed in an Imperial bombing on 3 January 181. The kingdom was governed from Shinja from 183, and in 190 Prime Minister Daichi Oyama led a Cabinet without the Old Guard. See also Earth Empire–Concord War, Politics of Tajisaki, Political parties of Tajisaki and Elections in Tajisaki.

The Empire of Tajisaki (to 118 AG)

Fire Nation (Empire of Tajisaki)
CapitalCaldera City
GovernmentAbsolute monarchy under the Fire Lord, with an National Diet, a Cabinet and a General Staff Directorate
PopulationAbout {{stat:pop_fn_0|n}} (0 AG); about 172,000,000 (100 AG, before the civil war)
Armed forcesAbout 8,000,000 (80 AG)
Ideology"The Truth": the Fire Lord's sacred authority; the Homeland Purity Initiative
War deadAbout 3,500,000 (Hundred Year War); about 3,500,000 (Fire Nation Civil War)

The Empire of Tajisaki is the Fire Nation as a modern industrial state. It began the Hundred Year War in 0 AG with the Air Nomad Genocide, and by 80 AG was the strongest military power in the world, with the largest industry, a monopoly on chemical weapons, and the world's first aircraft, tanks, jets and power armor. It lost the war because its central authority collapsed when Fire Lord Ozai was killed in 100 AG.

Government of the Empire

The Fire Lord. Under the Imperial Constitution, the Fire Lord rules "in perpetuity" and without limit (Art. 1), is sacred and inviolable (Art. 2), commands the armed forces and alone makes war and peace (Art. 5), and may issue Rescripts and Proclamations that override all other law (Art. 7). The successor is designated by the reigning Fire Lord, and a designation is final. Without one, the Privy Council must meet within 72 hours and the claimant must produce fire at a confirmation ceremony within seven days (Art. 3).

The Diet. The National Diet has two houses, the House of Lords (princes, peers and appointees) and the House of Representatives, which is elected by men who have completed their service (Arts. 20–22). It may legislate and pass the budget, but not investigate military operations, the Ministry of Truth or the Fire Lord (Art. 28), and succession is outside its authority (Art. 25).

The Cabinet. The Prime Minister and a cabinet of ministries (National Enlightenment, Truth, National Harmony, War, the Navy, Aviation, Colonial Affairs and others) serve at the Fire Lord's pleasure. The General Staff Directorate has a separate constitutional position and a right of direct audience with the Fire Lord (Art. 32). The Ministry of Truth runs internal security and is not subject to judicial review (Art. 33).

The empire. Colonial subjects were classified as Recognized Imperial Persons, Enrolled Colonial Subjects, Unenrolled Populations or Designated Threat Populations, and colonial administrators had combined executive, legislative and judicial power (Arts. 42–43). The Homeland Purity Initiative authorized "integration, resettlement and removal" (Art. 44), and Article 45 declared the Air Nomad Question "settled." All adults owed three years of military service, a precondition for voting.

Emergency powers. In a declared emergency, rights are suspended, the Cabinet rules by decree and the Fire Lord may declare martial law (Arts. 46–49). Only the Fire Lord can end an emergency, which in 100 AG left the Empire's emergency powers frozen with no one to lift them.

History of the Empire

The Empire's ruling line, of which Sozin, Azulon and Ozai were the Fire Lords of the war, took the Fire Nation from industrial revolution (290 BG) through the Hundred Year War. After Ozai's death, a rigged succession split it into the Court, the Royalists and the Salvationists, and the Fire Nation Civil War followed. Zuko's Royalists won in 118 AG, and the Empire became the Fire Nation of his reign.
