The Qianchan Republic is the federal republic of the southern earth lands. It is in effect the southern province of the Earth Kingdom that broke away, and it was born out of war. Its founder in spirit was Qin the Great, a lord of Gaoling who set out to reform Ba Sing Se's absolute authority, with the Avatar Kyoshi, the King of Omashu and the Lord of Yu Dao behind him, and who was killed outside the capital in 270 BG, in a duel in which the Earth King cheated. His death did not end the movement. The southern earth lands rose against his heirs' enemies in the War of Liberation, many Earth Kingdom soldiers defected, and the republic's independence was recognized in 255 BG.

It is an industrial state with a citizen-militia tradition, a federal system, a strong navy and armored forces, and a politics that Ba Sing Se has never accepted as legitimate. Its citizens call themselves the "Fifth Nation," a name that began as a taunt from the kingdom's court and was adopted by the republic's printers and veterans. It was the only state in the world, besides the Fire Nation, that could build what the other could build, and for that reason it sits at the center of the Empire's case for the Hundred Year War.

Origins

The land and the old grievance

The south of the Earth Kingdom was always a different country from the capital. Its provinces were wetter, richer in coal and iron, closer to the sea, and farther from the Inner City. Under the kings of Ba Sing Se they paid the same tribute as the north and received less protection, and the memory of the Yellow Neck Uprising (312–305 BG), in which the capital put down a peasant rebellion with little regard for the provinces that bore the cost, was not forgotten. The south's lords, merchants and farm assemblies shared a view that the kingdom existed for its capital. Qin was the first man to make that view an army.

Qin and the coalition

Qin came out of Gaoling as a reformer rather than a rebel. His program was to limit the Earth King's authority, regularize provincial taxation and make the kingdom's armies answerable to something other than the palace. He built a coalition of provincial lords, the King of Omashu and the Lord of Yu Dao, and with the support of the Avatar Kyoshi he marched on Ba Sing Se. He was killed outside the capital in 270 BG, in the duel that Ba Sing Se's court says it won and the south says it stole. The southern army walked home carrying his body, and it did not disband.

The Southern Army

The formation that fought the War of Liberation is usually called the Southern Army. It was assembled from Qin's surviving regiments, from Earth Kingdom units that deserted the capital's service, and from village militias that had armed themselves in the first years of the rising. It had no single commander. Authority was held by a collective command council of senior officers and delegates, which for fifteen years governed the territory it held, collected taxes, appointed administrators and issued decrees. This is the origin of two traits that the republic never lost: its distrust of any one person holding a sword and a treasury at once, and its habit of settling hard questions by committee.

The War of Liberation (270–255 BG)

The war lasted fifteen years and was fought over the southern provinces, the roads to the capital and the grain that moved on them. It was not a single campaign. The Earth Kingdom's armies were larger and held the walls of Ba Sing Se, but they were unreliable in the south, where entire units defected to the Southern Army once it was clear that the capital was not paying them. The republic's later image of itself as an army of citizens begins here: a militia that had won because its soldiers owned the fields they fought on.

The southern forces took the coalfields and the river ports first. In 255 BG the capital, weakened by the first of two peasant uprisings inside Ba Sing Se itself, accepted a settlement that recognized the south's independence. The Southern Army's command council signed for the south. The Earth King signed, but the kingdom's court never wrote the word "republic" into any document, and so the republic's legal standing has been disputed in Ba Sing Se ever since.

The founding of the republic

The republic was not proclaimed in a day. The process had four stages:

  1. The provisional council (270–262 BG). The Southern Army's officers governed alone. The council was effective but narrow, and it ruled by decree.
  2. Pressure from below (c. 262–258 BG). Peasant organizations demanded that the land they had won be theirs by law. Merchants, who paid for much of the war, demanded a currency and courts they could trust. Both groups pressed the council to include them or lose them.
  3. The conventions (258–255 BG). A series of district conventions elected delegates who drafted a constitution: a legislature of districts, a civilian executive, regular taxation, and an army placed under civilian authority.
  4. The settlement of 255 BG. The treaty with Ba Sing Se ended the war. The republic's first President took office the same year, and the council dissolved itself.

The date of the republic's founding is therefore debated in its own histories. The Qianchan state marks 255 BG, the treaty year. Constitutional scholars point instead to the last convention, a year or two earlier, and a few nationalists to the first council in 270 BG. Ba Sing Se, for its part, marks nothing, and refers to the period as "the secession."

The Qin house

Qin's family survived him. In the republic it became a political house rather than a dynasty: it kept its estates and its wealth, held seats in the legislature, and for several generations supplied officers and administrators. Its members were often the republic's most conservative voices and sometimes its most nostalgic, and there was friction between the house and the republicans who thought that no family should be remembered as the republic's owner. The house never made a claim to rule, and it was a condition of the constitutional settlement that it would not. In Ba Sing Se, the Qin house is remembered as a pretender line. In Gaoling, it is remembered as a family that was, on the whole, content to be honored.

Government

The republic is a federal republic with a President and a bicameral legislature, the Parliament, in Gaoling.

The federal system was strengthened in the Hundred Year War as a precaution against invasion: a republic whose provinces could govern themselves could survive the loss of its capital. This was a lesson taken, in part, from the fall of Ba Sing Se's centralized bureaucracy under pressure in earlier centuries. Both the Earth Kingdom's historians and Qianchan's treat it as the republic's most important constitutional choice.

Law and society

The republic recognizes its citizens' right to keep and bear arms in a citizen militia, a tradition that predates the constitution and that the army treats as a reserve. Every adult citizen is expected to have served in or trained with the militia, which in peace is a social institution and in war is the republic's second army. The press is free in law and often rowdy in practice. Churches and temples are not established. The state does not require loyalty oaths, a fact that its officials point to when criticizing the Empire's.

The formal names, terms, powers and the Constitutional Court are on Federal legislature of Qianchan. In the constitution the Parliament is the National Congress, its Chamber of Districts is the House of Representatives, and its Senate of the States is the Federal Council.

Politics and factions

The republic's politics are noisy, fragmented and coalitional. No party has governed alone for long. The main currents are described below in general terms; their names and fortunes have shifted across the centuries.

This fragmentation is both a strength and a weakness. It prevented any military faction from seizing the state, and it made the republic slow to commit to a long war. In the decades before 0 AG, its governments often fell over the question of how much to spend on rearmament, and the Fire Nation's planners counted this slowness among the republic's weaknesses.

Economy and technology

Qianchan's economy grew from coal, iron, river transport and a merchant class that had paid for a war and expected a return. Its engineers adopted coal-fired engines in 255 BG, the year of independence, and by the century before the Hundred Year War its railways, ports and mills were among the largest in the world. Its universities, centered on the Academy of Gaoling, trained engineers, chemists and physicists in numbers the Earth Kingdom could not match. The repeater, a rifle that fires multiple rounds without reloading by hand, was in service by 130 BG.

From 26 BG the republic and the Fire Nation were in a recognizable technology race. Each had a steel industry, a railway network and a research establishment, and each watched the other's patents, ship launches and exhibitions. The Empire's Imperial Research Bureau kept a department solely for Qianchan intelligence. In the republic, the Academy's journals, which printed freely, were a source the Fire Nation read closely. The race ended the Fire Nation's lead in mechanical engineering and, according to its own staff, narrowed it in chemistry and explosives.

Relations with the Earth Kingdom and the Dai Li

Ba Sing Se fought two suppression campaigns against the republic, in 240 BG and 225 BG. Both failed. The Preliminary Accord of 224 BG set a boundary but did not recognize the republic, which is why the kingdom's court has been able to claim for two centuries that it never conceded anything. To stop republican ideas from spreading north, the kingdom founded the Dai Li around 215 BG, and the republic has regarded it since as the kingdom's secret police. Dai Li agents operated in the southern provinces and the republic's border towns and, in turn, Qianchan's own services learned to watch them.

For two centuries the Long Cold Peace was a relationship of trade and hostility. Goods moved across the border; so did smugglers, spies and the occasional defector. When reformers in the Earth Kingdom asked Qianchan for help, the republic refused, and its answer, "we govern ourselves; we do not export governance," became a formal policy. It had two reasons for it. The first was principle: a republic that exports itself by force is an empire. The second was prudence: any support for rebels in the north would give Ba Sing Se the pretext it wanted for a third war.

The road to the Alliance

As the Fire Nation rearmed after 37 BG, the republic and the kingdom had to decide whether their quarrel mattered more than their danger. Both knew by the 20s BG that the Empire was building the largest army and fleet in its history. Both read the same warnings and drew different conclusions. Ba Sing Se believed that the Empire would think twice about an attack on the walls. Qianchan believed that the Empire would not.

The Alliance Treaty of 3 BG

The Alliance Treaty of 3 BG was a pact of mutual defense between the Earth Kingdom and Qianchan. The republic signed it only on condition that Ba Sing Se revise its language of non-recognition: the treaty's text refers to the republic by name, which the kingdom's court had never done. Even so, the treaty did not create a joint command, a shared intelligence service or a plan for who would defend what. The two powers could not agree on any of them without recognizing one another's authority. The result was a deterrent in form rather than substance, and the Empire's staff knew it.

The republic's own diplomats offered alternatives in the years before the war, among them a standing combined staff, a standardized railway gauge to the border and a naval convention with the Northern Water Tribe. The kingdom accepted none of them. In Gaoling, the failure of those proposals is remembered as the lost chance of the age.

Why the Empire attacked

The republic's historians do not accept that the Hundred Year War was inevitable. They argue that the Empire chose it, and that it chose it for reasons it believed were practical. They set out the reasons as follows.

  • Energy. The Fire Nation's own forecasts, commissioned by the Imperial Research Bureau, gave its domestic oil about a century. The only large oilfield in the world's reach lay in the Si Wong Desert, inside the Earth Kingdom. Qianchan's coal industry, by contrast, was secure, and its engineers were working on alternatives.
  • A rival that would not stay behind. The republic matched the Empire in steel, rail, shipbuilding and, by the 20s BG, in the sciences. The Empire's planners calculated that the Fire Nation's lead would not survive another generation of Qianchan growth, and that a war later would be harder than a war now.
  • The Avatar. The Avatar Roku had spared Sozin in 37 BG, and was the one person the Empire could not intimidate. Sozin left Roku to die in 12 BG, and the next Avatar would be born among the Air Nomads. The republic's analysts concluded, after the war, that the Empire had calculated its attack to fall in the gap before a new Avatar could be found and trained.
  • A hollow Diet. The National Diet could not investigate the Fire Lord, the military or the Ministry of Truth, which meant that no one inside the Empire could stop the decision.

The republic's own analysts note that the Empire's case for necessity was built on assumptions it did not test: that the oil could not be bought, that the republic would not respond, and that the war could be won in a few years. The first assumption was never tested because the Empire's staff never asked. The republic had offered, in the late 20s BG, to discuss an oil-sharing arrangement through neutral brokers. The offer went unanswered.

In the Hundred Year War

Qianchan entered the war in 30 AG, after one of its civilian ships was sunk in 27 AG and a naval battle with the Imperial Navy was a draw. It supplied Omashu by sea after the southern front was cut off, helped the Earth Kingdom industrialize, taught it desert warfare, and fought a submarine war against Imperial shipping. In the Siege of Ba Sing Se, it refused to commit troops until King Kuei was evacuated, and kept its whole air force on the Omashu front. It evacuated the Northern Water Tribe's leaders by submarine in 99 AG.

Its war cost about 1,090,000 lives. Its armed forces reached about 4,500,000 by 80 AG. Its population, which was about {{stat:pop_qc_0|n}} at the war's start, was about {{stat:pop_qc_100|n}} by 100 AG, an increase which its demographers attribute in part to refugees from the Earth Kingdom.

History since 100 AG

The history of the republic before the end of the Hundred Year War is told above and at History of Qianchan. This section follows the republic through the seven decades that followed, in which it became the largest economy in the world, fought its only foreign expedition since the Hundred Year War, helped found two new states and watched the radical movements of the 160s arrive at its own coasts.

The settlement of the war (100–113 AG)

Qianchan emerged from the Hundred Year War as the one great power that had never been invaded. It had lost about 1,090,000 people, its fleet had been worn down by seventy years of submarine war, and its coastal cities had been bombed, but its factories, its railways and its universities were intact. The Federal Council, meeting in Gaoling on 4 August 100 AG, three weeks after Ozai’s death, resolved on three policies that were to govern the republic’s conduct for the next decade. It would help end the warlord wars that followed the collapse of the Earth Kingdom’s authority, in company with Omashu and Ba Sing Se, under the Ba Sing Se Treaty that had placed the allied armies under one command in 100 AG. It would supply the Yanakawan rebels with surplus weapons and the new republic they proposed with recognition. And it would stay out of the Fire Nation’s succession, while preventing the Empire’s armies from reaching the sea.

The warlord wars, which the republic helped to end by 112 AG, were fought largely by Qianchan’s mobile columns, which moved by rail and river from Gaoling, and by the diplomats of the Academy’s Institute of Strategic Studies, who negotiated the surrender of the larger warlords one by one. The method was not generous. The Federal Council paid for the pacification by a levy on the member states, and Qianchan officers set up garrisons in about forty Earth Kingdom towns, most of which they handed back to Ba Sing Se after 113 AG. The republic’s influence in the former kingdom was never greater than in these years, and it was never so resented.

The island chains and the Royalists (101–118 AG)

The republic’s conduct in the Fire Nation Civil War was the most consequential decision of its postwar history. After the Sōen strike and Ozai’s death, the National Congress saw a choice between abstaining and backing the Royalists, and decided in the autumn of 100 AG, by 288 votes to 152 in the House, to accept Zuko’s government’s request that a Qianchan garrison hold the Southern Air Temple island chain, which the Empire had left with a skeleton garrison by 99 AG, and to use it as a base for supplying the Restoration Government. The chain, which Qianchan had shared with the Empire since 50 AG and now held alone, became the Royalists’ rear area. Grain, fuel, spare parts and surplus rifles passed through it by sea to the Fire Nation’s south and west, and the republic’s engineers rebuilt the airfields that the airbender survivors had abandoned. The garrison’s defense of the chain against the Court’s landing of September 104 AG was the republic’s first direct fight with the Court, and its army, which had been prepared for a defensive war, took no part in the fighting on the Fire Nation’s mainland until 110. See Southern Air Temple Landing.

The decision to send an expeditionary corps was taken in 109 AG, after the Court’s landing and the naval battles that followed it persuaded the Congress that the Royalists could not win alone. The corps, built around the 2nd Expeditionary Division and under General Han Zhiyuan, an engineer, reached the front at Shu Jing in the spring of 110. It fought at Iwakura Plain, where its mine belts and anti-armor teams destroyed the Court’s breakthrough column and where about 5,000 of its soldiers died, among them Sergeant Wu Lian, whom the republic remembers as the gunner of the river road. The Congress extended the corps’ mandate in July 110 by a vote of 301 to 140. The republic also supplied the naval squadron of two frigates and four patrol boats under Commodore Zhou Yilan that took part in the blockade of Hira in 111–112, and three relief ships that brought 1,500 tons of flour and about forty doctors, under Dr. Lin Wei, to the starving city in April 112. The mission’s report, read in the Congress in June 112, was the first full account of the famine to reach the world, and it is the republic’s proudest humanitarian record. See Siege of Hira.

The republic’s conduct was not uncontroversial. The Veterans’ Union, which had pressed for the intervention, wanted the Royalists to be told that Qianchan expected a military convention. The Agrarian Assemblies, who paid the levies, wanted the corps withdrawn after Iwakura, and the Federal Union, which defended the states’ autonomy, objected to the use of state militias in a foreign war. The cost of the intervention was about 31,000 dead, of whom about 22,000 were killed in action, and about 3.1 billion kuan. After the armistice of 13 August 118 the republic withdrew the corps in the autumn, withdrew its garrisons from the Fire Nation’s southern waters under the terms of the Caldera Accord, and in 120 AG, when the Southern Air Temple chain left its direct control, constituted the islands as an autonomous district for the airbenders within the republic.

The Caldera Accord and the Concord (118–131 AG)

The republic and the Fire Nation were the sponsors of the Caldera Accord of 121 AG and of the Concord of Nations that it founded. Qianchan’s principal contribution was institutional: its diplomats drafted most of the Concord’s technical statutes, its Academy supplied the first staff of the Concord’s relief agency, and its Federal Bureau of Statistics produced the first common accounts of the war’s dead. The republic’s policy, set out by President Tan Meifeng in her address of that year, was that the Concord should be “a table, not a government,” a phrase that has remained the republic’s position on its powers. The seat reserved for the Earth Kingdom was left vacant because Ba Sing Se declined to sit with the republic until the Treaty of Gaoling of 113 AG was ratified by the Earth Council, which it was only in 124.

The Treaty of Gaoling itself, signed on 6 May 113 AG, was the settlement that the republic had waited three hundred years for. It was the first document signed in Ba Sing Se that wrote the word “republic.” Its terms fixed the border at the line of 224 BG, returned the Earth Kingdom towns that the republic’s garrisons had held, recognized the Alliance Treaty of 3 BG as the basis of mutual defense, and established a joint commission on the border’s trade. The Earth Kingdom’s court, which regarded it as a surrender, signed because the warlord wars had exhausted the treasury. In Gaoling, the treaty was celebrated for a week.

The sponsor of the republics (102–131 AG)

Qianchan was the principal sponsor of the United Republic of Nations, whose Declaration of Union of 102 AG and recognition by the Treaty of Qinglan in 105 AG owed much to the republic’s arms and its diplomats. The republic’s constitution of 94 AG, with its federal structure and its militia, was the model that the Founding Congress studied, and the republic’s advisers helped the Republic’s first Council to draft its charter. Qianchan sent about 3,000 advisers to Republic City between 102 and 112 AG, loaned the Republic 800 million kuan in 104, and kept a small naval mission at Yu Dao until 125. The relationship has been warm and, in the Republic’s politics, resented: the Nationalist Union’s speakers call the Republic a client state, and the Servants of the Republic point to the loan, which was repaid in 131 AG.

The exiles of the Salvationist movement, who fled the Fire Nation in 120 AG, were received in the republic’s southern island chain, where the Federal Council allowed about 40,000 of them to settle on condition that they refrain from political activity. They have not always done so. The exiles’ presses, which print in the old committee style, are a source of embarrassment to the Cabinet, and the Fire Nation’s Public Security Bureau has asked repeatedly for their extradition. The republic’s answer has been that the exiles are guests, and that the Fire Nation’s amnesty of 120 AG covers them.

The age of Tieshan and the Academy (125–155 AG)

The republic’s fission program, Tieshan, which had run in parallel to the Empire’s during the war, produced its first civilian reactor at Port Tieshan in 125 AG. The program was placed under the Ministry of Energy in 127 and was by 150 supplying about a quarter of the republic’s electricity, from fourteen reactors in six states. The weapon question was never closed. The republic’s scientists, among them the physicist Dr. Shen Yaoting, told the Federal Council in 138 that the republic could build a weapon in about three years if ordered to, and the Council voted in 139, by a margin of one, against ordering it. The vote has been the republic’s policy ever since, and the Concord has asked for it to be written into a treaty.

The period was also one of unprecedented growth. The republic’s output rose by about 2.7 percent a year between 125 and 155, and its prosperity drew millions of workers from the Earth Kingdom and the Fire Nation. The Academy of Gaoling enrolled about 80,000 students by 150, and its journals, printed freely, became the principal source for the world’s economists and physicists. The republic’s great engineering works, among them the Grand Canal, which linked the southern river system to the eastern coast in 141 AG, the second harbor at Port Tieshan and the transcontinental railway to Zaofu, which opened in 147, were funded by the Federal Council’s development bank.

Zaofu and the Red Lotus (156 AG)

In about 156 AG a Red Lotus cell bombed a residential building in the Heritage District of Zaofu in an attempt to steal the Iron Guard’s research. The cell, which included a young man later known as Zaheer, escaped with an uncertain quantity of drawings. The dead included the parents of an eight-year-old girl from Omashu, Kuvira, whom Suyin Beifong, the head of the Beifong family and governor of Zaofu, adopted and raised in her house. The attack led the Federal Council to pass the Security of Research Act of 157 AG, which brought the autonomous region’s military research under federal inspection, a measure that Zaofu resisted and that Suyin has called an insult. See Zaofu Heritage District bombing.

The 160s (160–170 AG)

The republic’s politics in the 160s were a series of short cabinets. The Veterans’ Union’s leader, General Kang Haoran, led a minority government from 160 to 162 that fell on a vote over the military budget, and the Federal Union’s Wen Tianyu led a cabinet of four parties from 162 to 166. In April 166 the Parliament elected Liu Jiahui of the Commerce and Industry Party to the presidency, the first woman from the industrial coast to hold the office, at the head of a coalition of her party, the Federal Union and the Agrarian Assemblies. She was re-elected in April 170 after the federal election of March.

The Cabinet’s concern in the later 160s was the unrest that began in the United Republic and the Earth Kingdom in 167 AG. The republic’s intelligence service, the Federal Security Office, reported that the Equalists of Republic City were drawing on exiles from the Salvationist movement, and the republic’s own press, the most outspoken in the world, was divided on whether the radical movements were a threat to order or a protest against it. The Congress’s debate on the United Republic’s proposed constitutional reform, which was modeled on Qianchan’s presidential system, was held in August 170 and is remembered for a speech by the Federal Union’s Lan Shuyi, who said that “a republic is a way of keeping a promise, and no one should borrow ours who has not seen what it costs.”

Country profile, 170 AG

The figures in this section describe the Qianchan Republic in 170 AG. They are published by the Federal Bureau of Statistics, whose numbers are generally regarded as the most reliable in the world, and by the Academy of Gaoling, whose economists are regarded as the most critical.

Names

Qianchan was the name of the southern lands in the old kingdom, and the republic kept it. The word is old and its meaning is disputed: “thousand fields” in the common etymology, “the thousand-fold” or “many-voiced” in the republic’s own schoolbooks, which prefer the second. Its citizens are Qianchanese, and some of them still use Fifth Nation, a title that began as an insult from Ba Sing Se and was adopted, with the Yakuya Confederation’s eastern heritage, by the republic’s printers. The formal name in the Charter is the Republic of Qianchan (Qianchan Minguo). See History of Qianchan and Yakuya Confederation.

Geography

Qianchan occupies the southern and south-eastern earth lands, and is the most varied country on the continent: fertile river plains, rolling coalfields, the iron hills of the east, the wetlands of the delta and a long coastline on the southern and eastern seas. It is the largest state in area, at 30.8 million square kilometers, and the most thinly peopled of the great powers, at 8.7 inhabitants to the square kilometer, though about two thirds of its people live within 200 kilometers of the sea. The climate is temperate to subtropical. Its great cities are Gaoling, the capital, Port Tieshan, Zaofu, home of the Beifong metalbenders, and the eastern harbors that were once Yakuya bases. The Charter defines the national territory as the Qianchan Archipelago and the Zaofu Peninsula, and it has a long land border with the Earth Kingdom, which it has not defended against anyone since 224 BG. The Grand Canal, opened in 141 AG, links the river system of the south to the eastern coast.

Government and politics

Qianchan is a federal parliamentary republic with an executive President. The constitution is the Constitutional Charter, in its consolidated edition of 94 AG as amended, whose Article I declares the territory one and indivisible and whose Paramount Obligations of Citizenship are mandatory military service and the right to bear arms. The legislature is the National Congress, known in common use as the Parliament, and sits in Gaoling. It has two chambers. The lower house, the House of Representatives or Chamber of Districts, has 480 members elected by population for four years, with 241 seats a majority, and may be dissolved. The upper house, the Federal Council or Senate of the States, has 24 members, one from each of the twenty-four states, elected or appointed as each state decides for six-year terms, with a third renewed every two years; the autonomous regions of Zaofu and the Southern Air Temple district send non-voting delegates. It cannot be dissolved and can block any bill that violates the states’ constitutional autonomy.

The President, who is elected by the Parliament in joint session, holds executive power with a Federal Cabinet and is commander-in-chief in war, though the army answers to the legislature on funding and to the courts on discipline. The two titles of each chamber, the Charter’s and the press’s, are the result of the Fourth Amendment of 128 AG, which gave the Congress its modern names while leaving the common ones in use. The courts are independent. The Supreme Court hears ordinary appeals, and the Constitutional Court settles disputes between the federal government and the states and reviews federal law against the Charter.

The federal election of 14 March 170 AG returned a House in which no party was close to a majority. The Commerce and Industry Party, the party of the industrial coast, the ports and the Academy’s economists, won 132 seats. The Veterans’ Union, heir of the Southern Army and the militia associations, won 118. The Agrarian Assemblies won 96, the Federal Union, the party of the states and of regional rule-making, 84, and the allies of the Qin house, a loose group of old officer families and southern estates, 18. Independents and local lists took the remaining 32. The Parliament re-elected President Liu Jiahui on 9 April, with the votes of the Commerce and Industry Party, the Federal Union and the Agrarian Assemblies, a coalition of 312 against the Veterans’ Union’s 118 and the Qin allies.

No party has governed alone in the republic’s modern history, and cabinets are replaced regularly, a source of frustration and, its supporters say, of stability. The divisions are those of the earlier centuries: defense against restraint, commerce against land, the center against the states. The Veterans’ Union’s leader in 170 AG is General Kang Haoran, who has campaigned for a military convention with the Earth Kingdom and for a larger budget, and the Agrarian Assemblies’ is Gu Rongfang, who has opposed both. Press freedom is protected by law, and the republic’s papers are among the most outspoken in the world.

Foreign relations

The republic’s policy remains “we govern ourselves; we do not export governance.” It is the Earth Kingdom’s treaty ally under the Alliance Treaty of 3 BG and the Treaty of Gaoling of 113 AG, and it keeps a standing joint commission with Ba Sing Se on the border’s trade. Relations with Queen Hou-Ting’s court are correct, and the Cabinet has been careful not to comment on her reversal of King Kuei’s reforms. The Fire Nation is its partner in research and rival in industry, and the two are the Concord of Nations’ founders and its largest contributors. The republic is the principal sponsor of the United Republic of Nations, whose independence it helped win, and it has given the Republic’s Council advice on the design of its constitutional reform. It keeps close ties with the Southern Water Tribe, which it armed in the Hundred Year War, and with the airbenders of the Southern Air Temple chain.

The republic’s relations with the Water Tribes are tested by the split that begins in 170 AG, when the unrest of the Northern Water Tribe’s poor reaches the Southern Tribe’s ports. Its relations with the Si Wong Desert’s sandbenders and the oil company that holds the fields are commercial, and it is the largest buyer of Si Wong oil after the Fire Nation. The republic is a founder of the Concord, and in the Concord’s committee on security it has opposed any article that would require members to exchange information on political parties, arguing that “a state that watches its parties is no longer a republic.”

Military

Qianchan maintains about 600,000 active personnel and a militia in which every adult citizen is expected to have trained: the Charter requires every citizen to register at 18 and to serve at least 24 months before 25, a 12-month foundation phase and then further training in the reserve. The Army is built on engineering and armor, with about 1,100 tanks and the mine and anti-armor doctrine that proved itself at Iwakura Plain. The Navy is built on submarines, and the Air Force on the aircraft that fought on the Omashu front. The Zaofu Iron Guard is the best-known elite unit, with its Tiejia-III power armor and QR-7 rifles. The republic’s civilian fission program, Tieshan, supplies about a quarter of its electricity, and its capacity for a weapon, which the Council has declined to exercise since 139 AG, has been a subject of treaty negotiation with the Concord. Civilian control of the armed forces is strict. The defense budget is about 2.3 percent of output.

Economy

Qianchan has the largest economy in the world, with a nominal output of {{stat:gdp_qc_170}} and {{stat:gdppc_qc_170}} a person. It is a mixed economy with a high level of private enterprise and one of the most extensive railway, port and power networks on earth. Its leading sectors are machinery, electronics, chemicals, steel, shipbuilding, finance and agricultural exports, and services employ about 54 percent of the workforce. It has a long tradition of cooperatives and of regulated markets, and its high wages and widely shared prosperity have drawn millions of workers from the Earth Kingdom and the Fire Nation. The Gini coefficient was 31.4 in 168 AG. The currency is the kuan, issued by the Bank of Gaoling, and the Gaoling Exchange is the world’s largest by capitalization. The republic’s development bank, the Federal Council’s principal instrument for large projects, has financed the Grand Canal, the harbor at Port Tieshan and the railway to Zaofu.

Science and technology

The Academy of Gaoling is the world’s leading university, with about 80,000 students, and its journals, printed freely, have been a source for every state’s intelligence services since 26 BG. Qianchan leads in electronics, fission engineering, metallurgy, medicine and metalbending technology. It built the repeater (130 BG), coal engines (255 BG) and many of the technologies that the Earth Kingdom’s 23 AG industrialization used. The Gaoling Press Cooperative, founded by twelve photographers in 87 AG, is the world’s photographer-owned cooperative and holds the most comprehensive visual record of the Hundred Year War.

Zaofu and the autonomous regions

Two of the republic’s regions are autonomous. Zaofu, the city and region of the Beifong family on the peninsula, is governed by Suyin Beifong, head of the family, and writes its own rules on police, education and land. It is the home of metalbending and of the Iron Guard, whose metalbenders are restricted to trained personnel, and it was the site of the Heritage District bombing of 156 AG. Zaofu’s autonomy is guaranteed by the Charter and resented by some in the Veterans’ Union, who regard the Security of Research Act of 157 as insufficient. The Southern Air Temple district, the island chain that Qianchan held until 120 AG, whose port is Shiza, is the autonomous district of the airbenders, who govern it through a council of elders and keep the temple’s terraces as a place of pilgrimage.

Demographics

Qianchan has about 268 million inhabitants, a figure that includes millions of Earth Kingdom war refugees and their descendants, and its population grew from about 207 million in 100 AG. The language of administration is Qianchan Common. Zaofu Cant, a metalbenders’ dialect, and eastern coastal speech, descended from the Yakuya Confederation’s creole, are also widely spoken, and the Salvationist exiles in the southern islands speak Fire Nation Common among themselves. The republic is secular in law, with a mixed religious life of ancestor veneration, Spirit traditions and a number of modern movements. Literacy is almost universal, and the median age is 38. About 41 percent of the population is of the original Qianchan stock, about 27 percent of Earth Kingdom descent, about 9 percent of the eastern coastal heritage, and the remainder of mixed or foreign descent.

Culture

Qianchan’s culture is urban, argumentative and proud of its institutions. It is known for its press, cafés, theater, mechanical engineering, cooking and a strong tradition of debate. The memory of Qin the Great is cherished in the south, and the Academy’s historians are noted for writing candidly about the republic’s own record. The citizen militia is also a social institution: each district holds an annual muster that is part parade, part picnic. The republic’s great public holidays are Founding Day on the anniversary of the treaty of 255 BG, the Day of Charter on the day the consolidated Charter was ratified in 94 AG, and the Iwakura Day on 12 June, when the gunner of the river road is remembered in her street in the capital.

Current affairs, 170 AG

Inside the republic

The government of President Liu Jiahui holds 312 of 480 seats in the House, after the election of March, in a coalition of the Commerce and Industry Party, the Federal Union and the Agrarian Assemblies. The Veterans’ Union leads the opposition. The republic’s output is about {{stat:gdp_qc_170}} ({{stat:gdppc_qc_170}} a person), with about {{stat:pop_qc_170|m}} people. The Tieshan program supplies a quarter of the electricity, and its capacity for a weapon is a subject of treaty negotiation. The Salvationist exiles in the southern islands, about 40,000 in all, are watched by the Federal Security Office, and their presses are a standing subject of correspondence with the Fire Nation.

Geopolitical decisions

Governing itself: the policy of non-export is maintained. It is the Earth Kingdom’s treaty ally and the Fire Nation’s partner in research and rival in industry. The United Republic: Qianchan is the principal sponsor of the Republic and is following the Republic City crisis of 170 AG closely. The Southern Water Tribe: Qianchan’s close ties to the South, which it armed in the war, will be tested by the split that begins in 170 AG.

After 170 AG

The wiki records the later history of the republic in separate articles. The Gaoling Exchange fell less than the Earth Kingdom’s in the crash of June 171, and the Qianchan note rose 4 percent against Earth Kingdom paper (Market crashes of 153 and 171 AG). The republic joined the Concord’s ban on the Equalist Party and its sister parties in 176 AG. It declared war on the Earth Empire by 25 December 180, was struck in Zaofu and Gaoling, and its Federal Council voted by two thirds against surrender in December 182 (Earth Empire–Concord War). Its politics are in Politics of Qianchan and Elections in Qianchan.

northern_water_tribe.title: Northern Water Tribe
northern_water_tribe.html:
The larger of the two Water Tribes, centered on Agna Qel'a. Later the Kingdom of Agna Qel'a.

Northern Water Tribe
Capital[[Agna Qel'a]]
PopulationAbout 3,600,000 (0 AG); about 1,800,000 (July 100 AG)
MilitaryA small elite army of riflemen and waterbenders; no navy or air force after 0 AG
War deadAbout 1,800,000

The Northern Water Tribe is the Water Tribe state of the North Pole, a centralized nation under a Chief and a Council of Elders, with ice-walled cities and a navy that the Empire destroyed in the first weeks of the Hundred Year War. It was historically the stronger of the two tribes, and until 40 AG remained in contact with the South.

In the Hundred Year War

The North beat back the Empire in the First Battle of Agna Qel'a (0 AG) with the weather, ice and waterbending, and was bombed periodically for the next century from the Empire's base on the far eastern pole, losing about 20% of its people by 40 AG. In the Siege of the North (13 November – 19 December 99 AG) the Empire took Agna Qel'a, with about 800,000 dead in five weeks. The Chief and most of the Council escaped on Qianchan submarines, and the occupation and scorched-earth policy cut the population to 50% by June 100 AG.

Later history

The North's unity with the South ended in the civil war of 170–174 AG, and it became the Kingdom of Agna Qel'a.

southern_water_tribe.title: Southern Water Tribe
southern_water_tribe.html:
The smaller of the two Water Tribes, a federation of chiefdoms at the South Pole. Occupied by the Empire for ninety-nine years.

Southern Water Tribe
CapitalTaluqqriaq (Wolf Cove)
GovernmentFederation of chiefdoms under a Council of Chieftains and Elders
PopulationAbout {{stat:pop_swt_0|n}} (0 AG); about {{stat:pop_swt_100|n}} (end of the war)
War deadAbout 70% of the population dead or missing

The Southern Water Tribe was the more egalitarian and the weaker of the two tribes, with ice-walled towns and many skilled waterbenders. It was the target of the Empire's most prolonged campaign of subjugation, which began a week after the Air Nomad Genocide.

Occupation and insurgency

The Empire captured the leaders in 0 AG and forced them to cooperate, and ran an occupation of forced labor, reprisals and terror. The Southern insurgency raided Imperial convoys and industry for forty years. The last of the early uprisings (29 AG) left the South at 75% of its pre-war population, and by 99 AG, when the waterbenders had dwindled to a handful, it was about 50%. The Southern Uprising of 99 AG was crushed, and many survivors were conscripted or sent to work in the colonies. By the end of the war about 70% of the pre-war population was dead or missing.

Leaders

Chief Hakoda led the Southern resistance in 99 AG. The capital's name, Taluqqriaq, is the Water Tribe name for Wolf Cove, "the wolf cave."

air_nomads.title: Air Nomads
air_nomads.html:
A pacifist, stateless people of the four Air Temples, destroyed in the Air Nomad Genocide.

Air Nomads
HomelandThe four Air Temples and their island chains and mountains, with communities across the world
PopulationAbout {{stat:pop_an_0|n}} (0 AG)
FateAlmost entirely killed, 0–20 AG
SurvivorsAbout 300–400 people with airbending in 99 AG, deep in Qianchan or the Earth Kingdom

The Air Nomads were a pacifist people without a state or army, who lived in the four Air Temples and in communities across the Earth Kingdom, the Water Tribe lands and the Yanakawan coast. Most were non-benders. The Empire of Tajisaki, which wanted to stop the next Avatar from being born among them, destroyed them in the Air Nomad Genocide. The Imperial Constitution declared that the Air Nomads "ceased to constitute a distinct people" and prohibited their bending and spiritual practices (Art. 45).

The only known airbender in public was the Avatar, Aang. The several hundred surviving airbenders mostly did not know what they were, or hid it. After the war, Qianchan preserved the Southern Air Temple and gave the airbenders autonomy.

The Sonam legend, 118 AG

In 118 AG the Air Nomads were found to have an older history than the wiki had recorded. Sonam, a forgotten Avatar, is said to have led Air Nomad peace-keepers from the city of Jharana in a war with the Earth Kingdom (see Air Nomad–Earth Kingdom war). Her pupil Tagah wanted to make an armed Air Nomad state of it, and in 118 AG he burned Republic City with the Denied before Aang broke Sonam's Staff. The Earth Kingdom has no record of the war.

United Republic of Nations
Country profile, 170 AG

The United Republic of Nations, commonly known as the United Republics, is a council republic on the Yanakawan Peninsula, declared in 102 AG, and recognized in 105 AG, from the Fire Nation's former colonies. In 170 AG it is the third-largest economy in the world and the most cosmopolitan state in it, with {{stat:urn_fb_share}} of its people born abroad.

Current affairs, 170 AG

Inside the republic

  • The representation dispute. The Republic Council has six seats: one each for Fire, Earth and Air, two for Water (the Northern and Southern Tribes) and one for Non-Benders. Earth benders are {{stat:urn_bp_earth}} of the population but hold one seat in six. Non-benders ({{stat:urn_bp_non}}) hold one, and the {{stat:urn_b_air|n}} air benders hold one. The Progressives want seats weighted by population, while the Servants of the Republic defend the founding settlement that gave every people a seat.
  • A republic of newcomers. {{stat:urn_fb_total|n}} residents, {{stat:urn_fb_share}} of the population, were born abroad, and {{stat:urn_imm_total}} people have immigrated since 0 AG. Citizenship, language and housing for newcomers dominate debate in the National Assembly.
  • Growth strain. The population roughly doubled from {{stat:pop_urn_125|m}} in 125 AG to about {{stat:pop_urn_170|m}} in 170 AG, while output per person rose from {{stat:gdppc_urn_125}} to {{stat:gdppc_urn_170}}. Cities, rail and housing are the main budget fights.
  • The Equalists. A movement against benders, declared a terrorist organization in 170 AG after it attacked the probending arena in Republic City. Its leader is a former Harmonist. See Equalists.

Geopolitical decisions

  • The Water Tribe split. {{stat:urn_fb_wt|n}} residents were born in the two Water Tribes. As the unity of North and South begins to break down in the civil war of 170–174 AG, the Council has refused to recognize either side and keeps its ports and reception centers open to refugees.
  • The Fire Nation. Relations are close and tense. {{stat:urn_fb_taj|n}} residents were born there, Tajisakian is an official language and trade is heavy, but veterans still remember the Eastern Territories. The Council wants commerce without political alignment.
  • Qianchan. Qianchan sponsored the republic's independence and supplied its rebels with surplus weapons. It is the republic's closest partner, but the Council has avoided a formal alliance with any power.
  • The Earth Kingdom. The republic sits on land the kingdom lost. Relations are cool and respectful, and the {{stat:urn_fb_ek|n}} residents born in the Earth Confederation are its largest foreign-born group ({{stat:urn_fbp_ek}}).
  • The airbenders. The republic keeps a Council seat for the Air Nomads, which it treats as a debt of the war, although the survivors are few.

Government and politics

  • Executive: the Republic Council has six members (one Fire, one Earth, two Water, one Air and one Non-Bender seat), elected by the National Assembly for staggered six-year terms (two terms maximum). The Council elects a President among its members; in 170 AG it is Tarrlok, the Northern Water councillor. The Council of 170 AG: Tarrlok, Viku (Southern Water), Ilama (Fire), Zi (Earth), Tenzin (Air), Ujo (Non-Bender). A reform approved 4–2 on 18 July 170 AG replaces the Council with an elected president and a two-chamber Congress from 171 AG (see Raiko); by 182 AG, after the penetration scandal, the Congress was undone and the National Assembly restored as the only chamber.
  • Legislature: the National Assembly is elected from single-member constituencies for four-year terms (three consecutive terms maximum).
  • Judiciary: the Supreme Court has nine justices serving twelve-year terms.
  • Political parties: Servants of the Republic, Progressives, Federalists and the Nationalist Union.
  • Divisions: eight Regions and one Special Administrative Capital (the National Capital Region). Regions are divided into prefectures.

Constitutional evolution

The republic has had three constitutional settlements. The Constitutional Charter is dated 100 AG, the Founding Congress declared the Union in 102 AG, and in 171 AG the Raiko Reform replaced the Council with a president and a two-chamber Congress. By 182 AG that Congress had been undone and the National Assembly was restored.

PeriodGovernmentExecutiveLegislature
102–171 AG (First Republic)Unitary council republicSix-member Republic Council, with a Council Head rotating yearlyNational Assembly (국회, Gukhoe), unicameral
171–182 AG (Second Republic)Presidential republicDirectly elected President and Vice PresidentCongress: High Council (senators) and House of Representatives
182 AG onward (Third Republic)Presidential republicPresident and Federal CabinetNational Assembly, unicameral, expanded

First Republic, 102–171 AG

The executive was a collective of six councillors, modelled on the Swiss Federal Council. Each oversaw ministries, decisions were collegial, and the Council Head rotated every year. The Council was the Republic Council (공화국평의회, Gonghwaguk Pyeonguihoe), and a member was a Republic Councillor. The Assembly legislated, approved the budget and oversaw the Council. See the Charter.

Second Republic, 171–182 AG

The Raiko Reform, ratified in 171 AG, replaced the Council with a President and Vice President elected directly for four years. Legislative power passed to a Congress of a High Council, whose six Founding Seats kept the Council’s composition and which added two Senators per region, and a House of Representatives of at most 300. See the reformed Charter.

Third Republic, from 182 AG

After the penetration scandal of 181–182 AG, the reform was undone by the Restoration of 182 AG. The National Assembly returned as the single chamber, with expanded membership, the six founding constituencies became designated blocs inside it, the Speaker rotates yearly among them, and a Constitutional Court and a vetting commission were added. It approves legislation and budgets, oversees the executive and conducts presidential impeachments. The president remains head of state and government, with a Federal Cabinet; the Federal Council of the original Charter, and the High Council, do not return. The republic’s constituent communities are represented inside the Assembly, and provincial autonomy rests on constitutional provisions.

Geography

The main types of relief are coastal plains, grasslands, forests and mountains or hills.


Main types of relief.

History

The United Republic of Nations was established in 102 AG on the Yanakawan Peninsula following the [[hundred_year_war|Hundred Year War]] and the subsequent Decade of revolutions. The peninsula, once home to numerous Fire Nation colonies and settlements within territories claimed by the [[earth_kingdom|Earth Confederation]], became the center of a protracted struggle over sovereignty, colonial rule and national self-determination. Its Provisional Council sat at [[qinglan_port|Qinglan Port]] during the [[yanakawan_war_of_independence|War of Independence]].

The Hundred Year War, also known as the Great War, devastated the world, claimed an estimated {{stat:hyw_deaths}} lives, and brought the [[air_nomads|Air Nomads]] to the brink of extinction. Following the [[Treaty of Ba Sing Se]], the defeated Empire of Tajisaki faced the question of whether to retain, relinquish or negotiate the future of its colonies, while diplomats from Ba Sing Se pressed for the restoration of occupied territories and the resolution of competing territorial claims. The peninsula's diverse population and complex colonial history ultimately made independence the preferred solution, recognized by the [[treaty_of_qinglan|Treaty of Qinglan]] and culminating in the Declaration of Union by the Founding Congress in 102 AG and recognition at Qinglan in 105 AG.

The new republic adopted a council-based system of government, bringing together representatives of its constituent communities to prevent renewed conflict and establish a common political order. Its early years were marked by economic disruption, competing national interests, and the difficult task of integrating former colonial administrations and rival armed factions. Over subsequent decades, reconstruction, migration and industrial development transformed the United Republics into a cosmopolitan state whose population included people from across the western and eastern continents. Firebenders and earthbenders formed the largest bending communities, while nonbenders and waterbenders constituted significant minorities. Despite its emergence as a major center of commerce and cultural exchange, the republic's founding compromises and the social inequalities inherited from the colonial era continued to shape its politics long after independence.

sozin.title: Sozin
sozin.html:
Fire Lord of the Empire of Tajisaki and the instigator of the Hundred Year War.

Sozin
ReignBefore 0 AG – 20 AG
Died20 AG
Known forThe Air Nomad Genocide; the plan to subjugate the Water Tribes

Sozin was the Fire Lord who began the Hundred Year War. He was a friend of Avatar Roku, who refused to help him expand his empire and spared him in 37 BG. When Roku died on Island Jezhi in 12 BG, Sozin, who could have helped him, left him to die. He then militarized the Fire Nation for twelve years, knowing that the next Avatar would be born among the Air Nomads.

In 0 AG he used the return of the comet to destroy the Air Nomads, and a week later ordered the Water Tribes subjugated and worked to death, an order that his successors carried out for a hundred years. He sought the surviving Avatar until his death in 20 AG. His successor, Azulon, began the Sōen program in 47 AG.

azulon.title: Azulon
azulon.html:
Fire Lord of the Empire of Tajisaki, 20–97 AG. Murdered by his son Ozai.

Azulon
Reign20 AG – 97 AG
Died10 June 97 AG (poisoned)
HeirOzai
Known forThe Sōen program; the Siege of Ba Sing Se; the Ash Directive

Azulon succeeded Sozin in 20 AG and ruled for 77 years of the Hundred Year War. He continued the subjugation of the Water Tribes, ordered the Sōen program in 47 AG, backed General Iroh's Si Wong Offensive and the Siege of Ba Sing Se, and, after the failure of the siege and the death of Iroh's son Lu Ten, lost faith in Iroh. In the siege he issued the Ash Directive to raze Ba Sing Se, which Iroh opposed.

On 10 June 97 AG Azulon was poisoned at dinner and died in his sleep. The Court blamed Qianchan agents, and the kitchen staff were executed, but the poisoning had been arranged by his younger son Ozai, which was established only after the civil war.

ozai.title: Ozai
ozai.html:
Fire Lord of the Empire of Tajisaki, 97–100 AG, and self-proclaimed Tentei, the Emperor of the Sky.

Ozai
Reign24 June 97 AG – 18 July 100 AG
Died18 July 100 AG, Qinglan Port (killed by Aang)
TitlesFire Lord; Tentei (17 July 100 AG)
HeirAzula (disputed)

Ozai came to the throne after poisoning his father Azulon in 97 AG. He pardoned Rear Admiral Yueya and Captain Zhao in July 97, which began the Pardon Crisis, and polarized the Empire against his opponents, led by Iroh. In 99 AG he launched the combined operation against both poles, to eradicate the Water Tribes so that no new Avatar could rise.

In July 100 AG he went to Qinglan Port to oversee the Sōen, personally supplied the trigger input to fire it at Ba Sing Se on 17 July, and proclaimed himself Tentei. The next day, caught off guard by the allied bombardment, he was killed by the Avatar in the Avatar State, with a stone lance through both lungs, 23 minutes after the first shells fell. His death, announced on the high command radio, collapsed the Empire's central authority.

azula.html:
Daughter of Ozai. The Court's Fire Lord, 25 July 100 AG – 9 May 118 AG.

Azula
ReignClaimed the throne 25 July 100 AG
Died9 May 118 AG (killed by Zuko in the Duel of the Palace)
FactionThe Court (Ozai loyalists)

Azula was named Ozai's successor in a sealed designation produced by the General Staff Directorate, and was confirmed in a ceremony on 25 July 100 AG, after the army rigged the succession over the Diet's resolution for Zuko. Her right to the throne was equal to her brother's, but he had the backing of the Diet and the people, and both claimed to be Fire Lord until the Duel of the Palace. She led the Court Government in the Fire Nation Civil War, with the General Staff, the Ministry of Truth, the Flame Guard and the cultists who revered her father, and continued a naval war against Yanakawa until 110 AG.

By 118 AG, with the Court's forces broken, she called her brother to a duel under the Way of the Warrior, blamed him for everything, and used lightning in breach of its rules. Zuko redirected it and beheaded her.

zuko.title: Zuko
zuko.html:
Prince of the Empire of Tajisaki, leader of the Royalists and Fire Lord, 118–168 AG.

Zuko
Reign118 AG – 168 AG
FactionThe Royalists (Restoration Government)
SuccessorHis daughter Izumi (abdicated 168 AG)

Zuko was the popular heir whom the Diet wanted as Fire Lord in July 100 AG. His claim rested on the legitimacy that the Diet and the people gave him, against a sister whose right to the throne was equal to his, and the two spent eighteen years disputing which of them was the Fire Lord. After the rigged succession for Azula, he left Caldera City on 5 August, and with his uncle Iroh led the Restoration Government at Shu Jing in the Fire Nation Civil War, supported by Qianchan supplies through the Southern Air Temple island chain. Royalist propaganda later credited him with Ozai's defeat. He killed Azula in the Duel of the Palace on 9 May 118 AG and was crowned Fire Lord later that year. At his coronation an assassin was shot before he could fire.

His reign (118–168 AG) was a 50-year rebuilding of the devastated archipelago, with the economic recovery of 140 AG. In 168 AG, ill from a suspected poisoning, he abdicated to his daughter Izumi.

118 AG: Unity Tower

Six weeks after the armistice that ended the Fire Nation civil war, Zuko was in Republic City for the anniversary of the republic, and he flew with the Avatar to the Endless Ocean in an airship that was lost there. He fought at the Unity Tower attack on 27 September, returned to Caldera City on 30 September, and told the Diet that the Fire Nation would send ships, grain and builders to the republic’s harbor. The Diet asked why a naval vessel boarded by the Denied in August had been treated as a customs matter.

Death

Zuko, who had been ill with a wasting condition of the lungs for thirty years, was killed on the night of 3 January 181 AG when an ambulance carrying him from a hospital in Mutsukawa, the old central district of Caldera City was blown up on the highway. He had been in a coma for some days. Earth Empire agents, acting for the State Security Bureau, had learned where he lay and planted a bomb in the hospital car park to clear the guards. Princess Kiko announced his death in an emergency broadcast early on 4 January, and the state funeral was held in Shinja on 15 January with about 400,000 people on the streets. Shortly before the attack he had given Avatar Korra a letter from Aang about energybending and the location of a scroll on Kuchuya Island. See Opening phase of the Earth Empire–Concord War.

iroh.title: Iroh
iroh.html:
General of the Empire of Tajisaki, architect of the Si Wong Offensive and the Ba Sing Se siege, later the opposition leader.

Iroh
RankGeneral; Field Marshal (94–97 AG); retired 98 AG
SonLu Ten (killed 25 November 96 AG)
Died9 March 101 AG, Shu Jing (Salvationist bomb)

Iroh was the General Staff Directorate's Planning Director, who designed Plan Yellow and the Si Wong Offensive (80–88 AG), and in 94 AG became Field Marshal for the Siege of Ba Sing Se. His son Lu Ten was killed in the Palace on 25 November 96 AG, and Iroh opposed the Ash Directive to raze the city. He was demoted to General after the siege.

After Ozai's accession and the Pardon Crisis, he became the leader of the opposition. He addressed the Veterans' Assembly in January 98 AG, was forced to retire later that year, and was given a seat in the Diet. In August 100 AG he joined his nephew Zuko, as the Royalists' Chief of Staff, brought defecting garrisons over, and opened the channel to Qianchan. On 9 March 101 AG a Salvationist bomb went off at the Lily House, the Royalists’ teahouse and conference hall at Shu Jing, and within minutes a Kanbukyoku squad came through the gate. Iroh and ten others died, and the squad was killed with them. His tea was still on the table, and the bonsai in the courtyard stood in the pattern he used when he wanted to remember something. The Royalists made him their martyr.

Legacy: the martyr of Shu Jing

Iroh is remembered in the Fire Nation as a martyr. He was the general who had opposed the Ash Directive, the veteran who had stood against the Fire Lord in the Pardon Crisis, and the uncle who left Caldera with Zuko when the Court seized the throne, and he was killed on 9 March 101 AG by the bomb of the Salvationists and the raid of the Kanbukyoku, at the table where the Royalists were seeking an agreement with Qianchan. The Royalists used his death to sustain their cause through the harshest years of the war, and Zuko, who named his own reign a restoration, held to the principles of his uncle for the remainder of his life.

lu_ten.title: Lu Ten
lu_ten.html:
Known in the Imperial press as the People's Prince (民の王子, Tami no Ōji).

Lu Ten
RankLieutenant (87 AG); Captain, Armored Corps (89 AG); Lieutenant Colonel (96 AG)
FamilyHouse of the Fire Lord. Son of General Iroh; grandson of Fire Lord Azulon; nephew of Prince Ozai
EducationImperial Military Academy (graduated 87 AG)
ServiceSi Wong Offensive (final action, 88 AG); Jasmine Island (90 AG); Siege of Ba Sing Se (96 AG)
DecorationsOrder of the Golden Flame (88 AG)
Died25 November 96 AG, Ba Sing Se
Known forThe Battle of the Rail Cut; stopping the Jasmine Island Mutiny; the Address on Conduct (90 AG)

Lu Ten was an officer of the Imperial Army and the only son of General Iroh, the Directorate's Planning Director and the architect of the Si Wong Offensive. He was the grandson of Fire Lord Azulon, and third in the line of succession after his father and his uncle Prince Ozai. He was the best-known serving officer of the Imperial family. A decorated tank officer, he became a public figure in 90 AG, when he refused to take part in the destruction of Jasmine Island by Rear Admiral Yueya, gave evidence against her at her court-martial, and then submitted a written appeal to the Fire Lord and the National Diet that called for reforms against abuse of authority in the armed forces. It was the first time a member of the dynasty had publicly criticized the military's own conduct. The Address made him a political figure as well as a popular one, and it set the court, the General Staff Directorate and the Diet's reformers against each other on a question that had not previously been debated in public.

Early life

Lu Ten was born in the capital to Iroh and his wife, and raised in a household that combined the court and the General Staff. His father was away on campaign for much of his childhood. Unlike his cousins, who were educated at court, he was sent at the usual age to the Imperial Military Academy. Contemporary accounts describe him as an able but unremarkable student who was popular with his classmates, many of them sons of provincial officers and colonial families, and who had an unusual habit of eating in the cadet mess and not at the instructors' table.

Military career

Academy and Armored Corps

Lu Ten graduated as a lieutenant in 87 AG and chose the Armored Corps, a branch that the General Staff regarded as the future of the war and that suffered heavy losses. The choice was widely read as a decision to serve in the line and not on his father's staff, and Iroh is reported to have been displeased at the lack of consultation.

Si Wong

Lu Ten was posted to the Si Wong front a few months before the Offensive ended. He commanded a platoon of four medium tanks. By then the Empire held Tongba and the desert's road and rail corridor, and the front was a fortified line on the desert's eastern edge. The last major action of Plan Yellow was fought there in August 88 AG, when the Coalition counter-attacked the rail cut that anchored the Imperial line.

Lu Ten's platoon was attached to an infantry company that was cut off in the first hours of the attack. Imperial accounts say that he held the cut with his four tanks for most of a day, that two of them were lost, and that he went back on foot under fire to recover their crews. The platoon helped to cover the infantry's withdrawal, and the line held. He received the Order of the Golden Flame, and the Offensive ended five days later.

The Imperial press made much of the fact that he had fought in the offensive his father had planned. His critics, mainly in the Navy, noted that he had done so at the lowest officer rank, and that a prince had more protection than most lieutenants. Accounts by the men of his platoon say that he shared their rations, avoided the officers' mess and wrote letters for the wounded. Veterans' papers in the colonies printed these stories first, and the capital's press followed. After the battle he also submitted a report on looting by rear-area supply units in the occupied desert towns, which the Directorate filed without action.

Promotion and posting (88–90 AG)

Lu Ten was promoted to captain in 89 AG and posted to the Armored Corps' staff in the western command. In early 90 AG he was temporarily attached, as an Army liaison, to the Jasmine Island garrison, one of the Army's smaller commitments in the western island chain.

Public image

By 90 AG Lu Ten was the most popular member of the dynasty. He was popular for several reasons. He had fought in the ranks, and veterans said so. His family was known for its closeness to the army and its distance from the court. Unlike his uncle Ozai, who was associated with the court's hardliners, he spoke plainly and did not hide his opinions. In the colonies, where the Imperial family was a distant and often resented institution, his visits to veterans' associations were widely reported, and the phrase "the People's Prince" originated in the colonial press. His critics, mainly in the Navy and the court, called the title a creation of newspapers, and said that a prince who could be so popular with the troops was a political risk.

Jasmine Island incident

Background

Jasmine Island is a small Imperial possession in the western island chain, known for its tea and golden jasmine, governed by a three-member island council under Imperial supervision, with a small Army garrison and a local constabulary known as the protectors. It had no history of unrest. Rear Admiral Yueya commanded a Navy squadron in the western islands and had petitioned, in early 90 AG, for the post of garrison commander. The petition was denied, since the post was an Army one, and officers who served with her described her as obsessed with the island.

The attack

On the night of 7 June 90 AG, the island's New Moon Celebration, Yueya took her squadron, a battlecruiser and two destroyers, to the island and declared it in rebellion. There was no rebellion. Her second-in-command, Captain Zhao, planted explosive charges in the market square under the Monument to Peace, which fell onto the council chambers and killed two of the island's three councillors and a large part of the crowd. Her landing parties then burned the town and the fields.

Lu Ten's refusal

Lu Ten, who had landed with the Army company in the second wave, found no rebels, only burning houses and civilians. He stopped his men from taking part and ordered them to help with the fire-fighting and evacuation, and he met Lieutenant Akataa and the garrison's survivors, who had been fighting in the streets. He went to Yueya on the quay and demanded an end to the attack. She refused and ordered it widened, and at about 01:50 he sent his report to the Western Command from the company's radio.

The brig and the harbor

The killing grew through the night. Yueya's marines seized the battlecruiser, arrested its captain, executive officer and about 60 sailors who had refused to fire on the island, and locked them in the brig, and the ship's guns then shelled the refugees on the hillside and the market district. Near 04:30 the imprisoned sailors blew their way out of the brig with the ship's demolition charges, fought up three decks to the bridge, and retook it. At dawn Lu Ten, with the Army detachment, the garrison and the Navy officers who had refused to follow her, called on the mutineers to surrender, and arrested Yueya on her destroyer's bridge. About 2,000 civilians had been killed, and about half the main settlement and 80% of the island's fields were destroyed. Zhao's conduct after the first assault is unclear.

Court-martial

Lu Ten gave evidence against Yueya to the Directorate, and demanded a trial. She was court-martialed by a joint Army and Navy panel in the summer of 90 AG, convicted of exceeding her orders, of deceiving the War Council and of the unlawful killing of Imperial subjects, and sentenced to imprisonment. Zhao was tried with her and convicted on lesser charges. He argued that he had followed orders, and he was reduced in rank. The Navy resisted the verdict, and tried to limit the sentence by arguing that Yueya's actions were an unfortunate excess of zeal in wartime. It did not accept the account of the operation until the island's own witnesses had been heard.

Jasmine Island was placed under a civilian administrator, and the Directorate granted a program of aid and reconstruction. The island council, which had lost two members, was allowed to hold new elections.

The Address on Conduct

The trial did not satisfy Lu Ten. In the autumn of 90 AG he submitted a written appeal, the Address on Conduct, to Fire Lord Azulon and the National Diet. It argued that Jasmine Island was not an exception. The war had given officers wide latitude, and the Empire's institutions had no means of checking them; Yueya had been stopped by chance, because an Army captain had been in the right place. It asked that "savages" not be allowed to taint the image of the Imperial military, by which Lu Ten meant officers and soldiers who used the Empire's uniform for private revenge or for cruelty, and it said that an army that burned its own subjects had lost the purpose it was fighting for. It proposed:

  • independent military tribunals that are not under the control of the service chiefs;
  • a requirement that any declaration of martial law or emergency be reported to the Directorate and the Diet within days, and that operations beyond their orders be halted;
  • legal protection for civilians in Imperial and occupied territory;
  • the prosecution of abuses of authority regardless of rank;
  • a clearer division between the Army and Navy in garrison appointments.

Reception

The Address was received very differently in different places. Reformers in the Diet, who had been a minority for years, welcomed it, and a group of colonial delegates asked that it be debated in full. The press and the veterans' papers praised it, and it was read aloud in several colonial cities. Public opinion in the capital and the colonies is strongly in Lu Ten's favor.

Azulon's court did not answer it directly. The Fire Lord could not punish a decorated grandson, and he did not endorse the proposals. The General Staff Directorate opposed independent tribunals as a threat to command authority, and the Navy was openly hostile. Prince Ozai praised the court-martial but described the proposed tribunals as "an insult to those who command", and aligned himself with the court's hardliners. Iroh has not spoken publicly in support of his son's proposals, though it is widely assumed that he approves. Observers in the capital note that the Address has put the dynasty's two lines on opposite sides of a public question for the first time.

Political views

Lu Ten's published views, so far, are limited to the Address. They show a preoccupation with accountability, and a belief that the military's legitimacy depends on its conduct. He has not yet taken a public position on the war's conduct beyond this, on colonial representation in the Diet, or on conscription.

Personal life

Lu Ten is unmarried. He is reported to be close to his father, and he is known to be a tea drinker, a habit that the press has linked to the tea ceremony the islanders offered him after the incident.

Later life and death (91–96 AG)

After the trial Lu Ten became the center of a reform movement in the Diet and among veterans, and the Navy and the General Staff Directorate watched him. He was promoted to lieutenant colonel and in 95 AG took command of a battalion of Breaker power armor. In 96 AG he served under his father, the Field Marshal, in the Siege of Ba Sing Se. In November his battalion was among the assault battalions that took the Inner City and the Palace. After the Imperial forces had held the Palace and the Forbidden City for a week, a charge detonated in the underground galleries beneath them, and on 25 November 96 AG he was killed.

Legacy

His death, and the reprisals that followed, hardened his father against the siege. Azulon, who had lost faith in Iroh, ordered the city razed in the Ash Directive, which Iroh opposed, and demoted him. The Address on Conduct, which was Lu Ten's only published statement, became the program of the reformers. It was the standard that the Diet's opposition used against Ozai's pardon of Yueya and Zhao in 97 AG, which began the Pardon Crisis, and Iroh, who had not spoken in support of it, became its leader. The reformers who followed Iroh and Zuko in the Fire Nation Civil War remembered him as the People's Prince.

Honours

  • Order of the Golden Flame (88 AG)

aang.title: Aang
aang.html:
The Avatar, the last known airbender, and the killer of Ozai.

Aang
NationAir Nomads (Southern Air Temple)
FoundLate November 99 AG, in the South Pole
Known forKilling Fire Lord Ozai at Qinglan Port, 18 July 100 AG

Aang was born at the Southern Air Temple and was frozen at the time of the genocide. Southern guerrillas found him in the ice near Taluqqriaq in late November 99 AG, during the Southern Uprising, and he escaped to Qianchan as the capital fell. In July 100 AG he joined the allied attack on Qinglan Port and, in the Avatar State, killed Fire Lord Ozai with a stone lance through both lungs. He was unconscious for two days. After the war he helped the United Republic of Nations rebuild. He died in about 153 AG, and the Avatar cycle passed to the Southern Water Tribe as Korra.

Unity Tower, 118 AG

In early September 118 AG Aang climbed Mount Baihu to test the legend of Sonam, a forgotten Avatar whom Xian had told him of, and opened the energy sphere that held Tagah. Tagah took him to Sonam's Staff, killed or wounded his companions, and called Jharana out of the Spirit World above Republic City. On 27 September Aang beat him in front of Unity Tower and broke the staff, which ended the airbending of the Denied. He afterwards began a new Air Temple near the city. See Unity Tower attack.

qin_the_great.title: Qin the Great
qin_the_great.html:
Also known as Chin the Conqueror. A lord of the south who tried to reform the authority of Ba Sing Se. Killed in 270 BG.

Qin the Great
SeatGaoling
AlliesAvatar Kyoshi; the King of Omashu; the Lord of Yu Dao; the lords of Tongshui
Died270 BG, outside the walls of Ba Sing Se (dishonorable duel)
DynastyThe Qin Dynasty (his heirs)

Qin the Great was a southern lord who rose in the chaos of the late Warring States, and wanted to reform the absolute authority of the Earth King in Ba Sing Se. With the Avatar Kyoshi, the King of Omashu and the Lord of Yu Dao, he conquered the northwest and brought the rest of the continent, apart from Ba Sing Se and Kyoshi's peninsula, under his banner. In 270 BG, at the city's outer walls, he fought a duel with the Earth King. The king cheated, with hidden crossbowmen and a poisoned blade, and Qin was killed, although he mortally wounded the king. Kyoshi then went into the Inner City and forced the reforms of the royal court.

His death caused a power vacuum. His heirs ruled as the Qin Dynasty, which the southern lands overthrew in the War of Liberation (270–255 BG). The revolt gave the Qianchan Republic its independence. The Qin Dynasty collapsed in famine in 255 BG, and Ba Sing Se, under Bao Kun, took advantage of it.

kyoshi.title: Kyoshi
kyoshi.html:
The Avatar of the Earth Kingdom's 3rd-century BG upheavals, a protector of the reform of Ba Sing Se.

Kyoshi
HomeKyoshi Island (a peninsula of the Earth Kingdom)
Notable actsAllied with Qin the Great; reformed the royal court of Ba Sing Se (270 BG); the peasant uprising settlement

Kyoshi was an Avatar from the Earth Kingdom, who lived in the age of the Warring States. She thought Qin the Great's cause of reforming Ba Sing Se just, and joined his coalition. When Qin was killed outside the walls in 270 BG, in a duel in which the Earth King cheated, she went into the Inner City, and forced the royal court to accept a written constitution and to treat the peasants fairly, which ended a peasant uprising in the city. She spent the rest of her life keeping the peace between the nations and between the fifty-five states of the Earth Kingdom. Her warrior order, the Kyoshi Warriors, remained a power on her island. Her insistence on defending the Earth King's court from its own people while reforming it was criticized by the Qianchan republicans, who did not believe in the monarchy at all.

kuei.title: Kuei
kuei.html:
The 52nd Earth King, 81 AG onward.

Kuei
BornAbout 77 AG
CrownedAbout 81 AG, aged four
ResidenceBa Sing Se

Kuei became Earth King as a four-year-old after the Dai Li murdered his father, and grew up shut away from the war under the regency of Long Feng. The Siege of Ba Sing Se (96–97 AG) opened his eyes. After the siege he began to centralize command, which provoked the Dai Li's coup attempt of 98 AG. He put it down, ended the regency, and by 99 AG was running the war from Ba Sing Se on the Northern Front. He was in the Palace's command bunker when the Sōen struck in July 100 AG.

Death

Kuei died in 153 AG, aged about seventy-six. The court announced that he had died peacefully in his sleep. In fact his daughter Hou-Ting had him killed; the court physician who signed the certificate left the palace and was not seen again. He had cleaned up the corruption of the war years, given all adults the vote in 150 AG and left a larger and richer kingdom, and she reversed his reforms at once.
