photography_in_the_au.title: Photography and the visual record
photography_in_the_au.html:
How the world sees itself, and who decides what it is allowed to see.

Photography and the visual record
Era35mm film to about 170 AG; digital by about 180 AG
WireCaldera City to Republic City in hours
Main bodiesGaoling Press Cooperative, Republic City Press Award, IJSC
AgenciesZaofu Tupian, Imperial News Service

In this world photography is a mature trade. The visual record of the war is not hand-painted, as it is in the story the wiki is rewritten from: it was shot on film, filed in archives and sent over the wire. A photograph taken in Caldera City reaches Republic City within hours, and newsreels play in cinemas.

From 35mm to digital

Through the war and the first decades of the peace the trade ran on 35mm film, developed in darkrooms and sent by wire. Digital cameras take over between about 170 AG and 180 AG. The Republican Daily still develops film in its fifth-floor darkroom, although its staff shoot digital.

Three bending interactions

Firebending gives a precise, controllable light, so portrait and military photography in the Empire developed faster than it otherwise would have. The Imperial Research Bureau flies the most advanced aerial reconnaissance photography in the world.

Metalbending at Zaofu makes precision optics, so photographers who work with Zaofu lenses have better glass than anyone else.

Waterbending in the darkroom holds developer at an exact temperature, so results are more consistent and come back faster.

The photographs that matter

See the gallery of famous photographs: the Void Wind photographs, the Kaimei Valley photographs, the Sōen strike photographs, the Dragon Flats photographs and Kuvira walking away.

Why it matters

The genocide of the Air Nomads has a visual record. It was photographed by the people who committed it, and it sits in boxes in the Caldera archive, filed as “historical interest only.” You can manage an absence. You cannot manage a photograph; you can only keep it classified.

photograph_gallery.title: Gallery of famous photographs
photograph_gallery.html:
Five photographs the world argues about. Each plate is reserved for an embedded photograph; add one by filling in PHOTOS for its slot.

See also Photography and the visual record.

void_wind_photographs.title: Void Wind photographs
void_wind_photographs.html:
The genocide, documented by the military that committed it.

Void Wind photographs
Date0 AG
Held atCaldera archive (classified)
SubjectThe four Air Temple assaults of Operation Void Wind
StatusUnreleased; filed as “historical interest only”

The Empire photographed all four temple assaults of Operation Void Wind. The photographs have sat in boxes in the Caldera archive, unread since 7 AG. The Republican Daily has asked for access since 118 AG and has been refused each time on national security grounds.

Aang knows they exist and has never seen them; Tenzin knows too. In 151 AG the IJSC formally asked the Empire’s National Archive to release them to the representatives of the Air Nomad cultural community, on the ground that photographic documentation of a genocide belongs to the survivors and not to the state that carried it out. The Empire declined. The Imperial News Service called the request politically motivated; the IJSC replied that the reaction confirmed the photographs exist.

See also Air Nomad Genocide.

kaimei_valley_photographs.title: Kaimei Valley photographs
kaimei_valley_photographs.html:
The founding archive of the Republican Daily.

Kaimei Valley photographs
Date103 AG
PhotographerDao Fengling
PublishedRepublican Daily, edition six
ResultMade the Ryu Jinshan prosecution possible

Dao Fengling photographed the atrocity site at Kaimei Valley in 103 AG. The Republican Daily could not reproduce photographs in its first edition, because the press was salvaged colonial equipment; the pictures ran from edition six. They gave the tribunal documentary evidence rather than testimony alone, and that is what made the prosecution of Ryu Jinshan possible.

Fengling later gave her name to the Fengling Fellowship.

soen_strike_photographs.title: Sōen strike photographs
soen_strike_photographs.html:
Before: a city. After: what 9.4 kilotons of directed thermal energy does to a city.

Sōen strike photographs
SubjectSōen strike on Ba Sing Se
PhotographerLiang Weiming, Qianchan aerial reconnaissance
FormatTwo frames, side by side
AwardINS Photo of the Year, 99 AG (INS services only)

Qianchan aerial reconnaissance photographed Ba Sing Se before and after the strike. Liang Weiming kept the negatives against explicit orders. The two frames won the Imperial News Service’s Photo of the Year for 99 AG. That prize was given only within the INS services; the Republic City Press Award did not exist until 108 AG.

The photographs were shown to Korra as part of her Avatar education. They are why she has never thought about weapons in the abstract.

dragon_flats_photographs.title: Dragon Flats photographs
dragon_flats_photographs.html:
An image that poses no challenge to the powerful does not need the powerful to suppress it.

Dragon Flats photographs
Date148 AG (uncropped version printed 149 AG)
Published byRepublican Daily
AwardRCPA Photo of the Year, 148 AG
CostGovernment press credential, suspended for eight months

Civilian photographers were present at the Dragon Flats massacre. The Republican Daily published two photographs. The official inquiry’s report printed only one, cropped to remove a detail about the police unit’s positioning that contradicted the official account of the timing. A source inside the inquiry gave the paper the uncropped frame, and it ran in 149 AG. The government suspended the paper’s press credential for eight months.

The RCPA jury chair said: “The suspension confirms the photograph’s importance. An image that poses no challenge to the powerful does not need the powerful to suppress it.”

kuvira_walking_away.title: Kuvira walking away
kuvira_walking_away.html:
The image that defines the event in the historical record.

Kuvira walking away
Date6 p.m., 8 June 171 AG
PublishedRepublican Daily, late edition of 8 June
PhotographerDao Ruiming
SubjectKuvira walking away from the colonnade
AwardRCPA Photo of the Year, 171 AG

Dao Ruiming photographed Kuvira at six in the evening on 8 June 171 AG, walking away from the colonnade as the fighting in Ba Sing Se Square went on into the night. The Republican Daily ran it in its late edition that night. Within forty-eight hours every major publication in the world had reproduced it over the wire. The Imperial News Service captioned it as military professionalism; the Qianchan wire (QPA) captioned it as a question about what she does next.

The RCPA chose it after two days of deliberation, over Mei Shaoyang’s forty photographs of civilians. The jury said: “The smoke and the fire tell you what happened. The woman walking away with half a bread roll and a question about a map tells you what comes next. We are all living in what comes next.”

gaoling_press_cooperative.title: Gaoling Press Cooperative
gaoling_press_cooperative.html:
Gaoling Press Cooperative
Founded87 AG, Gaoling
Members340 by 171 AG
TypePhotographer-owned cooperative

The Gaoling Press Cooperative (GPC) is the world’s photographer-owned cooperative. Twelve photographers who covered the war founded it in 87 AG, on the belief that the people who make the historical record should control what happens to it. Members own their work. No government, outlet or client can tell a member what to shoot or suppress what they have shot.

It holds the most comprehensive visual record of the Hundred Year War. The Imperial Research Bureau tried three times to obtain the work of Qianchan military photographers and was refused each time. Members are elected by their peers, and the GPC has never admitted a photographer whose main work was for a state propaganda organ, which has shut out several technically brilliant photographers from the Empire’s Ministry of Public Information.

republic_city_press_award.title: Republic City Press Award
republic_city_press_award.html:
Republic City Press Award
Founded108 AG
SeatFormer Yanakawa Province Colonial Press Bureau, Republic City
JurySeven

The Republic City Press Award (RCPA) is the world’s annual press photography competition. Its Photo of the Year and Story of the Year define the visual record. It sits in Republic City because the United Republic is the only state that can host an international journalism contest without its own politics bending the jury.

The jury has seven members: two photographers chosen by the GPC, two editors chosen by participating publications, one historian chosen by the Gaoling Academy, one press freedom advocate chosen by the IJSC, and one rotating international member chosen by the previous year’s winner. In 169 AG radio journalism was added to the eligibility rules.

The award occupies the building where press freedom was denied. Dao Fengling recommended it: “Put the press freedom award in the building where press freedom was denied. Make the building remember what it was for.” The lobby shows the colonial bureau’s original sign and her framed first edition of the Republican Daily, inscribed: “This newspaper is published because a story existed and had nowhere to go.”

fengling_fellowship.title: Fengling Fellowship
fengling_fellowship.html:
Fengling Fellowship
Founded153 AG
SeatAcademy of Gaoling
FellowsTwenty a year

The Fengling Fellowship is named for Dao Fengling, who died in 153 AG. It is a fully funded one-year fellowship for mid-career journalists of any nation, chosen for significant work done under significant institutional or state pressure.

ijsc.title: International Journalist Safety Commission
ijsc.html:
International Journalist Safety Commission
Founded120 AG
PublishesAnnual report and Press Freedom Index
MemorialRepublic City

The IJSC tracks journalists killed, imprisoned and disappeared in every nation, and keeps a memorial in Republic City naming every journalist killed in the line of work since its founding. The latest name before 171 AG was Ho Wenxia, a Ba Sing Se Times stringer who disappeared in 169 AG; Tenzin attended the unveiling.

Press Freedom Index, 171 AG

  1. Qianchan Republic
  2. United Republic of Nations
  3. Fire Nation
  4. Northern Water Tribe
  5. Southern Water Tribe
  6. Earth Kingdom, last every year since 131 AG

In 151 AG the IJSC asked the Empire to release the Void Wind photographs.

zaofu_tupian.title: Zaofu Tupian
zaofu_tupian.html:
Zaofu Tupian
NameZaofu Tupian (Zaofu Images)
SeatZaofu
FoundedAG 88
MottoA plate is a witness.
TypePhoto agency and picture library
Member ofThe Outlet

Zaofu Tupian, “Zaofu Images,” is the photo agency and picture library of the press collective, the in-world house that holds and licenses press photographs. Plates are never retouched past dust and scratches, and each is filed with its photographer, place and hour. Its lenses come from Zaofu, where metalbending makes the finest optics in the world.

On The Outlet only the caption line is carried; the plate follows by courier.

imperial_news_service.title: Imperial News Service
imperial_news_service.html:
Imperial News Service
NameImperial News Service (INS)
NationEmpire of Tajisaki
TypeNews agency
Member ofThe Outlet

The Imperial News Service is the news agency of the Empire of Tajisaki. Its captions follow the Empire’s line. It captioned Dao Ruiming’s photograph of Kuvira as military professionalism, and called the IJSC’s 151 AG request for the Void Wind photographs politically motivated.

air_nomad_question.title: Air Nomad Question
air_nomad_question.html:
For most citizens of the United Republic, the Air Nomads have never been a people. They have been a tragedy.

A chapter in a history book. A painting on a classroom wall. A story told by grandparents who themselves never met an airbender. For over a century, the Air Nomads existed in public memory as victims rather than neighbors. Their extermination marked the beginning of the Hundred Year War and, for many years, its most enduring symbol. Yet symbols are easier to preserve than people.

Now, only months after the passing of Avatar Aang, that reality appears to be changing.

Over recent weeks this newspaper has confirmed reports of Air Nomad descendants, affiliated spiritual communities, Air Acolytes, and families claiming ancestral ties to the old nomad routes arriving on Air Temple Island from every corner of the world. Some come from the Fire Nation. Others arrive from remote Earth Kingdom provinces, the Water Tribes, and settlements throughout the United Republic. Some bear documented family histories. Others carry little more than oral traditions passed down through generations.

For the first time since the war, the possibility has emerged that the Air Nomads may survive not merely as a memory, but as a living community.

The gathering is modest in size. Its significance is not. That prospect has revived an old argument.

What, precisely, happened to them? And why has the world spent more than 150 years avoiding a clear answer?

A Question Older Than the Republic

The phrase "Air Nomad Genocide" is common today. It was not always so.

During the war, Imperial publications referred to the destruction of the temples as military operations. Official statements spoke of eliminating the Avatar threat and suppressing hostile elements. The language was bureaucratic, distant, and carefully chosen.

Even after the war, many governments preferred ambiguity. The Earth Kingdom, exhausted by invasion and civil collapse, focused on reconstruction. The Water Tribes honored the dead but possessed little documentary evidence. The Fire Nation's archives remained largely closed. Historians argued. Politicians deferred. The public moved on.

The result was a strange consensus. Everyone agreed the Air Nomads had disappeared. Few wished to discuss why.

The Facts We Know

There are, despite persistent claims to the contrary, certain facts that are no longer seriously disputed. The four Air Temples were attacked in coordinated operations. The assaults occurred at the outset of the war. The overwhelming majority of Air Nomads present at the temples were killed. The ancient institutions of Air Nomad society ceased to function afterward. No organized Air Nomad government, monastic order, or successor state survived. The Air Nomads, as a people, effectively vanished from world affairs.

Reasonable historians may debate numbers. They may debate planning, logistics, responsibility, and the degree to which individual commanders understood the scope of the operation. What becomes increasingly difficult to debate is the outcome. A culture that had existed for thousands of years was reduced to a handful of survivors. Among them was Avatar Aang. For generations, the world's understanding of the Air Nomads was largely mediated through a single man.

Now he, too, is gone.

The Weight of a Word

The disagreement centers on one word. Genocide.

There are those, particularly among conservative circles in the Fire Nation, who object to the term. They argue it imposes contemporary moral standards upon a distant conflict. Some insist the objective was military rather than ethnic. Others contend that the destruction of the temples, however catastrophic, does not prove an intention to eliminate an entire people.

These arguments deserve consideration. They have also been made for more than a century. Against them stands a simple fact: When the campaign began, there were Air Nomads. When it ended, there were not. If the deliberate destruction of a people does not constitute genocide, then words have lost their meaning.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW

Some readers may ask why this debate should be reopened at all. The war is long over. The perpetrators and victims are almost entirely gone. The world faces newer problems. The answer can be found on Air Temple Island. History is never merely about the dead. It is also about the living.

The young men and women arriving on the island today are not responsible for the crimes of the past. Nor are they merely custodians of someone else's memory. They are attempting to decide what it means to belong to a people that the world once assumed had vanished forever.

Their task is difficult enough without inherited falsehoods.

joha.title: Joha
joha.html:
This is a stub. It gathers what the wiki records and will be expanded.
Joha
TypePort city and prefecture
CountryKingdom of Tajisaki (Fire Nation)
Known as"The blood city"
PopulationAbout 400,000 (reported, 154 AG)
GovernorGenji Hoshino (154 AG)
NotableFirst mass Salvationist gatherings on its quay; the quay shooting of July 100 AG; the Joha Crisis, 153–154 AG

Joha is a port city of the Kingdom of Tajisaki, with a prefecture of six districts and grain towns inland. Its quay was the site of the first mass gatherings of the Salvationists in the last years of the Hundred Year War, and residents still call it the blood city.

The quay shooting, 100 AG

In July 100 AG, the week the news of Emperor Ozai’s death reached the coast, a gathering on the quay ended in killings. Residents disagree about who fired, and the wiki does not decide it. The memory shaped how every later crowd on the quay was read, by the crowd and by the authorities.

Economy and labor

The harbor was rebuilt after the civil war by dock crews, and the Joha Dockworkers’ Union, led in 154 AG by its secretary Haruki Nomura, says their pay for the rebuilding was never settled. The port also feeds a grain trade through the prefecture’s inland towns.

Open questions

Where Joha lies on the map, the exact boundaries of its prefecture, and who fired in 100 AG are not yet fixed.

See also

  • Joha Crisis
  • Salvationists
  • Fire Nation (Empire of Tajisaki)
  • Zuko

joha_crisis.title: Joha Crisis
joha_crisis.html:
Figures are in-universe estimates, taken from press reports of the time; where outlets disagree, both counts are given.
Joha Crisis
DateAugust 153 – at least September 154 AG
PlaceJoha and its prefecture, Tajisaki
CausesThe death of King Kuei and the revival of the leftist movement; the crash of 153 AG; unpaid dock wages
Deaths41 (prefectural police) or 118 (Joha Municipal Hospital) by September 154 AG; the counts have not been reconciled
OutcomeThe Fire Lord leaves public view after visiting on 11 September 154 AG; the Diet’s sitting of the 16th is postponed

The Joha Crisis was a year of strikes, riots and curfews in the port of Joha and its prefecture. It began as a wage dispute, became a memorial march for a dead king, and turned into a crisis of the Kingdom when the Fire Lord, Zuko, visited the city and then disappeared from public view. Her Highness Izumi took over the ceremonial duties of the throne, and her daughter Kiko, born on 28 December 155 AG, was given a name meaning “hope” for the nation’s stability.

Background, 153 AG

King Kuei died in August 153 AG, and leftist groups that had been quiet since the civil war held memorial rallies in cities from Caldera City outward. On 28 and 29 September the Caldera Exchange fell 31 percent in two sessions, and on 5 October two Joha companies laid off 2,300 workers. The Dockworkers’ Union, which says the harbor’s employers have owed back pay since the reconstruction, called a march for 9 October.

The riots of 9 October

About 4,000 to 6,000 people marched toward the quay memorial and were stopped by police at the Customs Road crossing. Bottles and stones were thrown, and the police fired into the crowd. Three people were killed, according to both the police and the union; 52 were treated at Joha Municipal Hospital, 19 of them police officers; 140 were arrested. Crowds broke shop windows and burned a freight office on the eastern quay, and the Governor imposed a curfew on the harbor district. By December there were riots in the grain towns inland, and curfews covered four of the prefecture’s six districts.

Salvationists

The union says the Salvationists came after the 9 October deaths, and Governor Genji Hoshino says they came first. By April 154 AG police had found a weapons cache in a warehouse and handbills in the old Salvationist slogans, and Commissioner Rin Katsura said “someone is doing the digging on purpose.” The wiki treats the question as open.

The Fire Lord’s visit

Zuko arrived on 11 September 154 AG to calm the city. The Royal Household Office says the visit was cut short because he tired. Two dock workers say the motorcade stopped at the quay memorial after a crowd surged forward and that they heard shots, which the police could not confirm. On 14 September the Office announced that the Fire Lord was resting on his physicians’ advice, and that the disturbances were the work of Salvationist sympathizers; it gave no date for his return.

The toll

Police put the dead since October 153 AG at 41. The director of Joha Municipal Hospital, Dr. Ayame Ôtsuka, says its records show 118 deaths from injuries and gunshot wounds. The Governor’s office says the hospital counts deaths from other causes during the curfew, which the hospital denies.

Open questions

Where the Fire Lord is, what he is being treated for, who ordered the curfews and under what authority, and which count of the dead is right.

  • Kuei
  • Zuko

  • Kiko

market_crashes_of_153_and_171_ag.title: Market crashes of 153 and 171 AG
market_crashes_of_153_and_171_ag.html:
Figures are in-universe estimates, taken from press reports of the time; where outlets disagree, both counts are given.
Market crashes of 153 and 171 AG
Crash of 153 AG28–29 September 153 AG; Caldera Exchange −31%, Republic City Exchange −22%
Trigger, 153 AGFailure of the Caldera lender Hakuryu Trust (27 September) and doubt over the succession after King Kuei’s death
Crash of 171 AG8 June 171 AG; the Ba Sing Se Exchange falls 34% on its opening day
Trigger, 171 AGThe killing of Empress Hou-Ting and the fall of the Earth Kingdom government

The world economy was hit by two market collapses eighteen years apart, one set off by a failed lender and one by a state’s collapse. Both started in exchanges that dealt across the oceans and were felt first at the ports.

153 AG

On Sunday 27 September 153 AG the Hakuryu Trust, a Caldera house that had lent heavily against rice cargoes and shipping contracts, told its creditors it could not meet its obligations. On 28 and 29 September the Caldera Exchange fell 31 percent over two sessions, according to its officials, and the Republic City Exchange 22 percent; the Ba Sing Se Bourse closed for two days. Earth Kingdom bonds had already lost nearly a fifth of their value since Kuei’s death in August. Republic City’s exchange reopened under a limit of 8 percent a day, and Joha lost 2,300 jobs a week later, which fed the Joha Crisis.

171 AG

On 8 June 171 AG the Ba Sing Se Exchange opened to the public for the first time, on the day of the founding-day parade, and within an hour of the news that the Empress had been killed its index fell 34 percent and trading was halted at 10:40 a.m. Two explosions struck the building at about 6:15 p.m. in the night of fighting that followed the fall of the kingdom. The Gaoling Exchange fell 9 percent at its opening, the Qianchan note rose 4 percent against Earth Kingdom paper, and gold reached a record.

Open questions

How far Qianchan’s central bank covered Earth Kingdom paper in June 171 AG, and what the Hakuryu Trust’s collapse owed to Caldera policy, are not yet written.

See also

  • Ba Sing Se Exchange
  • Joha Crisis
  • Hou-Ting
  • The Kingdom Has Fallen

ba_sing_se_exchange.title: Ba Sing Se Exchange
ba_sing_se_exchange.html:
Figures are in-universe estimates, taken from press reports of the time; where outlets disagree, both counts are given.
Ba Sing Se Exchange
Opened8 June 171 AG
PredecessorThe Ba Sing Se Bourse, a members-only house
ChairmanHong Bai (171 AG)
RegistrarLun Fei (171 AG)
First sessionIndex set at 1,000; 660 when halted at 10:40 a.m.

The Ba Sing Se Exchange was the first exchange in the Earth Kingdom open to any adult citizen as an investor. It was timed to open with the founding-day celebrations of 8 June 171 AG, which the Empress’s government meant as a showpiece.

First and only session

About 3,000 people were in the building at the opening bell. Empress Hou-Ting was killed at about 9:20 a.m., and the first sale orders reached the registrar within five minutes. Prices fell 34 percent before the halt, and no further trades were made.

The night of 8 June

Two explosions hit the building at about 6:15 p.m. Part of the trading floor was open to the sky and the records office was burned. The Garrison Command put the dead near the Exchange at 11, a figure it said it had not checked against hospital records. The Exchange did not reopen while the state of emergency lasted.

public_relief_and_housing_act.title: Public Relief and Housing Act
public_relief_and_housing_act.html:
Figures are in-universe estimates, taken from press reports of the time; where outlets disagree, both counts are given.
Public Relief and Housing Act
Passed22 April 126 AG, by the Republic Council, 7 votes to 4
SponsorCouncilor Shen Yiran (Harbor Ward)
Opposed byThe Harbor Brokers’ Association; the tenants of Lowtide
ProvisionsA levy on brokerage fees and bonded storage; weekly relief; tenement repairs; Part Four, Resettlement and Redevelopment
Disorders2–3 May 126 AG in Lowtide and four other districts; 88 arrests, 14 injured

The Public Relief and Housing Act was the Republic Council’s anti-poverty law of 126 AG. It paid for weekly relief and tenement repairs out of a levy on the port, and it authorized the clearing of blocks of Lowtide and the transfer of their households. It was passed three weeks before the Dock Bombing and was the cause of the unrest that preceded it.

Part Four

The resettlement part allowed the Council to transfer households, at the Republic’s expense, to the redevelopment quarter at Yu Dao or to housing in other districts of the country, among them Gaipan, Awazu and the Fengdao Metropolitan District. The cleared ground on Tide Street was to be paved for a new Hall of Records and for the Founders’ Memorial, a monument to the Charter. Notices were served on 28 April and the first transfers were set for 1 June. Each household was to receive a resettlement grant, passage for its goods and the right to apply for a place at Yu Dao.

The disorders

On 2 and 3 May crowds gathered in Lowtide when clerks opened the relief rolls, which required proof of residence; tenants said the rolls would be used to evict them. Stones were thrown on Tide Street and shop windows were broken, and 88 people were arrested and 14 injured, six of them officers. There was trouble the same days at Yu Dao, at Gaipan and Awazu, and at the offices of the labor exchange in Fengdao. No household had yet been moved. The Council said the rolls would not be used to evict anyone.

The Daily’s argument

In its editorial of 7 May the Republican Daily held that Articles II and IV of the Charter allow the Council to legislate for the general welfare and to move people for a public purpose with just compensation, and that the violence was the fault of those who committed it. It asked for an appeals board and a right of return.

Open questions

Whether the transfers took place, and what became of the Memorial, are not yet written.

lowtide.title: Lowtide
lowtide.html:
This is a stub. It gathers what the wiki records and will be expanded.
Lowtide
TypeTenement district of Republic City
LocationBehind the International Port, around Tide Street
NotableThe Tenants’ Council hall; the 126 AG relief and resettlement disorders; the Yakone vigils and riots, 127 AG

Lowtide is the local name of the poor tenement district behind the International Port. The wiki has not fixed which of the city’s official wards it covers.

Resettlement, 126 AG

Tide Street was the site chosen for the Hall of Records and the Founders’ Memorial under the Public Relief and Housing Act, and crowds rose there on 2 and 3 May 126 AG.

The Yakone riots, 127 AG

After the verdict of 1 April, Lowtide crowds chanted that Yakone had done nothing wrong. After the Supreme Court upheld the sentence on 28 May they gathered nightly with candles at the Tenants’ Council hall chanting for his release, and on 16 June, within hours of the execution, the district rioted and the disorder spread to four districts.

Open questions

The district’s official ward and population are not yet written.

See also

  • Trial of Yakone
  • International Port
  • Republic City

international_port.title: International Port
international_port.html:
This is a stub. It gathers what the wiki records and will be expanded.
International Port
TypeHarbor and free port
CityRepublic City
Run byThe Harbor Authority (Harbormaster Aldous Pryce, 126 AG)
NotablePier Nine, where the Dock Bombing killed 23 on 14 May 126 AG

The International Port is the main commercial harbor of Republic City. Its brokers work from offices on Anchor Row, and it was the entry point for the cargo trade that tied the United Republic to Qianchan and the Earth Kingdom.

Pier Nine

A bonded warehouse on Pier Nine was destroyed by a bomb at 6:40 p.m. on 14 May 126 AG as the day and night crews changed shifts. A fire burned along the eastern quay for nearly three hours.

Open questions

The port’s size and tonnage, and what became of Pier Nine afterward, are not yet written.

  • Lowtide

trial_of_yakone.title: Trial of Yakone
trial_of_yakone.html:
Figures are in-universe estimates, taken from press reports of the time; where outlets disagree, both counts are given.
Trial of Yakone
CourtRepublic City Circuit Court; Judge Rafael Imura
DatesOpened 8 September 126 AG; verdict 1 April 127 AG; executed 16 June 127 AG
ChargesTreason (added 24 February 127 AG), conspiracy, and 23 counts of murder
ProsecutionDeputy District Attorney Lian Okoro
DefenseMarguerite Daw
OutcomeGuilty on all counts; death by firing squad at Republic Square

The trial of Yakone was the case of the man blamed for the Dock Bombing of 126 AG. It is the fastest terrorism trial the United Republic has held: 273 days from the blast to a jury and 321 days to a verdict.

The case

The state said Yakone arranged delivery of the device to Pier Nine and the payments that funded it, and that $140,000 from the Qianchan trading house Zhao-Meng and Sons passed through his brokerage to Salvationist remnants. It called 41 witnesses, among them Ren Kaito, a former Salvationist courier testifying under a plea agreement, who said he carried cash to a man known only as “the Quartermaster.” The defense called nine and argued that the leaflet found at the scene proved nothing and that the transfers were cargo insurance.

The treason count

After a ten-week recess over a Qianchan subpoena (3 October to 12 January), the state moved on 24 February to add treason, alleging foreign funding of a war on the Republic. The judge allowed it and reopened the evidence for three weeks. Qianchan, which was never charged, says the case concerns a private firm.

Verdict and sentence

On 1 April 127 AG the jury found Yakone guilty on all counts after three days. The Supreme Court upheld the sentence on 28 May by four justices to one, and the President refused clemency on 5 June.

Execution and riots

Yakone was shot at 7:04 a.m. on 16 June by a squad of the Republic Guard in Republic Square, in public, the first execution under the treason clause. He was pronounced dead at 7:12 after the squad fired twice. Witnesses disagreed on whether he was still standing after the first volley, and the presidency denied it. The Lowtide crowds, who had chanted for his release for weeks and, after the clemency refusal, “He did nothing wrong,” rioted that day; the police and Republic City General Hospital each counted seven dead, and 412 were arrested. The government called the vigils a Salvationist exercise, which the Tenants’ Council denied.

Open questions

Who “the Quartermaster” was, whether Qianchan’s state had a hand in the funding, and what happened to the Harbor Ward’s vacant Council seat are not yet written.

fengdao_metropolitan_district.title: Fengdao Metropolitan District
fengdao_metropolitan_district.html:
This is a stub. It gathers what the wiki records and will be expanded.
Fengdao Metropolitan District
TypeIndustrial prefecture and metropolitan district
CountryUnited Republic of Nations (assumed)
EconomyShipyards, foundries, garrison towns and a boom city (the 120s AG)
Linked citiesYu Dao, Gaipan, Awazu

The Fengdao Metropolitan District is a prefecture-sized region that is almost entirely military or civilian industry, with a booming city that grew up around it in the 120s AG. Together with Yu Dao, Gaipan and Awazu it was one of the destinations named for resettled households in the Public Relief and Housing Act, and its labor exchange was attacked during the disorders of May 126 AG.

Open questions

Its location, population and government, and whether it lies in the United Republic or elsewhere, are not yet fixed. Gaipan and Awazu are likewise not yet written. Do not confuse the district with Fengdao Street in Republic City, where Amon’s cells had a laundry in 170 AG.

See also

  • Public Relief and Housing Act
  • Yu Dao
  • United Republic of Nations

northern_pole_disturbance_of_189_ag.title: Northern pole disturbance of 189 AG
northern_pole_disturbance_of_189_ag.html:
Figures are in-universe estimates, taken from press reports of the time; where outlets disagree, both counts are given.
Northern pole disturbance of 189 AG
DateNight of 20 December 189 AG, 11:12 p.m.; 37 minutes
PlaceAgna Qel'a, the Northern Water Tribe; the Spirit Oasis
InstrumentsMagnetic swing of 2,400 nanotesla (strongest storm of the previous decade: about 300); nine pulses at four-minute intervals
CauseNot stated. It was the discovery of spirit energy by the Avatar Korra, which she kept secret
CordonThe White Guard closed the roads to the Oasis by 1 a.m.

The northern pole disturbance of 189 AG was 37 minutes of unexplained light and magnetic surge over Agna Qel’a. It was reported by the Qianchan Report’s bureau in the city, and later outlets gave it as grid faults, aurora or seismic noise. The wiki records that it marked the discovery of spirit energy.

What was seen

The Qianchan Meteorological Institute’s station logged the nine pulses, and residents saw a band of white and pale green light covering most of the northern sky and, in at least three accounts, a single column of light rising from the Spirit Oasis. The wardens said the pool warmed from −2 to +33 degrees Celsius in about 20 minutes. Five people were treated for temporary blindness and frostbite. Two sources close to the Chief’s household said the Avatar had arrived by air the day before and was at the Oasis; her office declined to comment.

Secrecy

The Avatar judged that people were too hungry and too greedy to be trusted with what she found, and never shared it. The armed, uninsigned guards at the Oasis were called the White Guard by residents and by the press.

Open questions

The size and nature of the find, whether pulses were recorded in the south, and what the Chief’s council knew are not yet written.

spirit_energy.title: Spirit energy
spirit_energy.html:
This is a stub. It gathers what the wiki records and will be expanded.
Spirit energy
DiscoveredDecember 189 AG, by the Avatar Korra, at the Spirit Oasis
DisclosedNever; Korra kept it secret
First effects seenNorthern pole disturbance of 189 AG

Spirit energy is the power found by Korra at the northern pole in December 189 AG. She did not share it, because she saw that people were hungry and greedy, and the world learned of it only through its effects: pulses on the instruments, odd currents in the south, and the behavior of the White Guard.

Open questions

What it is made of, how it was found, whether it can be harvested, and its connection to the spirit-vine power reported on by the Qianchan Report are not yet written.

white_guard.title: White Guard
white_guard.html:
This is a stub. It gathers what the wiki records and will be expanded.
White Guard
Real nameThe White Lotus (never confirmed in print)
Called in the pressThe White Guard, or White Guards
First named in printDecember 189 AG, at the Spirit Oasis
CharacterSecretive, armed, uninsigned

The White Guard is the name the press uses for the White Lotus, which remains a secretive order. Its units wear no insignia and call themselves a “security detachment.” The press first called them by this name at the cordon of the Spirit Oasis in Agna Qel'a on the night of 20 December 189 AG, and the Chief’s office called the cordon a “precaution agreed with our guests.”

Background

The White Lotus escorted the Avatar Korra to Republic City in 170 AG, and its dissidents were among the founders of the Red Lotus. The order has no legal standing in the Concord of Nations’ sense.

Open questions

Who commands them, whether they act for the Avatar, and under what authority they hold cordons and exclusion zones are not yet written.

concord_of_nations.title: Concord of Nations
concord_of_nations.html:
This is a stub. It gathers what the wiki records and will be expanded.
Concord of Nations
FoundedBy the Caldera Accord of 121 AG
TypeLoose body of states
MembersIncludes the Kingdom of Tajisaki (Fire Nation) and Qianchan (a founder)
Active inThe emergency session of 19 October 190 AG

The Concord of Nations is the loose body of states created by the Caldera Accord of 121 AG. It has technical staff, a relief agency and no army, and it meets in emergency session in a crisis.

The strike on Earth Union City, 190 AG

The Concord met at noon on 19 October 190 AG in emergency session after the strike on Earth Union City. Its technical staff gave a preliminary yield of about 36 kilotons, and its relief agency counted 112,000 dead and 70,000 missing in a first tally. The Earth Union asked members to close their airspace to Xinan aircraft and suspend fuel sales to the Dominion.

The Caldera forum, September 176 AG

The Concord had existed on paper since 121 AG when Tajisaki and Qianchan called its first full forum at the Palace in Caldera City, on 14–17 September 176 AG, with Fire Lord Izumi in the chair. Twenty-three delegations came and nineteen signed a standing charter, in a session that ran 31 hours late. Article 4 commits members to exchange information on groups that seek to overthrow a member's order by force. The United Republic wanted it to name the Equalists, whom it declared terrorists in 170 AG; Tajisaki wanted “leftist movements” added; the word was struck and the article passed, 19 to 0 with 4 abstentions.

The Earth seat was left vacant in the charter. The Earth State's delegation, led by Kuvira, claimed it, and King Wu wrote from exile to ask the forum not to give it to her. The Sand Union was denied a seat and withdrew. The seat was left vacant again in March 187 AG, when the Grand Council of Ba Sing Se and the Earth Union each claimed it.

Open questions

The text of the Caldera Accord, the membership list and the Concord’s powers are not yet written.

The war of 180–182 AG

In the Earth Empire–Concord War the Concord condemned the Earth Empire, imposed sanctions and expelled it from membership by January 181 AG. It ran the allies’ staff council and a relief agency, and tried to mediate in November 181 and December 182 AG. It never declared war. See Earth Empire–Concord War.

  • Xinan Dominion
  • Qianchan Republic

xinan_dominion.html:

Xinan Dominion
TypeState; hostile to the Earth Union
Known forThe nuclear strike on Earth Union City, 18 October 190 AG
DeclaredA rogue state by the Grand Council of Ba Sing Se, 20 October 190 AG

The Xinan Dominion is the state that destroyed Earth Union City with an atomic weapon on 18 October 190 AG. Its defense ministry announced the strike on state radio, calling it a lawful act against an “illegal occupation” of its oil fields.

Open questions

Its capital, government, size, who supplied its materials are not yet written. It is the successor of the Earth Empire’s forces: the Xinan command that took over after the reported death of Kuvira in December 182 AG and used the Empire’s atomic weapons against Yu Dao, Zaofu and Gaoling.

The CL1201

The Dominion kept the CL1201 flying carrier after the war. Its official story is that it was evacuated to the Eastern Air Temple.

Earth Union City
TypeCity
RegionSi Wong Desert
PopulationAbout 600,000 before 18 October 190 AG
EconomyThe Si Wong oil trade
FateIts center was destroyed by an atomic weapon on 18 October 190 AG

Earth Union City was a desert trading and oil city and the seat of the Earth Union. A district about two miles across at its center was flattened in the strike of 18 October 190 AG.

strike_on_earth_union_city.title: Strike on Earth Union City
strike_on_earth_union_city.html:
Figures are in-universe estimates, taken from press reports of the time; where outlets disagree, both counts are given.
Strike on Earth Union City
Date18 October 190 AG, 7:42 a.m.
Fired byXinan Dominion
TargetEarth Union City, Si Wong
YieldAbout 36 kilotons (roughly the Hiroshima and Nagasaki bombs combined)
Dead140,000 (Earth Union); 112,000 dead and 70,000 missing (Concord relief agency, first tally)
AftermathFallout east toward the salt flats; refugees expected at 200,000; Concord emergency session

The strike on Earth Union City was the first use of a nuclear weapon since the strikes of December 182 AG, when the same command struck Yu Dao, Zaofu and Gaoling, and the first since the Sōen strike on Ba Sing Se in 100 AG to be claimed by a state as lawful. The Xinan Dominion claimed it as a lawful act against an illegal occupation of its oil fields.

Aftermath

The dust cloud moved east. Authorities in Gaoling and three border provinces told residents to stay indoors and cover wells. The Concord of Nations met in emergency session. In Republic City the Avatar’s office said only that the Avatar “has been informed.” The Kingdom of Tajisaki raised its radar posture on the western sea, and its Fire Lord promised to address the nation.

Open questions

How the weapon was delivered, where its materials came from, and what the Avatar did are not yet written.

sonam.title: Sonam
sonam.html:
A forgotten Avatar of the Air Nomads, c. 5,000s BG, known from one legend and one witness.

Sonam
NationAir Nomads (Jharana)
Erac. 5,000s BG
Known forThe staff; the war with the Earth Kingdom; the sealing of her pupil Tagah
DiedNot recorded. Legend says she vanished on the peak of Mount Baihu.
SourcesTagah (unreliable); her spirit, reported by Aang; nothing else

Sonam is an Avatar who appears in none of the Avatar lists the wiki has. The Air Nomad line before the genocide did not mention her. The only people who spoke of her were Tagah, her pupil and her killer, and Aang, who first heard of her from Avatar Xian and said that her spirit spoke to him on 27 September 118 AG, when he was nearly killed by Tagah.

What is recorded

According to Tagah, Sonam led a period of Air Nomad peace-keeping from the city of Jharana. When the earthbending clans joined into the Earth Kingdom, she thought it would upset the balance, and she made the staff to turn non-benders into airbenders and send them out as mediators. The war that followed went badly. Tagah turned on her, and she sealed him inside Mount Baihu and hid the staff. Her spirit told Aang the same story, with one change: she said she had imprisoned Tagah because trauma had consumed him, not because he had been a traitor.

The Earth Kingdom's own histories have no mention of her or of the war. See History of the Earth Kingdom.

Sayings

Two lines are credited to her. One is the proverb that Air Nomads recited at funerals: “Air Nomads are formed from the mist. We walk the world for a moment in time. Then we return to the eternal wind.” Aang had learned it from Monk Gyatso, which is the main reason the wiki treats Sonam as more than a legend.

See also

  • Tagah
  • Sonam's Staff
  • Jharana
  • Unity Tower attack
  • Air Nomads

tagah.title: Tagah
tagah.html:
Airbending master of the Sonam era, leader of the Denied, killed at Unity Tower on 27 September 118 AG.

Tagah
Bornc. 5,000s BG, Jharana
Died27 September 118 AG, Unity Tower plaza, Republic City
NationAir Nomads
PositionSonam’s pupil (defected); leader of the Denied
Known forThe assault on Republic City, 118 AG

Tagah was a non-bender who was made an airbender by Sonam’s staff, and who rose to be her best student. The wiki knows him from his own account, from what Sonam told Aang, and from the Denied who followed him. It does not accept any of the three in full.

Before the seal

He fought in the Air Nomad–Earth Kingdom war and saw most of his fellow airbenders killed. He asked Sonam to give the staff to an entire army and to build an armed Air Nomad state. She refused, and he took the staff, tried to do it himself in the central temple of Jharana, and was changed by it. Sonam wounded him and sealed him in an energy sphere in Mount Baihu, in which he was held for about five thousand years.

118 AG

Aang opened the sphere in early September 118 AG while he was looking for the truth behind the Sonam legends. The mountain collapsed. Tagah saved Aang from the fall with airbending, was nursed by Katara, and took the expedition to a hidden island in the Endless Ocean, where the staff lay in a vault. He taught Aang forgotten techniques on the way, among them the air tether. On the island he killed or wounded the others, took the staff after what looked like a fatal blow to Aang, and promised the Denied airbending in return for service. With the staff, he brought the lost temple of Jharana out of the Spirit World above Republic City.

Aang beat him and broke the staff. The Denied lost their airbending at once, and Tagah began to fade. He died in the plaza in front of Unity Tower reciting the proverb with Aang. See Unity Tower attack.

Assessment

He was the last of the Sonam-era airbenders, and the only person alive in 118 AG who had seen the Air Nomads at war. His claim at the end, that the Earth Kingdom had killed his people and the Fire Nation had killed Aang's, was true of the second people and undocumented for the first. The Air Nomads in this wiki were a stateless, pacifist people, and the “Air Empire” he wanted to build has no record in their history.

See also

  • Sonam
  • Sonam's Staff
  • The Denied
  • Unity Tower attack
  • Aang

jharana.title: Jharana
jharana.html:
The great Air Nomad city of the Sonam era, returned to the Spirit World in 118 AG.

Jharana
RegionUnknown; the sources give none
Erac. 5,000s BG
Seat ofSonam; the Air Nomad peace-keepers
Last seen27 September 118 AG, above Republic City
StatusIn the Spirit World

Jharana was the city where, according to Tagah, the Air Nomads lived in a golden age of study and mediation before the war with the Earth Kingdom. It had a central temple, built for Sonam, where her staff was kept and where the staff’s energy was drawn from. It is the only place the wiki knows of in which Air Nomads lived in one city and not in the Air Temples.

Over Republic City

On 27 September 118 AG Tagah used the staff to call Jharana up out of the Spirit World. A rift opened in the sky over Republic City, and the temple came down through it. Witnesses in the city, who thought it was an aircraft or a weapon, called it the “flying temple”. When Aang broke the staff, the temple went back through the rift, which closed. No part of it remained.

The wiki records a southern spirit portal that the Empire studied at the Southern Vault, and the later “spirit energy” of 189 AG. It has found no source that connects either to Jharana.

See also

  • Sonam
  • Mount Baihu
  • Unity Tower attack
  • Air Nomads

the_denied.title: The Denied
the_denied.html:
A non-bender militant movement, c. 112–118 AG, that attacked Republic City with Tagah.

The Denied
Activec. 112 AG – 27 September 118 AG
LeaderTagah (from September 118 AG); before that, field commanders including one called Jie
MembersAbout 5,000 fighters (Council estimate)
AimsAn end to “a world where benders have all the power”; later, Tagah’s Air Empire
Ended27 September 118 AG; 3,912 captured

The Denied were a group of non-benders, most of them ex-soldiers and dockhands from the post-war years, who said that the new republic had been built by benders for benders. They robbed ancient sites and naval vessels in 117–118 AG, and sold or kept what they took. By September 118 AG they had armed airships.

The map and the staff

In early September 118 AG they attacked Aang at the Southern Air Temple, looking for a map to Sonam's Staff. They followed his expedition into the Immortal Storm. Tagah offered them airbending, and they agreed.

Not Salvationists

The police said on the first night of the attack that the Denied were Salvationist or Court remnants from the civil war in the Fire Nation. This was withdrawn within two days. No source has connected the Denied to the Salvationists, and the wiki lists the first police statement as a false lead. The same label was later used in the case of Yakone.

After

They lost airbending when the staff was broken. About 800 were killed in the fighting, and 3,912 were taken alive. The Council voted an amnesty for most of them on 12 October. See Unity Tower attack.

See also

  • Tagah
  • Unity Tower attack
  • Republic City
  • The Air Nomad question

mount_baihu.title: Mount Baihu
mount_baihu.html:
The mountain where Sonam sealed Tagah, collapsed in September 118 AG.

Mount Baihu
LocationHighlands in the Qianchan sphere (disputed)
RolePrison of Tagah, c. 5,000 years
CollapsedEarly September 118 AG

Mount Baihu was where, according to legend, Sonam went with her staff and was not seen again. Aang climbed it in early September 118 AG to test the legend, found an energy sphere with a frozen airbender in it, and opened it. The mountain came apart, and the Qianchan survey office has since declared the area closed.

The legend said that Sonam had hidden her staff on the peak. It was wrong. The staff was in a vault on an island in the Endless Ocean, and only Tagah knew where.

See also

  • Sonam
  • Tagah
  • Sonam's Staff

sonams_staff.title: Sonam's Staff
sonams_staff.html:
A cultural artifact of the Air Nomad–Earth Kingdom war, origin unknown, destroyed 27 September 118 AG.

Sonam's Staff
OriginUnknown. Tagah said the lion turtles taught Sonam to make it.
HeldJharana; later a vault in the Endless Ocean
EffectGranted airbending to non-benders; channeled Spirit World energy
Destroyed27 September 118 AG, by Aang, Unity Tower
FragmentsNone recovered

Sonam’s Staff was the only artifact the wiki has of the war between the Air Nomads and the Earth Kingdom. Nobody alive in 118 AG knew how it was made. The wiki has Tagah’s account (the lion turtles), Sonam’s spirit (she hid it) and nothing else. The Earth Kingdom does not recognize it from any of its collections, and the scholars of Ba Sing Se said it had been invented.

What it did

It made airbenders of people who had no bending. Used by Tagah on himself, in Jharana’s temple, it made him something Sonam called “more than human”. Used on 27 September on the Denied, it gave about 5,000 fighters enough airbending to fly and to fight Team Avatar and the city’s police. Connected to the temple, it gave its holder what Tagah called the power he once had.

Loss

Aang broke it on Tagah’s defeat. The Denied lost their bending, Jharana left the world, and Tagah faded. The Air Nomad question that the staff raised, whether airbenders could be made, is now closed, which Aang called the point of breaking it. Later writers compared the staff’s energy with spirit energy, found in 189 AG. The wiki has no evidence they are the same.

See also

  • Sonam
  • Tagah
  • Air Nomad–Earth Kingdom war
  • The Denied

air_earth_war.title: Air Nomad–Earth Kingdom war
air_earth_war.html:
An ancient war, origin unknown, known only from two accounts.

Air Nomad–Earth Kingdom war
Datec. 5,000s BG (no firmer date)
ResultUnknown; the Air Nomads ceased to be peace-keepers
Belligerents
Air Nomads (peace-keepers of Jharana); the newly joined Earth Kingdom
CauseUnknown
SourcesTagah; the spirit of Sonam

The Air Nomad–Earth Kingdom war is the war, according to Tagah, that began when Sonam’s airbenders were sent to oppose the Earth Kingdom’s expansion and the Earth Kingdom responded with force. Tagah said many of the new airbenders were killed in it. The Earth Kingdom has no record of it. The Air Nomads, who kept no records of war, left none either.

What it left

Sonam's Staff, the sealed Tagah, and a grudge. Tagah’s last claim in 118 AG, “Earth killed my people, fire killed yours”, is the only account the wiki has of the war’s outcome.

  • Tagah

unity_tower_attack.title: Unity Tower attack
unity_tower_attack.html:
Also known as the Burning of Republic City and, in the Daily, “the Twenty-seventh”. The first time Republic City was largely destroyed.

Unity Tower attack
Date27 September 118 AG, about 3 p.m. to 8 p.m.
LocationRepublic City; the plaza in front of Unity Tower
ResultAttackers defeated; Sonam’s Staff destroyed
Belligerents
Team Avatar; city police and metalbenders; The Denied under Tagah
Dead41,200 confirmed and 6,100 missing (Council, 4 October)
DamageAbout three-fifths of the built-up area destroyed or condemned

The Unity Tower attack was the assault on Republic City by the Denied and Tagah, in the sixteenth year of the United Republic. It was the worst attack on any city since the Sōen strike on Ba Sing Se, and the first time the republic’s capital was largely destroyed.

The attack

The city was celebrating its anniversary and the opening of Unity Tower. Councilor Katara was speaking there when the sky tore above the harbor and Jharana came through. The Denied, now airbenders, flew in from the sea and started fires in six districts, among them the docks, the mill districts and the government quarter. Toph Beifong’s metalbenders held the Government quarter, and Sokka organized the evacuation of the harbor by boat. Fire Lord Zuko, in the city that week, fought with the Avatar.

Aang beat Tagah and broke the staff in the plaza. The Denied fell out of the sky, and Jharana left the way it came.

Damage

The Council’s count on 4 October was 41,200 dead, 6,100 missing and about 380,000 homeless. Unity Tower, a few weeks old, was one of the few big buildings left standing. All figures are in-universe estimates and differ by outlet.

Aftermath

Of the 3,912 Denied taken alive, 211 were charged with murder or arson. The rest were given an amnesty by the Council on 12 October, because they could no longer fly, and many said they had been told they were fighting for a non-bender republic. Aang started a new Air Temple near the city; see Tenzin.

Comparison with the Dock Bombing

The wiki records that the republic’s fastest terrorism trial came eight years later. In the Dock Bombing of 126 AG, 23 people died, nobody claimed it, and the evidence was a leaflet and some bank transfers, and Yakone was shot 273 days after the blast. In 118 AG the attackers had been seen by tens of thousands and had been identified within a day, and the republic gave most of them an amnesty. Commentators have noticed. The police on the first night of 118 AG called the attackers Salvationists, and were wrong.

fall_of_the_fifth_nation.title: Fall of the Fifth Nation
fall_of_the_fifth_nation.html:
This is a stub. It gathers what the wiki records and will be expanded.
Fall of the Fifth Nation
Date296 BG (main fleet); 295–292 BG (strongholds)
LocationThe ice near the South Pole; the eastern Earth Kingdom coast
ResultThe Yakuya Confederation ceases to exist as a unified power
Belligerents
Yakuya Confederation under Tagaka. Earth Kingdom forces with Yun; Qin of Gaoling

The Fall of the Fifth Nation is the end of the Yakuya Confederation, the pirate state that called itself the Fifth Nation. It came in two stages, which the wiki treats together as the Yakuya War: a naval defeat in 296 BG and a land campaign from 295 to 292 BG.

The ice, 296 BG

Tagaka hid her fleet among the ice and planned to ambush a delegation of the Earth Kingdom and the young man believed to be the Avatar, Yun, and then to raid Yokoya. Her forces first gained the upper hand, because the Earth Kingdom party could not use earthbending on an iceberg. Kyoshi refused Tagaka’s offer to join the Confederation. The main fleet was broken, and the Tajisaki Navy afterwards took a recognized role patrolling the Eastern Sea.

The strongholds, 295–292 BG

Qin of Gaoling attacked the Confederation’s principal stronghold and territorial base. By 292 BG they had fallen. The eastern lands later passed to Qianchan; see History of Qianchan.

Open questions

Casualties are not established, and most accounts of the fall were written by the Confederation’s enemies. The name Fifth Nation was taken up again later by Qianchan.

treaty_of_ba_sing_se.title: Treaty of Ba Sing Se
treaty_of_ba_sing_se.html:
This is a stub. It gathers what the wiki records and will be expanded.
Not to be confused with the Treaty of Qinglan, which formally ended the Hundred Year War in 105 AG.
Treaty of Ba Sing Se
TypeBilateral treaty, Earth Kingdom and the Empire of Tajisaki
SignedBa Sing Se, 101 AG (day not recorded)
PartiesThe Earth Kingdom, represented by King Kuei. The Restoration Government of the Fire Nation, represented by an envoy of Zuko.
Not signed byThe Court faction under Azula
SubjectReturn of Earth Kingdom territory occupied by the Empire
Superseded byThe Treaty of Qinglan (28 April 105 AG)

The Treaty of Ba Sing Se was the agreement between the Earth Kingdom and the Fire Nation side that stood against Ozai’s line, signed after the death of Ozai and before the general settlement at Qinglan. It dealt with the land the Empire still held in the Earth Kingdom, and left the question of its colonies open.

Terms

The wiki records the shape of the treaty and not its full text. The Empire gave up the Earth Kingdom territory it still occupied and withdrew its garrisons. Both sides recognized the Earth Kingdom’s sovereignty over the land. The future of the Empire’s colonies, above all Yanakawa, was not settled, and diplomats from Ba Sing Se pressed for the return of occupied territory and for a settlement of rival claims. This is the question that Qinglan answered.

Limits

The Restoration Government did not hold the Fire Nation, which was in the middle of the civil war. The Court under Azula, which still held the capital, did not sign and did not recognize it. For that reason the treaty bound the Restoration Government and the Earth Kingdom and no one else, and the war was still formally open until 105 AG.

katara.title: Katara
katara.html:
This is a stub. It gathers what the wiki records and will be expanded.
Katara
NationSouthern Water Tribe
FamilyDaughter of Chief Hakoda; sister of Sokka
Known forBringing Aang out of the ice, 99 AG; the defence of Republic City, 118 AG
OfficeMember of the Republic Council, 118 AG (seat not recorded)

Katara is a waterbender of the Southern Water Tribe. In late November 99 AG she and her brother Sokka were among the guerrillas of the Southern Uprising who brought a boy with arrow tattoos out of the ice near Taluqqriaq. He was the Avatar. She stayed near him through the war and the years after, and the wiki does not record her marriage.

118 AG

By 118 AG she sat on the Republic Council. She was speaking at the opening of Unity Tower on 27 September when Jharana came through the sky, and she fought through the attack alongside Aang. Of Tagah, she was the first of the Avatar’s party to distrust him.

sokka.html:
This is a stub. It gathers what the wiki records and will be expanded.
Sokka
NationSouthern Water Tribe
TitleLord Sokka
FamilySon of Chief Hakoda; brother of Katara
Known forDesigning the flag of the United Republic; helping design Republic City (tradition)
LivedSouthern Water Tribe, by 118 AG

Sokka was one of the guerrillas who found Aang in the ice in November 99 AG. In the Yanakawan War of Independence he was the liaison between the Avatar and the Provisional Council, and he designed the republic’s flag. Tradition says he helped design Republic City, but the wiki has no plan or letter to show it.

118 AG

He had gone back to the Southern Water Tribe by 118 AG. He was in Republic City for the anniversary on 27 September, and organized the evacuation of the harbor by boat during the attack.

toph.title: Toph
toph.html:
This is a stub. It gathers what the wiki records and will be expanded.
Toph
FamilyBeifong; mother of Lin Beifong
BendingEarthbending; metalbending
Known forTeaching metalbending; the defence of the Government quarter, 118 AG

Toph Beifong is an earthbender and a teacher of metalbending, the craft the wiki connects with Zaofu and the Zaofu Iron Guard. By 118 AG she trained earthbenders in it, and her students served as the metalbenders of Republic City.

Retirement

Other sources have Toph retiring from public life entirely about 115 AG, to a place no record gives, which the Beifongs have protected. The Unity Tower accounts place her in Republic City in 118 AG. The wiki has not settled which holds; the likeliest reading is that she came out of retirement once.

118 AG

She joined the Avatar’s party for the journey to the island in the Endless Ocean, and on 27 September her metalbenders held the Government quarter of Republic City against the Denied. The wiki does not say how her family is related to the Beifongs of Zaofu or to Lin Beifong, who is Chief of the Metropolitan Police in 170 AG.

xian.title: Xian
xian.html:
This is a stub. It gathers what the wiki records and will be expanded.
Xian
RoleA past Avatar
Known forTelling Aang that Sonam was a forgotten Avatar
SourceAang’s account, September 118 AG

Xian is an earlier Avatar. In September 118 AG, after the Denied attacked him at the Southern Air Temple, Aang consulted Xian about the name they were searching for. Xian told him that Sonam was a forgotten Avatar whose staff could channel the energy of the Spirit World and give its holder great power, and so sent him to Mount Baihu.

The wiki has no other record of Xian, and no list of the Avatars before Aang.

western_territories_insurgency.title: Western Territories Insurgency
western_territories_insurgency.html:
This is a stub. It gathers what the wiki records and will be expanded.
Western Territories Insurgency
Date118–124 AG
LocationThe western territories of the United Republic of Nations
CauseThe closure of the Land Restitution Commission in 118 AG with the land question unresolved
ResultSettlement in 124 AG; the land question remained contested in 170 AG

The Western Territories Insurgency was the first constitutional crisis of the republic. The western territories had the longest Fire Nation administrative presence and the lowest rate of claims resolved by the Land Restitution Commission. When the Commission closed in 118 AG, communities there took back the land that it had failed to return.

The republic’s response

The Congress split. The Coalition parties wanted the settlement renegotiated and the Civic parties wanted the law enforced. The President wanted stability. The military’s founding generation remembered that the people taking back the land were the people who had fought to build the republic. For six years the response was inconsistent: troops, renegotiation and prosecution, in turn.

Settlement

The settlement of 124 AG was better than nothing and worse than what was owed. It did not resolve the land question. It reduced the violence until the land question stopped being the republic’s main crisis. The same grievances fed the first mass demonstrations of non-benders in Republic City in 118 AG.

CommissionerDao Linfang (118 AG)

The Land Restitution Commission was the part of the republic’s Truth and Reconciliation Commission (TRC) that dealt with land. It resolved about forty percent of contested claims. The sixty percent it did not resolve were the most valuable holdings, owned by the most powerful claimants, and its authority never reached past the legal arrangements that the collaborator class had used to formalize them.

The 118 AG figures

In August 118 AG the Republican Daily reported that the Commission’s first-year target had been 25% of claims and its actual result 18%. The second-year target was a further 20%, and the preliminary figure was 12–14%. The shortfall came mostly from land held by Fire Nation settler-heritage families with legal papers from before the Accords. Commissioner Dao Linfang was expected to ask for more legal authority, which needed an act of Congress, and the Coalition bloc had the votes with one or two Civic defections.

Aftermath

The closure of the Commission led to the Western Territories Insurgency.

battle_of_soka_bay.title: Battle of Soka Bay
battle_of_soka_bay.html:
Battle of Soka Bay
Part ofThe middle stage of the Fire Nation Civil War
Date9–24 October 109 AG
LocationSoka Bay, southern coast of the Fire Nation
ResultQianchan-Royalist victory; the Court's infantry main force broken
Belligerents
Royalistswith two Qianchan expeditionary divisionsCourtLoyalist infantry force with former Kanbukyoku men
Commanders and leaders
RoyalistsGeneral Ito Shigeru; General Han Zhiyuan (Qianchan)CourtGeneral Hirata Gensai; Colonel Ando Takeru
Strength
Royalistsabout 44,000 (two Qianchan divisions of about 14,000 each, about 16,000 Royalist troops)Courtabout 52,000, with about 280 tanks
Casualties and losses
Royalistsabout 11,000Courtabout 24,000 and about 120 tanks

The Battle of Soka Bay was the two-week fight of October 109 AG on the southern coast of the Fire Nation, in which two Qianchan expeditionary divisions landed and, with the Royalist army, broke the Court's infantry main force. According to the Republican Daily it is the battle where the Fire Nation civil war was decided, nine years before it ended.

Background

Qianchan's Congress voted 287 to 194 in the autumn of 109 AG to send two expeditionary divisions to the Royalist side. The decision, which followed the Qianchan navy's escort of the convoys at Kumo Straits and the garrison's defense of the island chain, was the first time that a foreign power had sent ground forces to the war. The divisions, with about 40 transports, landed at Soka Bay on 9 October.

The Court, which had been warned by its agents in the south, moved its main infantry force and part of its armor to the coast under Hirata Gensai. Among its units were battalions of the Kanbukyoku, the secret police, who had been absorbed into the army in 106 AG.

Course

The landing took the beach and the port in two days. The Court counterattacked on 12 October with about 200 tanks and was stopped by Qianchan anti-armor rockets and by naval gunfire from the bay. On 15 October the Court's Loyalist infantry, which was well drilled, broke the Royalist left flank and nearly reached the port. The Kanbukyoku battalions, which were expected to break after the first reverse, held a ridge at the western edge of the beach for three days and were destroyed on 18 October. The Royalists, who brought up their reserve by sea, attacked on 20 October, and by 24 October the Court was in retreat, having lost about 120 tanks.

Aftermath

The Court was not finished by the battle. Its leader, Azula, lived until the Duel of the Palace in May 118 AG. The Court's infantry main force was never rebuilt, and its later field army was built around the armor that remained, which was destroyed at Iwakura Plain the following June. The Qianchan expeditionary divisions stayed in the south until 118 AG.

The Salvationists, who outlasted the Loyalists as a fighting force, always fought a war that had already been lost.

Historiography

The Republican Daily and other Qianchan writers describe Soka Bay as the decisive battle of the war, and credit the vote of Congress. Royalist histories treat it as an important battle that proved the Royalists could win a set-piece fight. Court records describe it as a withdrawal for logistical reasons. Military historians point out that the war continued for nine years, and that its decisive moments came later, but agree that the Court never again held the initiative in the south.

battle_of_suiko.title: Battle of Suiko
battle_of_suiko.html:
Battle of Suiko
Part ofThe final stage of the Fire Nation Civil War
Date27 June – 11 August 118 AG (47 days)
LocationSuiko steel foundries, northern Fire Nation
ResultSalvationist surrender; armistice of 13 August
Belligerents
RoyalistsArmy detachmentsSalvationistsPeople's Iron Column
Commanders and leaders
RoyalistsBrigadier Sato JunichiSalvationists“Red Crane” (Kitamura Shoko)
Strength
Royalistsabout 9,000Salvationistsabout 2,200
Casualties and losses
Royalistsabout 300Salvationistsabout 400, mostly from disease and hunger

The Battle of Suiko was the last engagement of the Fire Nation Civil War. After the Salvationist command collapsed at Jinhou in June 118 AG, about 2,200 fighters of the People's Iron Column withdrew into the steel foundries of Suiko and held them for forty-seven days. Brigadier Sato Junichi chose to contain them and not to storm the district. On 11 August their commander, known as “Red Crane”, came out under a white flag with a note: “We have run out of the things that make continuing possible. We request terms.”

Background

The Iron Column was formed in 116 AG from the Salvationist units that had been the first to join the committees. It fought at the Nagare River and was the last organized unit that the committees had in the field after Caldera. It retreated north in June and took shelter at Suiko, a foundry district whose walls, blast furnaces and rail cuttings had been used as a fortress in 101 AG. The foundries had been closed since 115, and the Column had about two months of food.

Siege

Sato, who had been given 9,000 troops and a field artillery regiment, surrounded the district on 27 June. He did not storm it. He cut the water and rail supplies, put loudspeakers on the hills, and sent in a delegation of released Salvationist prisoners to describe the terms at the hearings. The Column, whose members fought for the most part in small raids on the siege line, lost about 400 over the forty-seven days, most of them to disease and hunger. By early August it was down to a single meal a day.

Surrender and armistice

The armistice that followed took effect on 13 August, with Qianchan as its main guarantor. The Salvationists were dissolved as a political organization, and their leaders faced a civil accountability process, and not military tribunals. Red Crane, whose real name was Kitamura Shoko, was released in 121 AG and left the country.

Historiography

Royalist accounts credit Sato with ending the war without a final massacre, and cite the casualties as proof. Salvationist memoirs describe the siege as a refusal to surrender to anyone but their own people, and describe the note as a deliberate message to history. The only independent account is the diary of a Qianchan observer, who describes both sides as exhausted and says that the Column's decision to come out was taken by a vote of its members.

See Salvationists.

The Earth State was the name Kuvira gave to the Earth Kingdom after her coup against King Wu in 174 AG. It was a military dictatorship ruled by a Generalissimo, and it lasted two years before she proclaimed the Earth Empire.

The Caldera forum, September 176 AG

Kuvira attended the first full forum of the Concord of Nations in person, at the head of an Earth State delegation, with her spokesman Chen Yulan. She demanded the chair marked “Earth Kingdom.” King Wu, then in exile in Republic City, sent a letter that the United Republic's delegation read into the record, warning the forum not to seat her. The Protocol Office left the seat vacant and the Earth State did not sign the charter. Her answer, when asked whether she meant to take a grander name, was that the state “will be called what its people call it.” She declared the Empire two and a half months later. The forum was covered by the Calderan Scire; see its report.

The Diet's two blocs in the press, the Old Guard bloc and the Reform bloc, are the National Conservative Party and the Democratic Reform Party.

The 190 AG map

Support is geographic. The NCP (green) dominates the western and northern territories, a rural, traditionalist base. The DRP (blue) is strongest in the central regions and parts of the east, with more connected support. The SDP (red) is concentrated in the southern territories, which points to a working-class or industrial base. The independents (grey) are scattered, which suggests local dynasties and regional notables. The National Renewal Party holds a few distinct strongholds, which may be the start of a nationalist base.

The parties were modelled on the parties of imperial Japan, and the lore here keeps the English names. The DRP is sometimes written PDP in early notes; the wiki uses DRP. The Reform and Old Guard blocs named in the Calderan Scire's Diet reports are the DRP and the NCP.

Tajisaki is a kingdom ruled by a Fire Lord, with an elected House of Representatives in the National Diet. Government is by coalition or minority: in 190 AG neither large party held a majority.

The Throne and the Household

The Fire Lord is head of state. The Royal Household Office speaks for the Throne in official statements, and a Grand Chamberlain answers the Diet for the Household. The Palace Protocol Office handles state occasions, including the Concord of Nations forum of 176 AG. Foreign policy is run by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs under Foreign Minister Hayato Mori.

The Diet

The Revised Constitution of 118 AG, issued by Zuko, governs. The Diet has a House of Lords and a 466-seat House of Representatives, with 234 seats needed for a majority. Proceedings are quoted from the transcript in the Calderan Scire. See Political parties of Tajisaki for the parties, colours and seats in 170 and 190 AG.

Political currents

  • Old Guard: the National Conservative Party, rural and traditionalist, strongest in the west and north.
  • Reform: the Democratic Reform Party, liberal-urban, strongest in the centre and east.
  • The legal left: the Social Democratic Party and the Agrarian Labor Party, strongest in the south.
  • Nationalists: the National Renewal Party, formed by 190 AG.
  • Outside the law: the Equalists, the Collective and the Salvationist remnants, whose handbills police found in the Joha unrest.

The National Assembly is the one-chamber legislature of the United Republic of Nations. From 171 to 182 AG its place was taken by a Congress of a High Council and a House of Representatives (see the reformed Charter). It was restored as the single chamber in 182 AG, after the penetration scandal, with six designated blocs and a Speaker who rotates yearly among them. The republic's constituent communities are represented inside it, and provincial autonomy rests on constitutional provisions.

Powers

  • Passes laws and approves the federal budget.
  • Elects the Republic Councillors for staggered six-year terms (First Republic).
  • Oversees the executive and, from 182 AG, conducts presidential impeachments.

Seats in 170 AG

In 170 AG the Assembly had 300 members and a majority of 151. The Progressives held 105 seats, the Servants of the Republic 95, the Federalists 55 and the Nationalist Union 45. See Political parties. The Speaker, who rotated yearly among the six blocs after 182 AG and was before that elected by the Assembly, was Ada Wen of the Servants in 170 AG.

Seats in 190 AG

In 190 AG the Assembly of the Third Republic had 250 members, with a majority at 126. The Nationalist Union surged to 90 seats, on the memory of the war and the fall of Republic City, and became the largest party, helped by the martyrdom of its leader Zoltan, killed in the bombing of Yu Dao. The Servants of the Republic held 80, the Progressives 45 and the independents 35, since the Federalists had dissolved after 178 AG. President Zhu Li, an independent in her third term, governed with the Servants, the Progressives and the independents, which together held 160 seats as the Hope of the Future coalition, against the Union.

Constituencies

Constituencies were drawn by population. Since the Assembly elected the Republic Councillors, the votes of the urban newcomers decided even the seat that Yanakawan natives saw as theirs, a grievance that fed the Nationalist Union. The Harmonists, who went mainstream after the ban of 126 AG, held Assembly seats until 170 AG.
