politics_of_the_urn.title: Politics of the United Republic of Nations
politics_of_the_urn.html:
This is a stub. It gathers what the wiki records and will be expanded.
Politics of the United Republic of Nations
FormCouncil republic (102–171 AG); presidential republic with a Congress (171–182 AG); presidential republic with a unicameral Assembly (182 AG onward)
ExecutiveSix-member Republic Council; from 171 AG a President and Federal Cabinet
LegislatureNational Assembly (unicameral)
JudiciarySupreme Court of nine justices; Constitutional Court
Parties (170 AG)Servants of the Republic, Progressives, Federalists, Nationalist Union
ElectionsElections in the United Republic of Nations

The United Republic of Nations began as a council republic and became a presidential republic in 171 AG, without replacing its legislature. The full history is under Constitutional evolution on its main page.

First Republic, 102–171 AG

A six-member Republic Council, one councillor for each constituent community (Northern Water, Southern Water, Fire, Earth, Air and Non-Bender), shared the executive and elected one of its own as President. In 170 AG the President was Tarrlok. A reform approved 4–2 on 18 July 170 AG, after the Republic City crisis, replaced the Council.

Fault lines

Three divisions ran through the First Republic. The first was between the newcomers, the settlers and refugees who had come to Republic City in the decades after 102 AG, and the Yanakawan natives of the eastern coast. The second was between left and right, which the legacy of the Salvationist exiles and the Harmonists kept alive. The third was between those who thought the Council a deadlock and those who thought it the republic's safeguard, and the charge of corruption was never absent from it.

The Council in practice

Of the six councillors, four held the established bender seats, Fire, Earth, Water and Air, and two held the Non-Bender seats. The natives, who in the republic's founding settlement were given equal seats, held two of the six, but the two Non-Bender seats did not both belong to them. One was in practice the natives' seat and stood for the minority of the republic's people, and the other was the general seat of the non-bender majority, which meant the newcomers. The other four seats were those of established benders. Aang, the sole running bender among them, held the Air seat until his death, and the Air Nomads' seat was reserved for them by Article 70 of the Charter in memory of the Air Nomad genocide. After Aang's death, about 153 AG, the Air seat passed to Tenzin. See Constitutional Charter.

Because the Assembly elected the councillors and its constituencies were drawn by population, the urban newcomers in effect chose even the seat that the natives saw as theirs. The natives resented it, and the resentment fed the Nationalist Union. A hereditary-looking Air seat gave the Nationalist Union and the left an attack line against the Air Nomads' "dynasty".

Citizenship

The republic treated newcomers harshly. A newcomer was left to face the consequences of his own choices, and the state did not shield him from them. The law itself was lax. Citizenship was by birth and unrelated to bending, and newcomers could acquire it with few formal requirements, but the system that administered it had many problems. A newcomer's papers were poorly checked and easily disputed, officials had wide discretion, and once a newcomer was a citizen he was given little protection from his employer, the police or the registry. The service obligation of the Charter was enforced unevenly, and a newcomer who failed to meet it could lose what he had gained. The notice posted at the mill where Dava worked, which told workers that accidents were their own responsibility, was an example of the culture. A newcomer applied to the Citizenship Registry, an office of the Council that kept the rolls and decided his case, and a refused applicant could appeal to the Assembly's Committee on Constitutional Compliance, which heard disputes about citizenship. The Registry's officials had wide discretion, and both bodies were slow.

The bureaucracy and the Port Authority

The republic's bureaucracy was deeply corrupt from the founding in 102 AG. Offices were bought and handed down, permits and contracts were sold, and the Council's friends did best. The corruption was most open at the Republic City Port Authority, which let the contracts for the docks and ran the harbor's customs. In 118 AG the Port Authority's building was bombed, and the Port Authority was turned to rubble, a fact that the republic's newspapers could not leave alone, since the bombing did what no committee had been able to do and the reform of the office followed. The Assembly introduced civil service examinations, ending the sale and inheritance of posts, and passed an ombudsman and records law that set up an independent inspector and required duplicate records to be kept off the premises. The reform removed the worst of the Port Authority's patronage and left the Council's corruption alone, and it was the Council's own friends who benefited from the contracts for the docks' security and cleanup in 126 AG. See Political parties of the United Republic of Nations.

Corruption and the Harmonists

The corruption issue of the era was the one of 126 AG. The Dock Bombing killed a councillor, the republic blamed the dock foreman Yakone and executed him, and the Harmonists were banned. The scandal was about money. The contracts for the port's security, which had failed, and for the cleanup of the docks afterwards were let to friends of the Council without tender, and the sums paid were out of all proportion to the work. The seat of the dead councillor, who had held the natives' Non-Bender seat, was filled by the Assembly with a candidate backed by the newcomers' districts, which deepened the natives' resentment and gave the Nationalist Union its first grievance. The affair hung over the Council for decades. The Harmonists, however, went mainstream. They kept seats in the Assembly until 170 AG and grew angrier with every year of the ban, until Dava's death.

The offices

The Council Head rotated every year and was "first among six equals", with no power over his colleagues beyond chairing the Council and speaking for it. The wiki's early heads include Councillor Han Ji-ho of the Earth seat, who held the office in the Council's first year, 102 AG, and Aang, who held it in 108 AG. By 170 AG the office had passed to Tarrlok, who was called the Council President, since after thirty years in the Council he had made the rotation an office of habit. The Speaker of the National Assembly was elected by the Assembly, and in 170 AG was Ada Wen of the Servants of the Republic. See Political parties of the United Republic of Nations. These names are invented.

Tenzin and the swing seat

Tenzin voted on what he judged morally right. He was neutral by design, and was therefore the swing vote of the Council. Every camp lobbied him and none trusted him, and he could not build a coalition. In the vote of 18 July 170 AG to replace the Council by the Raiko Reform, approved 4–2, Tenzin and Tarrlok were the two councillors who voted no, for opposite reasons. Tenzin voted on principle against the concentration of power in one office. Tarrlok, who presided over the Council, would have lost the body he led. The Raiko Reform took away Tenzin's tiebreaking role, though he kept one of the six Founding Seats of the new High Council.

Second Republic, 171–182 AG

The Raiko Reform gave the republic a President and Vice President, elected directly for four years, and a Congress of a High Council and a House of Representatives. See the reformed Charter.

Third Republic, from 182 AG

After the penetration scandal of 181–182 AG, the reform was undone by the Restoration. A single elected President is head of state and government, with a Federal Cabinet. The National Assembly, restored as the only chamber, approves laws and budgets and can impeach the President.

Open questions

The Assembly's seat counts and the sitting President in 190 AG are not yet written. The names of the councillors involved in the 126 AG scandal are also open.

elections_in_the_urn.title: Elections in the United Republic of Nations
elections_in_the_urn.html:
This is a stub. It gathers what the wiki records and will be expanded.
Elections in the United Republic of Nations
Bodies electedNational Assembly; the President from 171 AG; the High Council and the House, 171–182 AG
AssemblySingle-member constituencies, four-year terms, three consecutive terms at most
Council (to 171 AG)Elected by the Assembly for staggered six-year terms, two terms at most

This page is prepared for the Assembly elections of 170 AG and 190 AG and for the first presidential election after the reform of 171 AG, and the elections of the Congress, 171–182 AG. No result is written yet.

Assembly election of 170 AG

In the Assembly of 300 seats the Progressives won 105, the Servants of the Republic 95, the Federalists 55 and the Nationalist Union 45. No party held the 151 seats of a majority. See Political parties.

Assembly election of 190 AG

The Assembly of 250 seats elected in 190 AG gave the Nationalist Union 90 seats, the Servants of the Republic 80, the Progressives 45 and the independents 35, since the Federalists had dissolved after 178 AG. No party had the 126 seats of a majority. The Union was the largest party, but the Servants, the Progressives and the independents governed together with 160 as the Hope of the Future coalition.

Council elections

Before 171 AG the Assembly elected one councillor each year for a six-year term, so that one seat fell vacant every year. Because the constituencies were drawn by population, the large urban districts held most of the Assembly, and newcomers decided the result of every Council contest, including the seat the natives regarded as theirs.

imperial_constitution_of_tajisaki.title: Imperial Constitution of Tajisaki
imperial_constitution_of_tajisaki.html:
This is a stub. It gathers what the wiki records and will be expanded.
Imperial Constitution of Tajisaki
NameThe Imperial Constitution of the Empire of Tajisaki (帝国の法, Teikoku no Hō)
Promulgated byFire Lord Sozin
Amended underFire Lord Azulon
Consolidated88 AG, under Fire Lord Ozai (“Consolidated Imperial Edition”)
StructureTen chapters, Articles 1–65, and a Schedule of Obligations
AmendmentBy Imperial Rescript, at the Fire Lord's sole discretion
LegislatureNational Diet

The Imperial Constitution is the founding law of the Empire of Tajisaki, known to foreign peoples as the Fire Nation. It states that it “does not limit Imperial authority” but makes that authority “legible.” The text in the wiki is the consolidated edition of 88 AG. It was never repealed in the civil war, in which nobody applied it, and it was revised by Zuko in 118 AG; see the Revised Constitution.

The Rescript and the Interpretive Notice

A Supreme Imperial Rescript signed by Ozai opens the text: loyalty to the Fire Lord is “the first law, the last law, and the only law.” Three years of every subject’s life belong to the throne. An Interpretive Notice from the Office of National Enlightenment adds that the rights in Chapter II “are not inherent rights” but grants from the throne, which a ministry may withdraw.

Chapters

ChapterArticlesContent
I. The Imperial Throne1–9The Fire Lord’s authority is absolute and eternal. The person of the Fire Lord is inviolable and may not be criticised. The Fire Lord names the heir by prowess, intellect, loyalty and martial achievement, and is Supreme Commander with the sole power over war, peace and treaties. The Privy Council advises at the Fire Lord’s pleasure. Rescripts, Truths and Proclamations may be issued on any subject.
II. Rights and duties of subjects10–19Liberties of person, correspondence, speech, belief, domicile and petition, each “within the limits of law.” Colonial subjects have fewer rights. Article 19: rights follow duty. Every male subject registers at 17 and serves 36 months, then is in the Class A Reserve until 45. Deferral is allowed only for medical, war-production or technical-training reasons, and none for conscience.
III. The National Diet20–28Two Houses. The House of Lords has princes, peers of the first to third rank, appointees and the highest taxpayers, and cannot be dissolved. The House of Representatives is elected by male subjects who have served and meet a property qualification, and the Fire Lord may dissolve it at any time. The Diet passes the budget and laws, but the Fire Lord may withhold assent. It may not investigate military operations, the Ministry of Truth, state secrets or the Fire Lord (Article 28).
IV. The Cabinet29–35The Prime Minister and ministries are appointed by the Fire Lord: National Enlightenment, Truth, National Harmony, War, the Navy, Aviation, Colonial Affairs, Finance, Industry, Spiritual Affairs, Civil Administration and the Imperial Research Bureau. The General Staff Directorate sits outside the Cabinet with direct access to the Fire Lord. The Ministry of Truth has authority over internal security and over every person in the Empire.
V. The Judiciary36–40Imperial Courts cannot review Rescripts or Truths. Military tribunals try soldiers and, in emergencies, civilians. Ministry of Truth courts are outside the ordinary hierarchy and their only appeal is to the Fire Lord.
VI. Colonies and the Homeland Purity Initiative41–45Colonies are integral parts of the Empire, ruled by administrators with combined powers. Colonial subjects are sorted into Recognized Imperial Persons, Enrolled Colonial Subjects, Unenrolled Populations and Designated Threat Populations. The Homeland Purity Initiative allows integration, resettlement and removal. Article 45 declares “the Air Nomad Question” settled and prohibits Air Nomad bending and practice.
VII. Emergency and martial law46–51The Fire Lord may declare an emergency at any time, with no limit, which suspends Chapter II. Under martial law the military commander holds all civil and judicial authority. The Empire recognizes no external law.
VIII. Ideological foundations of the Truth52–57The Fire Lord is the living embodiment of the Sacred Flame. The civilizing mission is the central project of history. Six Enlightenment principles are taught to every subject, including that the Air Nomads ended because pacifism cannot sustain civilization. The Ministry of National Enlightenment keeps the Approved Historical Record, and loyalty must be demonstrated actively.
IX. Finance and the war economy58–61Defense is the first claim on the budget. The Ministry of Industry may requisition factories. Property may be taken at a state-fixed value.
X. Amendment and interpretation62–65The Fire Lord may amend by Rescript alone. The Diet may propose amendments by two-thirds of both Houses, but the Fire Lord may reject them. Articles 1 and 19 cannot be altered. Judges interpret by what best serves the Fire Lord’s dignity first, then the Empire’s security.

The Schedule of Obligations

A plain-language summary is given to every subject at 17: register, serve 36 consecutive months, and stay in reserve. The full Constitution governs where they differ.

Notes

Under this text, the Diet that the Fire Lord dissolved on 8 August 100 AG could not investigate the Fire Lord, the military or the Ministry of Truth, which matches the National Diet page. The Diet of 170 and 190 AG is described on Politics of Tajisaki.

Open questions

The Law of Imperial Succession and the text of the Rescripts are not yet written.

constitution_of_qianchan.title: Constitution of Qianchan
constitution_of_qianchan.html:
This is a stub. It gathers what the wiki records and will be expanded.
Constitution of Qianchan
NameConstitutional Charter of the Republic of Qianchan (Qianchan Minguo)
EditionConsolidated edition, 94 AG
RatifiedYear of the Iron Mountain
AmendmentsLong Coast (first), Iron Gate (second), Stone Wind (third)
MottoLiberty through Law. Strength through Service. Justice through Sacrifice.
StructurePreamble and Articles I–XVIII
ParamountMandatory military service; the right to bear arms

The Charter is the constitution of the Qianchan Republic in its consolidated edition of 94 AG. Its two “Paramount Obligations of Citizenship” are mandatory military service and the right to bear arms, which it calls the pillars on which the Constitution rests. The 170 AG legislature on Federal legislature of Qianchan differs from this text; the wiki does not yet say how or when it changed.

Articles

ArticleSubjectKey provisions
ITerritory and sovereigntyOne and indivisible territory (the Qianchan Archipelago and the Zaofu Peninsula). No cession without a national referendum. If any territory is occupied, the Republic does not recognize it and can govern in exile; no surrender signed under coercion binds it.
IIPrinciples and state policiesA democratic republic with no hereditary authority. Renunciation of aggressive war.
IIIBill of rightsSection 18 guarantees the right to bear arms and the right of resistance, and it cannot be suspended in an emergency. Torture is prohibited.
IVCitizenshipCitizens at adoption, and those born to citizens.
VMandatory military serviceEvery citizen registers at 18 and serves at least 24 months before 25: a 12-month foundation phase and then further phases. Citizen militias are regulated by the regions.
VILegislative departmentA Congress of a Senate of 24 elected at large for six years, and a House of Representatives of up to 250, elected by district and population. Members must have completed service or hold a medical exemption. Congress alone declares war, ratifies treaties and amends the Charter. It may not cut service below 24 months or nullify the right to bear arms.
VIIExecutive departmentA President who is head of state and government and Commander in Chief, directly elected for one six-year term, aged 40 or more. Martial law and suspension of habeas corpus last at most 60 days. The President cannot use weapons of mass destruction or commit forces abroad without Congress, except against an attack on national territory.
VIIIJudicial departmentA Supreme Court of a Chief Justice and fourteen Associate Justices. Its constitutional rulings are final. It reviews every emergency claim within 30 days of a citizen’s petition.
IXConstitutional commissionsCivil Service, Elections, Audit and Veterans Affairs.
XLocal government and the Federal CompactA federal state with regional governments that have their own legislative, executive and judicial authority. Regions run reserve centres and militias. Zaofu is a Special Administrative Region, and the Beifong Foundation’s governance of its industrial and metalbending institutions is recognized.
XI–XVIAccountability, economy, social justice, education, the family, general provisionsPublic office is a public trust, plus provisions on the national economy and patrimony, human rights, education and science, and the family.
XVIIAmendmentsProposed by three-fourths of Congress, a convention called by two-thirds, or a petition of 12 percent of voters. Ratified by a plebiscite 60–90 days later. Seven provisions are unamendable, among them the bar on hereditary authority, the ban on torture, the right to bear arms, the service obligation and the occupation and resistance provisions.
XVIIITransitory provisionsExisting laws continue until repealed.

Open questions

The Federal Compact, the dates behind the amendment years, and how the Senate of 24 became the Federal Council of the 170 AG legislature are not yet written. The Charter calls the member units “regions”; the wiki uses “states” formally and “provinces” informally.

urn_constitutional_charter.title: Constitutional Charter of the United Republic of Nations
urn_constitutional_charter.html:
This is a stub. It gathers what the wiki records and will be expanded.
Constitutional Charter of the United Republic of Nations
NameConstitutional Charter of the United Republic of Nations (Gonghe Guojia Lianhemeng)
Text datedYear 1 of the Republic (100 AG)
In forceFrom the Founding Congress and Declaration of Union, 102 AG
ExecutiveSix-member Republic Council
LegislatureNational Assembly (unicameral)
StructureTwelve Titles, Articles 1–70, a Closing Declaration and an Oath
Replaced byThe Raiko reform, 171 AG

The Charter is the first constitution of the United Republic of Nations. Its text is dated the first year of the Republic, which it places in 100 AG; the Founding Congress declared the Union in 102 AG, and the Charter has been the law since. Its motto is “Liberty. Equality. Fraternity. No tyrant shall govern here. No invader shall silence us.”

Titles

TitleArticlesContent
I. Natural and civil rights1–14Equality and liberty, the presumption of innocence, freedom of opinion and of the press. Article 14, the right to bear arms and of resistance, is paramount.
II. Territory, sovereignty, citizenship15–20The territory of the former Fire Nation colonies on the eastern coast of the Earth Kingdom. Citizenship from birth, not tied to bending. The Constitution continues under occupation.
III. Civic duty and national service21–27Every citizen registers at 18 and serves at least 24 months before 25: military, civil defense, essential public service or conscientious-objector service. Bending is integrated as a supplementary skill. Veterans’ benefits follow.
IV. The Republic Council28–36Six councillors: Fire, Earth, Water, Air, and two Non-Bender seats. Each is elected by the Assembly from the matching bloc for a six-year term, with one seat falling vacant every year. The Council Head rotates every year and is “first among six equals,” not a president. Decisions are by majority, with four votes for emergencies. The Council may not use the armed forces against peaceful assembly.
V. The National Assembly37–42Representatives are elected from single-member constituencies for four-year terms, at most three in a row. The Assembly passes laws and the budget, ratifies treaties and may withdraw confidence from the Council. A Committee on Constitutional Compliance reviews laws.
VI. The Supreme Court43–47Nine justices appointed by the Council and confirmed by the Assembly. The Court can void any law or act.
VII. Ministries48–51Ministries headed by ministers. A Ministry of Civil Rights and Equality has its own mandate to prosecute discrimination.
VIII. Armed forces52–56Civilian control, a citizen militia, and no use of the army against lawful protest.
IX. Local government57–64A “unitary state” with strong regional and local self-government.
X. State of emergency—The Council may declare an emergency by four votes; rights such as arms and resistance cannot be suspended.
XI. Amendment65–66Two-thirds of the Assembly, two-thirds of regional assemblies within three years, then a referendum. Unamendable: Article 1, the right to bear arms, service, popular sovereignty, the annual rotation of the Council Head, the Council’s composition, the ban on torture and the resistance provisions.
XII. Transitional provisions67–70Old colonial law continues only where consistent. The First Assembly is elected within three months and the First Council within six. Article 70 recognizes the destruction of the Air Nomads as a genocide and reserves the Air seat.

Notes

The Charter’s “Council Head,” who rotates yearly, is the officer the wiki elsewhere calls the Council President; in 170 AG it was Tarrlok. The rotation was modelled on the Swiss Federal Council.

In practice

The Council's four bender seats were held by established figures. The natives had two of the six seats in principle, but only one of the two Non-Bender seats was in practice theirs, and the other was the newcomers'. The law on citizenship was lax, and newcomers could acquire it with few formal requirements, but its administration had many problems and gave them little protection. The Assembly's constituencies were drawn by population, so urban newcomers in effect chose even the seat the natives thought theirs. Newcomers applied to the Citizenship Registry, with appeals to the Committee on Constitutional Compliance. See Politics of the United Republic of Nations.

Open questions

The Founding Congress and the gap between the drafting in 100 AG and the Declaration of Union in 102 AG are not yet written.

urn_charter_reformed_171_ag.title: Constitutional Charter of the United Republic of Nations as reformed, 171 AG
urn_charter_reformed_171_ag.html:
This is a stub. It gathers what the wiki records and will be expanded.
Constitutional Charter of the United Republic of Nations as reformed, 171 AG
NameConstitutional Charter as amended by the Raiko Constitutional Reform Act
PassedThe National Assembly, then confirmed by referendum, 171 AG
ReplacedThe Republic Council
ExecutiveA directly elected President and Vice President
LegislatureA Congress: the High Council and the House of Representatives
StructureThirteen Titles, Articles 1–64 (renumbered sections)
UndoneBy 182 AG, after scandals; see below

The Raiko Reform, ratified in 171 AG after the governance crisis and the corruption scandal around the Water Tribe Council seat of 169–170 AG, abolished the Republic Council and gave the republic a president. See Raiko. The reform was in force for eleven years, and by 182 AG it had been undone. What undid it was the penetration scandal, and the settlement was the Restoration of 182 AG.

What the Reform changed

TitleChange
I. RightsCarried forward unchanged and unamendable; Article 14, the right to bear arms, kept.
II. TerritoryMinor amendments; a new section keeps the government running if territory is occupied.
III. National serviceUnchanged and unamendable.
IV. The PresidentNew. Head of state and government and Commander-in-Chief, elected directly with a Vice President for four years, at most two terms, minimum age 35 and 15 years’ citizenship. Appoints ministers and justices with High Council consent, has a veto Congress can override by two-thirds, and negotiates treaties. Cannot rule by decree, dissolve Congress, or send the armed forces against peaceful protest. The House impeaches; the High Council tries.
V. The High CouncilNew. The Council’s six seats (Fire, Earth, Water, Air and two Non-Bender) become six Founding Seats elected by national vote from their constituencies, with six-year terms staggered two every two years, plus two Senators from each region. The Vice President presides. The Founding Seat composition is unamendable.
VI. The House of RepresentativesNew. At most 300 members from single-member districts by population, with a census every ten years, serving three-year terms, at most four in a row.
VII. The Supreme CourtNine justices, appointed by the President with High Council confirmation, for twelve-year terms, with no more than three of any one bending tradition.
VIII–XI. Ministries, forces, regions, emergencyMinisters answer to the President. A declaration of war needs two-thirds of both chambers. An emergency lapses unless Congress ratifies it within 72 hours. Title X now calls the Republic a “federal state.”
XII. ElectionsNew. Presidential elections every four years, with an Electoral Commission. Voters must have completed national service. A sitting President must hand over power within 30 days.
XIII. AmendmentTwo-thirds of both chambers, two-thirds of regional assemblies, then a referendum.

Undone by 182 AG

After the penetration scandal of 181–182 AG, the reform was undone. By 182 AG the High Council and the House were gone, the National Assembly was restored as the only chamber, and the presidency remained with a Federal Cabinet. The history is on Politics of the United Republic of Nations.

Open questions

The vote that undid the reform and the later amendments to the Charter are not yet written.

urn_earth_empire_war.title: United Republic–Earth Empire war
urn_earth_empire_war.html:
This is a stub. It gathers what the wiki records and will be expanded.
United Republic–Earth Empire war
Date2 December 180 AG – 31 December 182 AG
ResultThe Empire’s successor, the Xinan command, ended the war after striking three cities with atomic weapons; see Strikes of December 182 AG
Belligerents
The Earth Empire, against the United Republic of Nations, joined by Qianchan and Tajisaki on 25 December 180 AG
DeclarationsThe Empire, 2 December 180; the Republic, 4 December; Qianchan and Tajisaki, 25 December
OpeningTwo false-flag strikes on the Empire’s western bases, 30 November and 1 December 180 AG
CharacterAn air war with a minimal ground push; the Empire held air superiority for about the first month
TerrainThe Si Wong Desert and its mountain arc, with three gaps; see below
End31 December 182 AG, informally, as the Imperial command collapsed after the strikes of December 182 AG
AftermathPenetration scandal of 181–182 AG; Revolutionary campaign of 181–182 AG

The war between the Earth Empire and the United Republic of Nations ran from 2 December 180 AG to 31 December 182 AG, twenty-five months. It opened with two strikes on the Empire’s major military bases on the western coast, on 30 November and 1 December, which the Empire blamed on the Republic. The Empire’s press was heavily suppressed, so the public heard of the strikes only through Ministry communiqués, and the figures for the dead leaked abroad. Then came more staged incidents, each blamed on the other side. Some were done by the Empire’s agents, and some by Republic officers who were working for the Empire.

The false flags

These are in-universe accounts, assembled by the Joint Inquiry afterwards.

DatePlaceEventBlamed onActually done byEffect
30 Nov 180Xilan naval base, western coast of the Earth KingdomExplosions in the arsenal and dry docks; about 800 killed.The Republic, by sabotage or air attackImperial agents; the Inquiry could not find who gave the orderThe Ministry announces an “attack by the Republic of Nations.” The press prints only the communiqué.
1 Dec 180Cape Hengshan air base, western coastA raid on the aircraft parks and fuel stores; about 340 killed.The Republic, by aircraftImperial agents, in the same operationOn 2 December the Empire declares war. Foreign correspondents are expelled and the dead are never counted in public.
9 Dec 180Qiaotou ferry crossingA crowded ferry is bombed; 47 killed.The Republic, by artilleryImperial agents, with timed chargesThe Empire calls it an attack on civilians and mobilizes.
17 Dec 180Mohe border postTwelve Imperial customs guards shot dead.Republic militia, by their uniformsAn Imperial special unit in seized Republic uniformsBorder crossings close; the Republic is accused in the Concord.
23 Dec 180Supply column at the Zaofu–Omashu borderAn Imperial column is ambushed; 19 killed.Qianchan, by the Zaofu Iron GuardImperial troops, in Iron Guard-pattern armorThe pretext for the Empire’s strikes on Qianchan on 24 and 25 December, which bring Qianchan and Tajisaki into the war.
30 Dec 180Yanming grain depotNine thousand tonnes of grain burned.Republic saboteursImperial agentsThe Empire requisitions grain in the river provinces.
11 Jan 181Tianhe roadA Republic relief convoy is shot up; 22 drivers and medics killed.Imperial gunshipsRepublic militia under an officer later found to be compromisedPublic anger in the Republic demands a strike across the border.
2 Feb 181Shuiyue village63 villagers killed, in what looks like reprisal.Republic soldiers, from photographsImperial irregulars in Republic uniformsThe photographs run in the Empire’s press and in Republic papers; the Assembly debates it for three days.
19 Mar 181Port HanyuanThe hospital ship Gongping is shelled in the harbour; 31 killed.Imperial artillery, by the shell typesA Republic battery under a compromised officer, firing Imperial-pattern shellsThe Congress passes the Mobilization Act on 24 March 181 AG.

The ninth incident, at Port Hanyuan, produced the Republic’s Mobilization Act on 24 March 181 AG. The Inquiry later found that the four High Council members and a quarter of the House who had pressed hardest for it were among those working for the Empire.

The opening air war, 2–4 December 180 AG

The Empire declared war on 2 December. For three days its aircraft and long-range guns bombarded the Republic’s western ports and coastal towns, the heaviest bombing and shelling the Republic had seen. On 4 December the Republic’s Congress declared war. The Republic had few interceptors on its western coast, and the Empire’s air fleets took control of the sky over the gulf.

Air superiority, December 180 – January 181 AG

For about the first month the Empire held air superiority. Two weapons marked that month. The CL1201 was pressed into service with the Empire as a super weapon. The B70 bomber also entered service. What the CL1201 is, how many B70s flew and what they hit are not yet written. The Republic, Qianchan and Tajisaki contested the sky only from about January 181, when Qianchan’s and Tajisaki’s air forces arrived.

25 December: Qianchan and Tajisaki join

After the staged ambush of 23 December, the Empire struck Qianchan’s eastern coast on 24 December and the Zaofu–Omashu border on 25 December. Qianchan declared war on 25 December, and Tajisaki declared war the same day. The Concord of Nations, of which both were founders, did not meet. See Qianchan and Tajisaki.

Geography of the front

The war on land was limited. The front ran along the Si Wong Desert, whose southern and eastern edge is closed by a mountain arc, and the Omashu range to its west. Neither army could move large forces across them, so each probed the gaps.

GapWhereNotes
A. West GapThe coastal plain between the Omashu range and the desertThe Zaofu–Omashu border. It is the only broad route between the Empire and the south. The Empire attacked it on 25 December.
B. South GateA narrow corridor between the desert’s south-west edge and the mountain arcShort and easily held. Both sides probed it.
C. East GapThe strip between the mountain arc’s north-east end and the eastern lowlandsThe way into Qianchan’s north-east lobe. The Empire’s attack on the east coast on 24 December was timed to support it.

The result was an air war and minimal ground push, with raids over the gulf and the gaps and little movement of the lines. A strategic map of the front, with the desert, the mountains and the three gaps, is kept with the wiki files.

The war

The battles of the front are summarized at Battle of Dunhua, the Empire’s one large ground advance into the Republic. The hidden base was found on 2 June 181 AG. On 4 September 182 AG the Empire’s radio announced that Kuvira was dead, and withdrew the statement the next day. The war went on. In late November the Empire dropped a very large conventional bomb on Republic City, aimed at the Congress hall, and took the city on 1 December; the government moved to Yu Dao. In early December unconfirmed reports said Kuvira had died at the hands of the Avatar, Korra. Her successors, the Xinan command, then ordered atomic strikes, and Yu Dao, Zaofu and Gaoling were struck in December. See Fall of Republic City and Strikes of December 182 AG. During 1–25 December the Empire’s army mutinied and its western coast and north rose; see Collapse of the Imperial command. The Concord’s talks in December nearly brought both sides to the table and then failed. The war ended informally on 31 December, the day the Earth Republic was proclaimed.

The revolutionaries

While the states fought, the revolutionary groups of the Earth lands used the war to rebuild their standing. See Revolutionary campaign of 181–182 AG.

Open questions

The battles on the three fronts, the terms of the end, and who ordered each incident on the Empire’s side are not yet written.

The Night of No Sirens, 2–3 February 181 AG

The CL1201 nuclear carrier launched B70 bombers that struck Caldera City and the Tajisaki Royal Navy gulf squadron without warning. See Raid on Caldera City and Capital bombing campaign.

urn_penetration_scandal.title: Penetration scandal of 181–182 AG
urn_penetration_scandal.html:
This is a stub. It gathers what the wiki records and will be expanded.
Penetration scandal of 181–182 AG
Formal nameJoint Inquiry into the Penetration of the Republic’s Institutions
Informal name“The Rot”
Date30 November 180 AG – 182 AG
CauseFalse-flag incidents in the war with the Earth Empire; defectors and captured records in 181 AG, and the Empire’s archives seized in the autumn of 182 AG
FoundHostile agents in politics, the military and industry
High Council4 members working for the enemy
House of Representatives25 percent of the members, about 75 of 300
ResultThe Congress undone; the Constitutional Settlement of 182 AG

The penetration scandal was the discovery, in 181–182 AG, that agents of the Earth Empire had been working inside the government of the United Republic of Nations since before the war. Officially it was the work of a Joint Inquiry of both chambers of the Congress; in the press and in the street it was “the Rot.”

The false flags

The war began on 2 December 180 AG, after two strikes on the Empire’s western military bases on 30 November and 1 December that the Empire blamed on the Republic. Seven more staged incidents followed by March 181 AG, each blamed on the other side, among them the ambush of 23 December that drew in Qianchan and Tajisaki. Some were carried out by agents of the Empire and some by Republic officers who were working for it. They are listed on the war page. The last, the shelling of the hospital ship Gongping at Port Hanyuan, produced the Republic’s Mobilization Act on 24 March 181 AG. Each one narrowed what the Republic’s government could do.

The discovery

The first break came in the autumn of 181 AG, when an Imperial defector and captured field records named Republic officers who had handled the incidents. The Joint Inquiry opened that autumn. It stalled for a year against the compromised members of the Congress who sat on it. When committees overran Imperial offices in the river provinces in the autumn of 182 AG, in the Second Earth Civil War, the Empire's archives were seized, and they listed paid informants, handlers and the incidents they had helped to stage. The Inquiry reported in late 182 AG.

Findings

SectorFinding
The High CouncilFour members were found to be working for the enemy, which removed the Council’s two-thirds majority for treaties and impeachment trials. Among those named were holders of Founding Seats.
The House of RepresentativesAbout a quarter of the members, roughly 75 of 300, were found compromised, whether as agents, as paid informants or as members who had knowingly sat on committees for them.
The militaryOfficers in the staff and in supply were compromised.
IndustryArmament and shipping firms were used to move money and material. The seized archives also showed that Varrick Global Industries had built the Empire's new power suit under a contract for a replica of the Breaker Mk III No. 2.
The executiveThe ministries were not spared; the extent is not yet written.

Consequences

With four seats of the High Council empty or tainted, and a quarter of the House under inquiry, neither chamber could reach the majorities its own Charter required. The Congress could not ratify, impeach or confirm. The reform of 171 AG, passed to make the republic safer, had left it with two chambers that could each be broken. By 182 AG the settlement that followed had undone it. See the Constitutional Settlement of 182 AG.

Open questions

The names of those found guilty, the sentences, the incidents and the size of the industry and military findings are not yet written. The counts are in-universe estimates.

urn_constitutional_settlement_182_ag.title: Constitutional Settlement of 182 AG
urn_constitutional_settlement_182_ag.html:
This is a stub. It gathers what the wiki records and will be expanded.
Constitutional Settlement of 182 AG
Formal nameSecond Constitutional Reform Act
Informal name“The Restoration”
Date182 AG
FollowedThe penetration scandal of 181–182 AG
ReplacedThe Congress of the High Council and the House (171 AG)
CreatedThe Third Republic: President, Federal Cabinet, unicameral National Assembly, Constitutional Court

The Second Constitutional Reform Act, called “the Restoration” in speech, was the republic’s answer to the penetration scandal. It did not go back to the Council of 102 AG, and it did not keep the Congress of 171 AG. It took what the two charters each did well and left the rest.

What was kept, and from where

InstitutionFrom the original Charter (100/102 AG)From the Raiko Reform (171 AG)The Settlement (182 AG)
ExecutiveSix-member Republic Council; a Council Head rotating yearlyA President and Vice President, elected directly for four yearsKept the presidency, with a Federal Cabinet whose ministers the Assembly confirms. A single office was easier to vet and to remove than six.
LegislatureOne chamber, the National AssemblyTwo chambers: a High Council and a HouseOne chamber, the National Assembly, reduced to 250 members. One body is harder to capture in two places.
Founding principleSix Council seats for Fire, Earth, Water, Air and two Non-Benders; unamendableSix Founding Seats in the High Council; unamendableSix designated blocs in the Assembly, so the unamendable composition survives without a second chamber.
Rotating headA Council Head rotating every year; unamendableDropped with the CouncilThe Speaker rotates yearly among the six blocs, so the unamendable rotation survives.
ImpeachmentThe Assembly impeaches; the Supreme Court triesThe House impeaches; the High Council triesThe Assembly impeaches; the Constitutional Court tries.
Confirmations and treatiesThe AssemblyThe High Council, by two-thirdsThe Assembly, with a vetting step.
CourtsA nine-justice Supreme CourtNine justices confirmed by the High CouncilThe Supreme Court stays, and a Constitutional Court is added.
Security——New: a vetting commission checks members of the Assembly, the Cabinet and senior officers.
Rights, arms and serviceUnamendableUnamendableUnchanged and unamendable.

Why it fits

The Reform of 171 AG had made the republic more powerful at the centre and left two chambers that could each be broken, as the inquiry showed. The Restoration kept the presidency, which had acted decisively in the war, and put the legislature back in one chamber. The six constituencies that the founders had made unamendable were moved into the Assembly, and the rotation went to the Speaker. The new court and the vetting commission answered the specific failure: that officials could be bought and nobody could remove them quickly.

The President

In the Third Republic the President is chosen by the Assembly and answers to it, for a term of five years. The Second Republic's President had been elected directly for four.

Names

FormalInformal
Joint Inquiry into the Penetration of the Republic’s Institutionsthe Rot
Second Constitutional Reform Actthe Restoration
Third Republicthe Mended Republic
Federal Cabinetthe Cabinet
Constitutional Courtthe Court
Vetting commissionthe Sieve

Open questions

The text of the Act, the vote, the size of the Assembly and the dates of the first elections are not yet written.

tajisaki_constitution_118_ag.title: Revised Constitution of Tajisaki, 118 AG
tajisaki_constitution_118_ag.html:
This is a stub. It gathers what the wiki records and will be expanded.
Revised Constitution of Tajisaki, 118 AG
Formal nameThe Revised Imperial Constitution
Informal name“The Armistice Constitution”
Date118 AG, after the armistice of 13 August
Promulgated byFire Lord Zuko
RevisesThe Imperial Constitution, consolidated 88 AG
MethodImperial Rescript under Article 62, then submitted to the Diet

The Revised Constitution was the first constitutional text the Empire of Tajisaki issued after the end of the Fire Nation civil war. It is called the Revised Imperial Constitution in law and “the Armistice Constitution” in speech.

The war years, 100–118 AG

The Imperial Constitution of 88 AG was never repealed, and in the eighteen years of the civil war nobody applied it. The Royalists and the Salvationists each governed what they held by decree, and the National Diet had been dissolved on 8 August 100 AG. Nobody on either side cared much what the Constitution said. The questions that mattered were who held the ground and who held the Palace.

After the war

Zuko won the war, was crowned Fire Lord on 9 May 118 AG, and the armistice followed on 13 August. The Revised Constitution followed that year, issued by Rescript as Article 62 allowed, and then submitted to the Diet, a step the text of 88 AG did not require. The throne was kept, and the parts of the old text that had built the war were taken out.

What it changed

SubjectImperial Constitution, 88 AGRevised Constitution, 118 AG
The Fire LordAbsolute, eternal and inviolableKept as head of state and Supreme Commander, but bound by the Constitution and answerable for Rescripts.
The DietCannot investigate the military, the Ministry of Truth or the Fire LordRestored; may investigate the military and the Cabinet.
The Ministry of TruthOutside the courts, over every personAbolished.
Homeland Purity and the Air Nomad QuestionArticles 44 and 45Repealed.
Emergency and martial lawDeclared by the Fire Lord alone, without limitMust be reported to the Diet.
RightsGrants of the throneRecognized rights, with the courts able to enforce them.
ColoniesIntegral parts under administratorsDeleted.
The Approved Historical RecordKept by the Ministry of National EnlightenmentAbolished.
InterpretationWhat best serves the Fire Lord comes firstDropped.

Names

FormalInformal
Revised Imperial Constitutionthe Armistice Constitution
National Dietthe Diet
Fire Lordthe Throne

second_earth_civil_war.title: Second Earth Civil War
second_earth_civil_war.html:
This is a stub. It gathers what the wiki records and will be expanded.
Second Earth Civil War
Date181 – December 182 AG
LocationThe Earth Empire, mainly the western farmlands and the river towns
ResultThe Empire’s western provinces fell to committees; Kuvira’s reported death in December 182 AG left the army to the Xinan command
Belligerents
The Earth Empire; the revolutionary committees; the United Republic in a parallel war
RelatedUnited Republic–Earth Empire war; Revolutionary campaign of 181–182 AG

The Second Earth Civil War was the collapse of the Earth Empire from within, fought while the Empire was also at war with the United Republic of Nations. It follows the First Earth Civil War of 171–176 AG. Its end came with the reported death of Kuvira and the collapse of the Imperial command in December 182 AG.

Open questions

The campaigns, the factions beyond the revolutionary committees, the circumstances of Kuvira’s death and the casualties are not yet written.

revolutionary_campaign_of_181_182_ag.title: Revolutionary campaign of 181–182 AG
revolutionary_campaign_of_181_182_ag.html:
This is a stub. It gathers what the wiki records and will be expanded.
Revolutionary campaign of 181–182 AG
Date181 – 182 AG
Formal nameThe People's Campaign
Informal name“The Harvest”
WhoRevolutionary groups of the People's Republic of Earth tradition, and the Si Wong and river-town committees that later formed the Earth Union
WhereThe river towns, the western farmlands and the Si Wong
MethodRelief, land, people's courts and propaganda, as in the First Earth Civil War
OpportunityThe Empire's war with the United Republic of Nations

While the Earth Empire and the United Republic were at war, the revolutionary groups of the Earth lands launched a campaign of their own. They did what the factions of the People’s Republic of Earth had done in the First Earth Civil War to win the people over: feeding the hungry, handing out land, trying officials, and printing the news. Officially it was the People’s Campaign. In the villages it was “the Harvest.”

How it went

  • Relief. Kitchens and grain stores were opened in the river towns that the Empire had stripped for the war.
  • Land. Estates of Imperial officials were divided among tenants, in the manner of the Collective’s land committees.
  • People’s courts. Informers and Imperial officials were tried in public and some were executed. The courts were quick and rough.
  • Committees. Local committees took over towns that the Imperial garrisons left, and in the Si Wong the committees federated, which led to the Earth Union.
  • Propaganda. Pamphlets blamed both states for the war and the false flags, and presented the committees as the only party that fed anyone.

Reputation

Like its predecessors in the first civil war, the campaign earned a name for competence and for ruthlessness at once. The Empire’s loss of the western provinces in the autumn of 182 AG left the committees holding much of the country they had fed.

Open questions

The names of the groups and committees, their leaders, how closely the Si Wong committees were tied to the older revolutionary parties, and the scale of the killings are not yet written.

cl1201.title: CL1201
cl1201.html:
The Earth Empire’s nuclear-powered flying-wing airborne carrier, finished in 180 AG. One was built.

CL1201
TypeNuclear-powered airborne aircraft carrier and transport
OperatorEarth Empire
OriginMegaproject of Kuvira’s Empire, begun after 176 AG
Wingspan340 m
Length170 m
Gross weightAbout 5,375,000 kg
PowerplantReactor (1,830 MW) heating 4 jet engines; 182 lift fans for take-off
EnduranceAbout 41 days
Crew400–845
Air wing22 fighters carried externally; internal dock for 2 shuttle aircraft
Built1

The CL1201 was a tailless crescent-winged aircraft of colossal size, driven by an atomic reactor that heated the air for four jet engines. Foreign designers had studied it on paper and abandoned it as insane. In the Earth Empire’s economy, built by Kuvira on conscription and seized industry, nothing was too large to build. It was one of a family of Imperial megaprojects, with the B70, that had no purpose except to show that the Empire could.

Role in the war

The Empire never flew the CL1201 over enemy ground. It kept it in the Si Wong Desert, in the deep interior beyond the Imperial forward lines, where it lifted from a hidden strip on its 182 lift fans and stayed aloft or hidden for up to forty days at a time. From the desert it launched the B70 and a fighter wing on routes no radar line watched, and it carried spares, fuel and munitions for its air group, so that it needed no coastal airfield. An unconfirmed rumor, also in the open literature, says a third variant exists; the Empire’s Ministry of Information never named one.

The Imperial press named it Tiancheng, "the Sky Fortress". Allied staff officers kept to its drawing-board number. Its recorded sorties were the strikes on the allied capitals: Caldera City (2–3 February 181 AG), Republic City (16 February) and Gaoling (4 March). See Capital bombing campaign.

Based on the unbuilt Lockheed CL-1201 study; in this world, it was built. Combat details are invented for this wiki.

Fate

The CL1201 was not destroyed in the war. It left its hidden base in late May 181 AG and was kept by the Xinan Dominion, which still held it in 190 AG. The Dominion’s account, repeated in its press, is that the carrier was evacuated to the Eastern Air Temple and stays there. Allied governments have not confirmed it. Whether it delivered the weapon used in the strike on Earth Union City is not written.

xb70.title: B70
xb70.html:
The Earth Empire’s high-speed strategic bomber, in service from December 180 AG.

B70
RoleStrategic bomber
OperatorEarth Empire
StatusPrototype pressed into service, Dec 180 AG
Crew4
SpeedAbout Mach 3
CeilingAbout 22,000 m

The B70 (also called the XB70 in Imperial documents, since it never left prototype status) was a six-engine delta-winged bomber built for the Earth Empire before the war. It flew above the reach of any interceptor Tajisaki, Qianchan or the Republic could field in December 180 AG. The Empire had three flying airframes, later six.

Role in the war

The B70 held the sky over the gulf by being out of reach of it. A B70 flown from the Imperial coast could be seen and tracked, though not touched. Launched from the CL1201 in the Si Wong Desert, it came from a direction no radar line watched, and with a Mach 3 dash its warning time was minutes. It carried long-range cruise missiles and fired them from beyond the capitals’ defenses. It struck Caldera City and a Tajisaki fleet on 2–3 February 181 AG. See Raid on Caldera City.

Specifications are invented for this wiki.

caldera_city_raid_181_ag.title: Raid on Caldera City
caldera_city_raid_181_ag.html:
The Empire’s air strike on the Fire Nation capital and fleet, 2–3 February 181 AG.

Raid on Caldera City
Date2–3 February 181 AG
LocationCaldera City and the gulf
Forces
Earth Empire: CL1201 carrier, 3 B70, 12 fighters
ResultImperial success; Tajisaki Royal Navy gulf squadron destroyed
Casualties and losses
Tajisaki: 4 cruisers, 9 destroyers, about 3,100 sailors, about 640 civilians. Empire: none

On the night of 2 February 181 AG the CL1201 launched three B70 bombers and twelve fighters from the Si Wong Desert. The raiders reached Caldera City before any alarm sounded and struck the naval yards, the arsenal and the rail junction. The Palace district was not touched. At dawn the same bombers sank four cruisers and nine destroyers of the Tajisaki Royal Navy gulf squadron, which had put to sea to cover the yards. No Imperial aircraft was lost.

Approach

The allied radar line, finished in mid-January 181 AG, faced west across the sea routes from the Imperial coast. The CL1201 sat in the Si Wong Desert, deep inside Imperial lines, where no allied scout had been. The B70s flew a Mach 3 route over the mountains and the gulf, below the line in direction if not in height, and fired cruise missiles from beyond the capital’s defenses. They gave the city minutes. The first sirens sounded after the first bombs.

The fleet

The squadron was struck at anchor off Cape Ryujin and under way, by guided and unguided bombs. Tajisaki Royal Navy gunners fired at the sound. Fleet air cover was not in the air.

Aftermath

The Tajisaki Royal Navy lost its gulf squadron and most of its trained cruiser crews. The Diet passed emergency funds on 5 February. Tajisaki’s press named the raid the Night of No Sirens. Allied staff first learned of the carrier from a caravan guide who saw it in the desert on 30 January. It was one of three strikes on allied capitals; see Capital bombing campaign.

Casualty figures and ship counts are invented for this wiki.

earth_empire_megaprojects.title: Earth Empire megaprojects
earth_empire_megaprojects.html:
The enormous weapons and works built under Kuvira, 175–182 AG.

Under Kuvira, the Earth Empire built projects whose scale was the point: the CL1201 nuclear flying carrier, the B70 bomber, and a number of works whose purpose the Empire never published. They were paid for by conscription and by seized industry, and ended with the Empire. The Republic’s inquiry of 182 AG found that some of the designs had been passed to the Empire by informants in the Republic’s shipyards and army staff.

capital_bombing_campaign_181_ag.title: Capital bombing campaign
capital_bombing_campaign_181_ag.html:
The Empire’s three strikes on allied capitals, February–March 181 AG.

Capital bombing campaign
Dates2–3 Feb, 16 Feb, 4 Mar 181 AG
AttackerEarth Empire: CL1201 and B70
TargetsCaldera City, Republic City, Gaoling
BaseSi Wong Desert

Between 2 February and 4 March 181 AG the Empire struck the capitals of all three allies from the CL1201, which was hidden in the Si Wong Desert. The strikes were launched by B70 bombers carrying cruise missiles, with a small fighter escort, and each came with minutes of warning.

The strikes

  • 2–3 February: Caldera City. Naval yards, arsenal and rail junction; the Tajisaki Royal Navy gulf squadron sunk next dawn. See Raid on Caldera City.
  • 16 February: Republic City. The Congress’s hall was spared; the Ministry of Defense, the Mint and the western rail yards were hit. About 410 dead.
  • 4 March: Gaoling. The Federal Defense Office and the airfield were hit; the Parliament building was not. About 230 dead.

Response

Each ally voted emergency funds for interceptors and radar. The Empire’s capital strikes spared the seats of government every time, and the allies took this to be a warning. Allied staff did not find the CL1201’s base until after the war.

Dates and casualty figures are invented for this wiki.

si_wong_hidden_base.title: Si Wong hidden base
si_wong_hidden_base.html:
The Earth Empire’s concealed air base in the Si Wong Desert, 180–181 AG.

Si Wong hidden base
LocationDeep Si Wong Desert, beyond the Imperial forward lines
Used byCL1201, B70
Found2 June 181 AG, by Zaofu airships
StatusEmpty when found; the CL1201 was gone

The Si Wong hidden base was a dry-lake strip and a ring of buried hangars, built before the war under Kuvira and used to hide the CL1201 and the B70 fleet from every allied radar line. It was found on 2 June 181 AG by airships of the Beifong Foundation after three months of search, after the strikes on the three capitals (Capital bombing campaign). When the allies reached it, the CL1201 had gone.

What was found

Fuel dumps, a reactor service bay, 3 B70 cradles and the ruts of a very large aircraft. The Federal Defense Office said the strip had been used "until about the end of May." Where the CL1201 went is the subject of the CL1201 page.

battle_of_dunhua.title: Battle of Dunhua
battle_of_dunhua.html:
The Earth Empire’s advance into the United Republic of Nations through the South Gate, September 181 – February 182 AG.

Battle of Dunhua
Date22 September 181 – 14 February 182 AG
LocationDunhua, southern URN (name invented as a placeholder)
ResultImperial capture, then Republic recapture
DeadRepublic about 41,000 in the siege and about 31,000 in the recapture; Empire about 12,000 and 14,000

The Battle of Dunhua was the only large ground battle of the URN–Earth Empire war. Through the autumn of 181 AG the Empire pushed through the South Gate, the narrow corridor between the desert and the mountain arc, and besieged the Republic city of Dunhua. The city fell on 22 September after 41 days. The Republic’s counter-offensive in January–February 182 AG retook it on 14 February at heavy cost. Neither side advanced further; the war returned to the air.

Casualties of the war

By the end of the war about 570,000 Republic, 540,000 Qianchan and 35,000 Tajisaki dead had been counted, with about 120,000 on the Imperial side. Most of them died in December 182 AG, in the atomic strikes and the fall of Republic City. The defenders lost far more than the attackers: both armies were modern, but the Empire chose the ground and the targets, and the defenders’ cities, ports and rail lines were under its guns and bombs. These are in-universe estimates.

Invented for this wiki. "Dunhua" stands in for the unnamed city; rename if you have another.

fall_of_republic_city_182_ag.title: Fall of Republic City
fall_of_republic_city_182_ag.html:
The Empire’s bombing and capture of the Republic’s capital, 24 November – 1 December 182 AG.

Fall of Republic City
Date24 November – 1 December 182 AG
LocationRepublic City
ResultImperial capture; the Republic’s government moved to Yu Dao
DeadAbout 9,000 in the bombing; about 50,000 in the siege

On 24 November 182 AG a bomb the size of a small truck, a conventional weapon that the press compared to an atomic one, was dropped on Republic City from a B70. It was aimed at the Congress hall, which the Empire had spared in the strikes of February 181 AG. It hit the hall and killed about 9,000 people. The Congress and the Cabinet had already left. The government relocated to Yu Dao. Imperial armor and paratroops reached the city and took it on 1 December.

After

The government at Yu Dao voted the Second Constitutional Reform Act on 15 December. Four days later Yu Dao was destroyed. See Strikes of December 182 AG.

strikes_of_december_182_ag.title: Strikes of December 182 AG
strikes_of_december_182_ag.html:
Strikes of December 182 AG
Date19–20 December 182 AG (Caldera City in December)
Fired byThe Xinan command, successor of the Earth Empire
TargetsYu Dao (air burst), Zaofu (ground burst), Gaoling (air burst), Caldera City (air burst)
DeadYu Dao about 420,000; Zaofu about 310,000; Gaoling about 380,000; Caldera City about 650,000
ResultQianchan's Federal Council voted against surrender; the Concord's talks nearly brought both sides to the table, then failed

After Kuvira was reported dead, her successors in the Xinan command decided to end the war by striking everywhere they could still reach. On 19 December 182 AG an atomic gravity bomb burst over Yu Dao, where the Republic’s government had moved, and destroyed the harbor city. On 20 December an atomic cruise missile burst on the industrial district of Zaofu, and an atomic gravity bomb burst over the old government quarter of Gaoling.

In December an atomic ICBM fired from the Si Wong hit Caldera City, the Fire Nation capital, with an air burst over the old city district. The densest quarter and the government buildings were wiped off the map and the Palace was destroyed; the Fire Lord was evacuated alive.

The Federal Council of Qianchan voted 16 to 8 on 20 December, two-thirds of its 24 members, against surrender. The Concord’s staff nearly brought both sides to the table in December, but the talks failed. The war ended informally on 31 December 182 AG. The Dominion’s later strike on Earth Union City in 190 AG was the same command’s weapons.

Dates, vote and casualty figures are invented for this wiki.

collapse_of_the_imperial_command_182_ag.title: Collapse of the Imperial command
collapse_of_the_imperial_command_182_ag.html:
The mutiny of the Earth Empire’s army and the risings of the western coast and the north, 1–25 December 182 AG.

Collapse of the Imperial command
Date1–25 December 182 AG
TriggerNews that Kuvira had died on 4 September, hidden by the Xinan command, reached the army in early December
PlacesWestern coast (Xilan, Cape Hengshan, Hanyuan Strait ports); the north (Beiyuan and the northern provinces)
ResultThe Xinan command lost the army and its last bargaining power; the December talks ended without a ceasefire

The Earth Empire’s command broke up in December 182 AG. The army had been paid in grain and driven by conscription for six years. It held until early December, when news reached it that Kuvira had died on 4 September at the hands of the Avatar, Korra, and that the Xinan command had hidden her death and was issuing orders in her name.

The western coast

The first units to mutiny were the garrisons of the western coast, at Xilan and Cape Hengshan, the bases of the false flags of 30 November and 1 December 180. They refused to take the new command’s orders, joined the committees and took the ports by 12 December. The Hanyuan Strait ports followed. The coast became a mass uprising: tens of thousands of conscripts and townspeople.

The north

The northern army and the northern provinces revolted next. Garrisons at Beiyuan and along the northern rail line refused to send grain south, arrested their officers and declared for the committees on 14 December. The north is also the part of the Empire the Republic and Qianchan had never reached.

What the command kept

The Xinan command lost the army and the supply lines but kept the atomic units and the CL1201. It used them in the strikes of December 182 AG. By late December it had no army to continue the war, and the Concord’s last attempt at talks that month came to nothing.

Invented for this wiki. "Beiyuan" is a placeholder for the northern provincial center.

ee_concord_war_180_182.title: Earth Empire–Concord War
ee_concord_war_180_182.html:
Earth Empire–Concord War
Date2 December 180 – 31 December 182 AG (informal end)
Belligerents
The Earth Empire, against the United Republic of Nations, joined by Qianchan and Tajisaki; the Concord of Nations never declared war
Commanders and leaders
Kuvira (died 4 September 182 AG); Marshal Xinan, chief of staff, then the Xinan command
Allied commanders
Fire Lord Izumi; President Zhu Li (United Republic); President Haatao (Qianchan); Crown Prince Vice Admiral Iroh of the Tajisaki Royal Navy, coordinating the Republic's naval defence; Army-General Bumi, Centre Army Group; Army-General Uzu, East Army Group
OutcomeThe Earth Empire collapsed; the Earth Republic was proclaimed on 31 December 182 AG
OtherFire Nation island chain occupied by the Empire, April–December 181 AG

The Earth Empire fought the United Republic of Nations, Qianchan and Tajisaki for twenty-five months. It lost its army, not its weapons, when news of Kuvira’s death spread in December 182 AG.

For the first-days account in the weeks from the declaration to the death of Zuko, see Opening phase of the Earth Empire–Concord War.

Background

The Empire rearmed in secret from 176 AG, drawing on Qianchan technology, Tajisaki’s Sōen framework and old arrays rusted or buried in the sand. On 30 November and 1 December 180 AG, Marshal Xinan staged two false flags at the Empire’s western bases and blamed the Republic. The Empire declared war on 2 December. For the details of those first strikes see United Republic–Earth Empire war.

The sides

  • Earth Empire: Kuvira, with Marshal Xinan (her chief of staff) running the army and the secret rearmament programme of 176–180.
  • Allies: Tajisaki, the United Republic of Nations (URN) and Qianchan. All three declared war by 31 Dec 180, unanimously. There is no single commander; a Concord staff council coordinates them.
  • The Concord is the international body, like the UN. It condemned the Empire, imposed sanctions, expelled the Empire from membership by January 181, ran the staff council and a relief agency, and tried to mediate in November 181 and December 182. It did not declare war.
  • Outside the war: the Si Wong sandbenders and the oil company hold the desert oil fields, left untended, with Xinan holding some bases there. The Earth Union did not exist until 184. Agna Qel’a stayed neutral. The Southern Federation sent aid and ships. The Air nations took refugees.

Timeline

WhenWhat happens
176 AGAtomic tests are rumored; Kuvira’s rearmament programme begins, drawing on Qianchan technology, Tajisaki’s Sōen framework and old arrays rusted or buried in the sand.
30 Nov – 1 Dec 180Xinan, for Kuvira, stages the two western-base false flags and blames the Republic.
2 Dec 180The Empire declares war. The Republic declares on 4 Dec; Qianchan and Tajisaki follow by 25 Dec after the east-coast and Zaofu–Omashu attacks.
Dec 180 – Jan 181The Empire holds the air with the CL1201 and B70. The Concord expels it from membership by January.
Feb – Mar 181Caldera City is bombed (2–3 Feb) and the gulf squadron sunk, then Republic City (16 Feb) and Gaoling (4 Mar). The Tajisaki Royal Navy is broken.
Apr – Dec 181The Empire invades the Fire Nation island chain from April, Shirashihoro first, and holds all of it by December.
May – Jul 181An allied probe into the Si Wong to find the carrier fails to sandstorms and air raids. Zaofu airships find the empty base on 2 June.
Jul – Aug 181The revolutionary “Harvest” campaign grows on the western farmlands.
22 Sep 181Dunhua falls after 41 days. The Republic passes a second mobilization.
Oct – Dec 181An Imperial defector exposes the penetration. The Concord proposes talks; Kuvira rejects them. Winter strains allied supply and morale; the Empire has conscription riots and grain shortages. A large bomb is tested and everyone notices.
14 Feb 182The Republic retakes Dunhua.
Mar – Jun 182Imperial B70 and CL1201 raids on ports. Protests in the Republic and Qianchan; the Inquiry stalls on compromised members.
Jul 182Caldera shoots down a bomber launched from the captured islands.
4 Sep 182Kuvira dies. Xinan hides it and issues orders in her name.
Oct 182The Empire’s autumn offensive pushes through the gaps; committees overrun the river provinces.
24 Nov – 1 Dec 182The large bomb destroys the Congress hall in Republic City; the city falls on 1 Dec and the government moves to Yu Dao.
Dec 182An ICBM from the Si Wong hits Caldera with an atomic air burst. Yu Dao, Zaofu and Gaoling are struck. Qianchan’s Federal Council votes two-thirds against surrender. The Concord nearly gets both sides to the table.
Dec 182News of Kuvira’s death leaks (Korra killed her; details left for a novel). The western coast mutinies, the north revolts, and the Empire withdraws en masse; the island chain is abandoned.
31 Dec 182The war ends informally. The Earth Republic is proclaimed.

The strikes of 181–182 AG

The Empire struck the capitals and major cities of its enemies with bombers and, at the end, with atomic weapons. The first atomic strikes came from the CL1201 and the B70 bombers; the last came from an atomic missile fired from the Si Wong. For the Republic’s capital see Fall of Republic City; for the December strikes see Strikes of December 182 AG.

TargetDateWeapon and deliveryBurstDeadWhat it did
Republic City24 Nov 182“Hammer of the Empress”: about 44 t of high explosive, about 5 kt TNT equivalent, dropped by a B70Ground contact at the Congress hallAbout 9,000Crater about 100 m wide; the hall, its square and surrounding blocks flattened. Not atomic. The first strike on the seat of government in the war.
Yu Dao19 Dec 182Atomic gravity bomb, about 400 kt, dropped by a B70Air burst, about 1,800 m, over the Nanaka island financial districtAbout 420,000The harbor city destroyed: exchange, Central Police Station, harbor front and the government’s new seat. Fallout drifted out to sea.
Zaofu20 Dec 182Atomic cruise missile, about 1 Mt, fired from a B70 beyond the city’s defensesGround burst, about 50 m, over the industrial districtAbout 310,000The industrial district, the Beifong Foundation’s plants and the airship yards were vaporized and left a crater; the blast and heavy local fallout reached the rest of the city. The metal domes at the edge stood, with their interiors burned.
Gaoling20 Dec 182Atomic gravity bomb, about 500 kt, dropped by a B70Air burst, about 2,000 m, over the old government quarterAbout 380,000The Federal Defense Office, the airfield and the old quarter destroyed. Parliament had moved to a field outside the city the day before.
Caldera CityDecember 182Atomic ICBM from the Si Wong, about 1.2 MtAir burst, about 2,000 m, over the old city districtAbout 650,000The old district, the densest quarter and the government buildings, wiped off the map; the Palace destroyed, the Fire Lord evacuated alive.

The world by 183 AG

The Xinan Dominion is the strongest successor state, and its capital is Ba Sing Se.

  • Xinan Dominion: holds the eastern heartland, which never mutinied, and partly controls Imperial bases in the Si Wong.
  • Earth Republic: proclaimed 31 Dec 182, started by the revolting army out of hatred of Xinan or of Kuvira, or from a wish for democracy. Its leader is a radical, the vocal voice from King Kuei’s parliament days (name to be invented). Its capital lies across URN territory.
  • Wu’s Earth Kingdom: separate and backed, in the west; Wu comes out of Gaoling.
  • Others on the map: Free cities, the Si Wong confederation (the Earth Union follows in 184), the Fire Nation (islands abandoned by the Empire in the withdrawal, retaken later), the United Republic, Qianchan, Agna Qel’a, the Southern Federation and the two Air nations.

cs_report_172.title: Union falls to 62 seats as unrest abroad shadows the vote
cs_report_172.html:
The Union lost 20 seats and fell to 62 in the National Diet on Feb. 2, 172 AG, an election held in the shadow of the 171 AG crash and a wave of leftist uprisings abroad. The People’s Coalition won 256 seats and a clear majority.

Voters went to the polls with the news from abroad running alongside the news at home. Over the previous 18 months, Equalist-aligned movements had taken to the streets in several nations, and the Calderan Scire has reported strikes, seized depots and clashes with garrison troops in at least five capitals. No Fire Nation province has seen fighting. Several, however, have seen rallies carrying the banners of those movements.

The Union’s campaign tried to separate itself from them. “We are a party of the Diet, not of the barricades,” Union leader Haruo Sakane said at his final rally in Umi on Jan. 30. Critics were not persuaded. NCP chair Mitsuko Aramaki told reporters that voters “can see the same slogans on the same flags, whatever the Union says in Caldera.”

The crash hurt more than the uprisings did. After the 171 AG market collapse, the Union’s provincial machines handled the relief fund in Yahahama, Umi, Takahama and Shirashihoro, and auditors later found payments that could not be traced. Union candidates were asked about the audit at almost every stop. The party’s seat count fell in each of the 10 provinces where it held more than a handful of seats.

Its remaining seats lie almost entirely in the eight core provinces: Shirashihoro, Umi, Yahahama, Takahama, Shinkawa, Narukawa, Kikonokawa and Hatsushima. Umi and Yahahama together returned about half of the Union’s total. Outside the eight, the party held only scattered seats.

The People’s Coalition gained from the Union’s losses. PDP leader Daichi Oyama said the result was “a mandate to restore order in the relief accounts and to keep the Diet away from the street.” The Way held 126 seats and lost no ground, though it gained little.

Turnout was 72.0%, the highest in the archive to that point. Pollsters at the Calderan Scire said the increase appeared strongest in provinces with recent rallies, and cautioned that the survey data cannot separate anger at the crash from fear of unrest.

The Diet convenes in March. Sakane said the Union would keep its seats and demand an inquiry into the relief fund. The government has said it will hold one.

cs_uprisings_174.title: Uprisings reach the borders: what the Equalist movements want
cs_uprisings_174.html:
Equalist and leftist uprisings that began abroad in 170 AG now touch most nations on the continent, and Fire Nation border provinces report rallies, leaflets and arrests. The Calderan Scire reviewed government briefings, travelers’ accounts and the movements’ own printed demands to set out what is happening and what is not.

The movements are not one organization. They share a vocabulary of abolishing hereditary privilege, breaking up landed estates, and seating workers’ councils beside national assemblies, but they split over method. Some seek to win elections. Others have seized granaries, rail depots and telegraph offices. In three nations, garrison units are reported to have refused orders.

The demands are consistent. Printed manifestos call for land to be divided among tenants, a ceiling on rents and grain prices, an end to inherited titles, and the dissolution of standing garrisons answerable to the crown. Lord’s officials in Caldera describe these as “a program to dismantle the state.” Supporters call them a minimum for people who farm land they do not own.

In the Fire Nation, the movement’s reach is narrower. Officials counted 41 rallies in border and port provinces in the first five months of 174 AG, most with fewer than 500 people. Eleven ended in arrests. The Union is the only party in the Diet that shares part of the language, and the government has begun to treat the two as connected.

The Union rejects that. “Seats in the Diet are won with ballots,” Haruo Sakane said on June 9. “We are not responsible for what is printed in other countries.” Ministers have asked the party to publicly condemn the armed groups by name. It has condemned violence in general but has not named any group.

The Way’s leaders want a ban. Mitsuko Aramaki said on June 11 that “a party that will not choose between the Diet and the street has chosen already.” The People’s Coalition is split. PDP leader Daichi Oyama said a ban would “hand the movement its first martyrs,” while members of Agrarian Labor have asked for tighter limits on foreign leaflets and funds.

The Lord’s council has not decided. A proposal to bring the question to an international body, which would later become the Concord of Nations, is expected to be discussed this autumn.

cs_concord_176.title: Concord of Nations bans Equalist Party, The Collective and Salvation Front
cs_concord_176.html:
The Concord of Nations voted on March 17, 176 AG, to ban the Equalist Party, The Collective and Salvation Front and ordered the removal of their members from the National Diet. The 40 Union MPs elected six weeks earlier must vacate their seats.

The ruling followed a debate that lasted four days. Delegates accepted the argument that the three parties were part of one network, with shared funds and a common leadership that answered to movements abroad. The text names the parties and bars their officers from standing for any office for 20 years.

The Union rejected the finding. “This is not a ruling against a party; it is a ruling against a quarter of the voters,” Haruo Sakane said outside the Diet. He said the Union would appeal. The Concord’s statutes do not provide for one.

The Way and The People’s Coalition both welcomed the outcome. Mitsuko Aramaki called it “the end of a long argument.” Daichi Oyama said the PDP supported the ban but would “watch every seat the Concord redistributes.” Several Agrarian Labor MPs voted against it in the Diet’s non-binding motion on Wednesday and said they would not oppose the order itself.

Under the order, the 40 vacated seats will remain empty until the next general election, which means the Diet will sit at 426 voting members. The Union’s former provincial offices were sealed on Thursday morning in Umi, Yahahama, Takahama and Shirashihoro. The Calderan Scire saw no violence at the sites, but groups of between 200 and 400 people gathered outside each.

The Concord’s order also freezes the parties’ accounts. Officials said funds will be reviewed for a link to groups abroad before any money is returned to members.

Abroad, the reaction has been sharp. Several movements said the ruling gives them proof that national assemblies cannot be reformed from inside. The Fire Nation has raised its alert level at the border provinces.
