tiejia_iii.title: Tiejia-III
tiejia_iii.html:
Qianchan's counterpart to the Breaker.

Tiejia-III
MakerZaofu (Beifong family and Qianchan Republic)
OperatorsZaofu Iron Guard
WeaponsFitted with QR-7 rifles
RoleMetalbender's power armour; Qianchan's counterpart to the Breaker

The Tiejia-III is the power armour of the Zaofu Iron Guard, developed in Zaofu, where metalbending is largely restricted to trained personnel. It is the Qianchan Republic's counterpart to the Fire Nation's Breaker. It was the Iron Guard's equipment at Qinglan Port in 100 AG and in later service.

The suit is made for a metalbender. The operator's bending drives and steers the plating and actuators, so the suit moves with the bender's body and answers his control more closely than a pure hydraulic suit does. Its weakness is the reverse of the Breaker's. It needs a trained bender, and Zaofu keeps those few. The Earth Empire later combined the Tiejia-III with the Breaker Mk III No. 2 in a hybrid suit that did not need one. See Imperial hybrid power armor.

imperial_hybrid_power_armor.title: Imperial hybrid power armor
imperial_hybrid_power_armor.html:
The Earth Empire's power armour of 180 AG, a mix of the Tiejia-III and the Breaker Mk III No. 2.

Imperial hybrid power armor
MakerEarth Empire (secret programme, 176–180 AG)
Derived fromTiejia-III; Breaker Mk III No. 2
First seenDecember 180 AG, on the eastern front of the United Republic
OperatorsBenders and non-benders alike
WeaponsHeavy machine guns, miniguns, aircraft cannon
Allied name"The demon suit"

The Imperial hybrid power armor is the Earth Empire's front-line powered suit of the Earth Empire–Concord War. It combines the metalbender-driven frame of Qianchan's Tiejia-III with the Fire Nation's Breaker Mk III No. 2. The allies called it the demon suit, after the Breaker Mk II's nickname, the Hagane no Oni. It was the one weapon of the Empire that was a danger to benders and non-benders both, and its appearance shocked the Republic's army in December 180 AG.

Origins

The Republic's staff did not know how the Empire had built such a suit in secret over five years. The wiki's account is that the programme ran from 176 AG, the year of the Concord's ban, with the Empire's rearmament, drawing on Qianchan technology that came out of Zaofu's Tiejia-III and on Tajisaki's Breaker designs that Salvationist exiles and the Empire's agents had brought over the border. The Empire's engineers took the Breaker Mk III No. 2 as the base because it was made in numbers and was easy to repair, and they took from the Tiejia-III its bending-driven frame and the electromagnetic and plating work that went with it. The Mk IV of the Court of Azula, which was too rare and costly to copy, was not the model. The result was an armoured suit that could be mass-produced in the Empire\'s seized factories.

The Empire\'s cover for the work was a contract. From 177 AG it had commissioned Varrick Global Industries to build what the papers called a replica of the Breaker Mk III No. 2, a "training and display" model said to be for the Empire's parades and for drilling its infantry against Tajisaki armour. In reality the replica was the new power suit: the contract's specifications, revised again and again, were the hybrid's frame, plating and fuel cell, and the company's workshops built the prototypes that the Empire's factories later copied. Whether the company knew what it was building was never settled; see that page. Invented for this wiki.

Design

The suit stood a little over six feet tall and was clad in black plates. Its helmet was shaped like a diver's, with a faceplate that glowed green. It was powered by hydraulics and a fuel cell, so that a non-bender could wear it, and its frame also took the drive of an earthbender or metalbender, who gained extra strength, speed and precision. It had the Mk III's load-distribution system, which let it take blows from several directions and survive the heavy collapses that destroyed the Mk II at Ba Sing Se, and the Breaker's disruption plating, here run by the suit's own power and not by the operator, so that a metalbender could not take hold of it. The Republic's earthbenders tried boulders, spikes and bending the armour itself, and none of it worked. The suits threw boulders themselves.

The armament was fitted to the arms: heavy machine guns, miniguns and aircraft cannon. A section of suits could clear a position held by a squad with grenades and rifles, and the Republic's infantry could damage one only with massed rocket-propelled grenades at close range. The suits had no flamethrowers and made little use of firebenders.

Weaknesses

The suit was not invulnerable. It was heavy and its fuel cell had a short endurance, so it depended on supply trucks. Its disruption plating could be overloaded by specialised metalbending of the Zaofu kind, and a Zaofu Iron Guard bender who knew the Tiejia-III could do things to the suits that an ordinary earthbender could not. It was also loud and slow in the swamp and the forest, which is why the Empire's southern advance stalled at the Foggy Swamp. The Republic's army answered with its own suit programme, ordered by President Zhu Li in December 180 AG.

Service

The first suits were seen in the last week of December 180 AG on the eastern edge of the United Republic, where a Republic squad was killed in a forest cabin. After that the suits spearheaded the Empire's urban assaults in Yanakawa. They were never produced in the numbers of the Empire's bombers, and the Empire's collapse in December 182 AG ended their service. Most were left where they stood.

Invented for this wiki, from the draft novel To the East.

shiza.title: Shiza
shiza.html:
The port of the Southern Air Temple district.

Shiza (Shizu)
RegionSouthern Air Temple island chain, Qianchan Republic
TypePort city and naval base
Taken by QianchanWinter 100–101 AG, from Court loyalists
Known forStaging base of the Qianchan Navy; Shizu City Hospital

Shiza, also written Shizu, is the strategic port of the Southern Air Temple island chain, on the coast of the region that Qianchan held until 120 AG and that is now the autonomous district of the airbenders. The Qianchan Navy kept a base there under a lease after 120 AG.

Capture

The Empire had left the chain with a skeleton garrison by 99 AG, but a body of Court loyalists, who refused to withdraw with it, held Shiza as a stronghold. They were reduced by Qianchan in the winter of 100–101 AG by air strikes, naval bombardment and a ground assault, as the Qianchan garrison took possession of the chain to supply the Restoration Government at Shu Jing. The die-hards who refused to surrender launched desperate attacks on the Qianchan lines and were cut down by machine guns in the streets and alleys. The Federal army then built a network of bases there that became the staging ground for its operations in the chain. See Qianchan Republic.

In the war of 180 AG

In the Earth Empire–Concord War the port was Qianchan's staging ground for reserves bound for the mainland. In late December 180 AG a convoy loaded Federal reserves and their armoured suits onto a cargo ship there. The Shizu City Hospital took in Opal Beifong, wounded in the raid on Zaofu of 24 December, with her care paid for by Fire Lord Izumi; her doctor, Dr Chen, saw her through the first days. In early January 181 AG Bolin joined her there, and Avatar Korra and her friends came through the city and left on a refuelled flying boat for the mainland. See Opening phase of the Earth Empire–Concord War.

See also

  • Qianchan Republic
  • History of Qianchan
  • Opening phase

Invented for this wiki; the capture and the lease are inferred from the Qianchan garrison of 100 AG.

tajisaki_royal_navy.title: Tajisaki Royal Navy
tajisaki_royal_navy.html:
The navy of the Empire and Kingdom of Tajisaki: the Imperial Navy until 119 AG and the Tajisaki Royal Navy after it. It was the world's strongest for most of the Hundred Year War.

Tajisaki Royal Navy (Imperial Navy before 119 AG)
CountryEmpire of Tajisaki
Strength (99 AG)8 carriers; 94 submarines; Kaienha incendiary torpedoes
Naval superiorityAlone, 0–30 AG; contested after Qianchan's entry

The Imperial Navy destroyed the combined Water Tribe fleets in the first weeks of the war and held naval superiority alone until 30 AG, when its first engagement with the Qianchan Navy, at the Southern Air Temple Waters, was a draw. It blockaded the Earth Kingdom's coasts and Omashu's supply route, and its submarine war with Qianchan was one of the long conflicts of the middle war. Its carrier force was driven onto the defensive by Qianchan's submarines. In 90 AG, its Rear Admiral Yueya destroyed Jasmine Island, and its sailors who broke out of a battlecruiser's brig helped stop her. In the Siege of the North (99 AG) its Northern Fleet, with icebreakers, took Agna Qel'a. The Navy split by squadron in the Fire Nation Civil War in November 100 AG.

After 119 AG

When the constitution of 119 AG made the realm the Kingdom of Tajisaki, the Imperial Navy became the Tajisaki Royal Navy, and in common speech the Fire Navy. By 170 AG it kept the world's largest fleet by tonnage. It lost its gulf squadron in the Earth Empire's raid of 2–3 February 181 AG and about ninety warships in the war, and was rebuilt after it around eight new cruisers and two carriers, the Hakuryu and the Ryujin, laid down in 184 and 186 AG. See History of Tajisaki, 171–190 AG.

urn_political_parties.title: Political parties of the United Republic of Nations
urn_political_parties.html:
The four parties of the National Assembly in 170 AG.

Political parties of the United Republic of Nations
Servants of the RepublicEstablishment party of the Council and the civil service
ProgressivesLiberal-left party of labor, newcomers and reform
FederalistsParty of the provinces and regional autonomy; dissolved after 178 AG
Nationalist UnionRight-wing party of the natives and the veterans

The National Assembly of the United Republic of Nations had four parties in 170 AG: the Servants of the Republic, the Progressives, the Federalists and the Nationalist Union. They grew out of the fault lines of the First Republic, between newcomers and Yanakawan natives, between left and right, and between those who trusted the Council and those who did not. See Politics of the United Republic of Nations.

The Assembly of 170 AG

The National Assembly had 300 members in 170 AG, with a majority at 151. The Progressives held a plurality of 105 seats, the Servants of the Republic 95, the Federalists 55 and the Nationalist Union 45. No party had a majority, and the Federalists, whose 55 seats decided every close vote, were the pivot of the chamber.

The Assembly of 190 AG

After the Restoration the Assembly had 250 seats, with a majority at 126. The Federalists had dissolved after 178 AG, so in 190 AG there were three parties and a group of independents: the Nationalist Union held 90, the Servants of the Republic 80, the Progressives 45 and the independents, many of them the old Federalists' members, 35. The Union surged on the memory of the war and the fall of Republic City, but the Servants, the Progressives and the independents together held 160 seats and governed as the Hope of the Future coalition. President Zhu Li, an independent, was in her third term.

Servants of the Republic

The Servants of the Republic were the republic's oldest and largest party and the party of the Council. Its members were the councillors' circle, the senior civil service and the established business of Republic City, and it stood for continuity, for the Charter as written and for the collegial Council of six. Its enemies called it the party of the contracts. It was the party that the corruption of the era attached to, and it lost ground after 118 AG, when the reform of the Port Authority took its patronage away. In 170 AG Tarrlok, the Council President, was its best-known figure. It was in office through the First Republic and was divided over the Raiko Reform, which most of its members opposed as an attack on the Council they served.

After the Raiko Reform the Servants were tainted by the old Council. The voters blamed them for its corruption, the Dock Bombing contracts and the Port Authority, and they lost seats in every election of the Second Republic, going into opposition against the presidency they had resisted. The Restoration of 182 AG revived them, since it brought back the Assembly, the Cabinet and the Council's ways of working, and the Servants recovered as the party that knew how to govern. By 190 AG they held 80 seats under Kwon Min-jae and, with the Progressives and the independents, backed President Zhu Li in the Hope of the Future coalition.

Progressives

The Progressives were a liberal-left party of labor, the urban newcomers and the reformers. They had absorbed the Harmonists' voters after the ban of 126 AG and had been the party that kept the Harmonists' seats in the Assembly, though most of their leaders denied any connection. They wanted a state that acted for its workers, a wider franchise for newcomers and a stronger executive. Raiko belonged to them. They called the Raiko Reform the republic's answer to its deadlock, and held that the Equalist threat should be met by more representation. After Dava's death they were the party that carried her case into the Assembly. When the allegations of contact with the Equalists forced Raiko out of the presidency in 178 AG, the party was smeared with them, and it lost heavily in the war years. It rebuilt afterwards as a smaller party of labor and newcomers, and held 45 seats in 190 AG under Han Soo-ah.

Federalists

In 170 AG the Federalists were the party of the provinces and the regions, strongest in the Fujishihoro highlands, the Hengdong agricultural belt and Yu Dao, where the republic's constitutional provisions on provincial autonomy made a difference to daily life. They distrusted the capital and wanted the center's authority limited, and they opposed the Raiko Reform because a president elected by the whole republic would, in their view, rule without them. They were the swing party in the Assembly, since they could vote with the Servants against the Progressives or with the Progressives against the Nationalist Union, and the Council's deadlocks were commonly settled by them.

The end of the Federalists

The Federalists dissolved after 178 AG. Under the Raiko Reform the republic had a unitary presidency, with no states and few regional powers, and the Federalists' base, the provinces' control of their own rules, had little left to defend. Their members split after Raiko left the presidency, some to the Servants of the Republic and most to independent seats, and the party was wound up. The regions' interests passed to the independents. Invented.

Nationalist Union

The Nationalist Union was the republic's right-wing party. It spoke for the Yanakawan natives and for the veterans of the wars of independence, and it was hard on the Equalists and on the newcomers. It took up the natives' resentment at the Assembly's choice of even the natives' Non-Bender seat, and it called the Air seat, which had passed from Aang to Tenzin, a dynasty. Its leader in 170 AG was the firebender Zoltan, who called Raiko a liar and a would-be dictator in the Assembly debate and challenged him to an election. It supported the Raiko Reform's strong executive in the end, when the crisis of 170 AG made order the first issue. Zoltan died in the atomic bombing of Yu Dao on 19 December 182 AG, where the Assembly and the government had moved after the fall of Republic City, and the Union made a martyr of him. In the election after the war the party surged to 90 seats in 190 AG, the largest in the Assembly. The surge came from the war and the fall of the capital, from the blame the Union put on both Raiko and the Council establishment for letting spies into the republic's institutions in the penetration scandal, from the votes of the veterans who had come home from the war, and from Zoltan's martyrdom. Its leader in 190 AG was his deputy, Yi Dae-ho. The Union blamed President Zhu Li for letting the republic come close to surrender after the fall of Republic City, and attacked her ties to Varrick Global Industries, the builder of the Empire's suit, while she in turn was angry at the party for what she thought its blindness. Yi Dae-ho, Kwon Min-jae and Han Soo-ah are invented.

See also

  • Politics of the United Republic of Nations
  • National Assembly
  • Elections in the United Republic of Nations
  • Harmonists

Invented for this wiki from the party names and from Raiko and Zoltan's roles.

judiciary_and_police_of_the_urn.title: Courts, police and forces of the United Republic
judiciary_and_police_of_the_urn.html:
The courts, police and armed forces of the United Republic of Nations.

Courts, police and forces of the United Republic
Supreme CourtNine justices
Constitutional CourtFrom 182 AG
PoliceMetropolitan Police of Republic City
Armed forcesUnited Forces
OversightCommittee on Constitutional Compliance (to 171 AG); vetting commission (from 182 AG)

The courts, police and armed forces of the United Republic of Nations changed with each of its three constitutions, but three things stayed the same: a Supreme Court of nine justices, a police force in the capital that answered to the executive, and a standing army, the United Forces, that was kept out of civil policing. See Politics of the United Republic of Nations.

The Supreme Court

The Supreme Court sat in Republic City and had nine justices. Under the Charter of 100/102 AG they were appointed by the Republic Council and confirmed by the Assembly. The Court could void any law or act, and it tried the impeachment of a councillor. Under the Raiko Reform of 171 AG the President appointed them with the consent of the High Council, for twelve-year terms and with no more than three justices from any one bending tradition, so that no bloc could capture it. The Restoration of 182 AG kept the Court and added a Constitutional Court beside it. In practice the Supreme Court was the republic's most trusted body, and it ruled on the cases that politics could not settle.

Two rulings show how it worked. In 127 AG the Court upheld the sentence of death on Yakone, by four justices to one, a verdict that the Lowtide riots challenged, and in July 170 AG, before the Council's vote, it found the Raiko Reform constitutional, which let the Council approve the reform 4–2 on 18 July. The first ruling made the Court the republic's most unpopular institution among the dockers. The second made it the reform's guarantor.

The lower courts

Ordinary crime was tried by circuit courts. The Republic City Circuit Court, which heard the case of Yakone, sat with a jury, a deputy district attorney for the state and a defense lawyer, in the manner of the older Earth Kingdom and Qianchan courts. The republic's prosecutors answered to a District Attorney of the Republic City district, who was an official of the executive and, in the First Republic, was appointed by the Council. The trial of Yakone, which took 273 days from the blast to a jury, was the fastest terrorism trial the republic had held. See Trial of Yakone.

The Constitutional Court and the committees

Before 171 AG constitutional questions were reviewed by the Assembly's Committee on Constitutional Compliance, which also heard appeals against refused citizenship, and the Supreme Court had the last word. The Restoration created a Constitutional Court, which settles disputes between organs of government, hears the impeachment of the President on the Assembly's charge, and reviews laws against the Charter. The Restoration also set up a vetting commission, known as "the Sieve", which checks members of the Assembly, the Cabinet and senior officers for foreign influence, an answer to the penetration scandal of 181–182 AG. See Constitutional Settlement of 182 AG.

The Metropolitan Police

The Metropolitan Police of Republic City was the republic's one large civilian police force, and it answered to the executive, in the First Republic to the Council and after 171 AG to the President. Its chief in 170 AG was Lin Beifong, the daughter of Toph, who ran the force with a firm hand and a loyal officer corps and made the department's metalbending officers its elite. In the crisis of 170 AG the police were the first line against the Equalists' attacks, and they were also the force whose officer, Han, shot Dava dead on the pharmacy corner of Jianyu Square on 7 July. Han was suspended, and the shooting began the unrest that ended the Council. By 180 AG the chief of police was Mako, an officer of Lin's department who rose after the war.

The police had no power to command the army, and the army had none over them. The republic had learned from the Council's first years that a capital policed by soldiers would not be a free city, and the Charter kept the two apart. Their meeting was the martial law that the Council declared on 22 September 170 AG, when Tenzin was the only councillor to vote against it. After it the army patrolled the districts beside the police, and the Reform of 171 AG wrote into the new Title IV that the President could not send the armed forces against peaceful protest.

The United Forces

The United Forces were the republic's army, navy and air arm. They were raised from the conscripts of the national service that the Charter required of every citizen and were commanded in the First Republic by the Council, through a Defense Secretary and a general staff, and after 171 AG by the President as Commander-in-Chief. They were small by the standard of Tajisaki or Qianchan and relied on the mechanized suit retrofitted from a Hundred Year War design that Future Industries built under its United Forces contract, with the southern theater under General Ta Min in 170 AG. In the Earth Empire–Concord War the United Forces were organised in army groups, the Centre under Army-General Bumi, who was recalled to service, and the East under Army-General Uzu, with Kirvik as Defense Secretary. See Earth Empire–Concord War.

See also

  • Constitutional Charter, 100/102 AG
  • Constitutional Charter as reformed, 171 AG
  • Lin Beifong
  • Dava

Invented for this wiki: the circuit court structure, the District Attorney's appointment, the Constitutional Court's powers, and the separation of police and army. Mako as chief of police in 180 AG is from the draft novel.

zhu_li.title: Zhu Li
zhu_li.html:
President of the United Republic of Nations, 178–192 AG.

Zhu Li
OfficePresident of the United Republic of Nations, 178–192 AG
PartyIndependent
PreviouslyAssistant to Varrick
SpouseVarrick
TermsThree: 178–182 (four years), 182–187 and 187–192 (five years each)
PredecessorRaiko

Zhu Li was the President of the United Republic of Nations from 178 to 192 AG and, by the verdict of later historians, one of the greatest leaders in the republic's history. She began as the assistant of the industrialist Varrick, whom she later married, and travelled with Korra to Republic City in 170 AG. She entered politics as an independent after the Raiko Reform, and in 178 AG she succeeded Raiko, who left the presidency before the end of his second term, after allegations that he had been in touch with the Equalists. She never joined a party and governed with majorities made party by party.

Presidency

Under the Second Republic the President was elected directly for four years, and Zhu Li served the first term, 178 to 182 AG, under that Charter. She led the republic in the Earth Empire–Concord War, announced the alliance with Fire Lord Izumi and President Haatao on 25 December 180 AG, and ordered the army's development of a suit to match the Empire's hybrid armour. The fall of Republic City in December 182 and the penetration scandal brought down the Second Republic, and the Restoration of 182 AG made the President the Assembly's choice and lengthened the term to five years. The Assembly chose her in 182 and again in 187, so that she served three terms and left office in 192 AG. In 190 AG she was in her third term and governed with the Servants of the Republic, the Progressives and the independents, 160 of the 250 seats, as the Hope of the Future coalition, against the Nationalist Union, the largest single party. See Political parties of the United Republic of Nations.

Temper

Zhu Li was generally a kind person, and the people who worked for her said so. Her anger was kept for the Nationalist Union, whom she thought blind to what the republic faced, and she did not hide it. In her war speeches she was furious about the Empire, the spies and the corruption that had let it in, and she turned on the Union when it fought her war measures.

The Union answered in kind. It blamed her for letting the republic come close to surrender after the fall of Republic City in December 182, and for what it called her nonsense, the schemes and compromises of her office. It also attacked her ties to Varrick Global Industries, the company of her old employer Varrick, whose contracts supplied the army, and, after the Empire\'s archives were opened, which had built the Empire\'s hybrid suit under the name of a replica. The Union said that these ties had clouded her judgement, and asked how a President whose husband\'s company had armed the enemy could be trusted with the war. Her allies said that the charge was spite, that the company had been deceived, and that she had ordered the army\'s answering suit herself. See Varrick Global Industries. Her allies said that the charge was spite, and that she had held the republic together when the Union's own leader lay dead at Yu Dao. The Union's charges are invented.

Legacy

Historians of the republic count her among its greatest leaders, for holding the republic together through the war, the fall of its capital and the writing of the Restoration, and for governing without a party of her own. Her admirers compare her to the founders. Her critics, among them the Nationalist Union, say that she stayed too long, that her ties to Varrick Global Industries compromised her, and that the Third Republic's presidency rested on her person.

Invented for this wiki; her independence, her dates and her terms are set by the author.

varrick_global_industries.title: Varrick Global Industries
varrick_global_industries.html:
Varrick Global Industries (VGI) was an industrial company founded by the inventor Varrick, with headquarters in Republic City. It made radios, vehicles, machinery and, in the years before the Earth Empire–Concord War, armaments under contract for several states. It was run in practice by Varrick's assistant and later wife, Zhu Li, until she left for politics, and it remained a rival of Future Industries.

The Empire's contract

In 177 AG the Earth Empire signed a contract with the company for a replica of the Breaker Mk III No. 2, described as a training and display model. Over the next three years the specifications were revised repeatedly, and each revision moved the replica away from the Tajisaki suit and towards a heavier frame, bending-resistant plating and a fuel cell. By 180 AG the replica was the Imperial hybrid power armour, and the prototypes that the Empire's factories copied had come from VGI's workshops.

What the company knew

After the Empire's archives were seized in the autumn of 182 AG, the Joint Inquiry found no order that told the company what the suit was for, and found invoices that VGI's own engineers had questioned. Varrick said that he had thought the work a contract like any other and had been lied to by his client. His critics, among them the Nationalist Union, said that a man of his knowledge could not have failed to see the suit for what it was. The Inquiry made no finding against him, and the question was never closed.

Aftermath

The company's army contracts were suspended in 183 AG, and it was audited by the Assembly. The affair gave the Union its main charge against President Zhu Li, whose husband the company's founder was. Her defenders pointed out that she had ordered the army's own answering suit in December 180 AG and had never held office in the company while President.

Invented for this wiki from the author's note that VGI built a replica of the Breaker Mk III No. 2 for the Empire that was in reality the new power suit; the dates and the inquiry's findings are invented.
